Common_Goldeneye.Similar Looking Birds: Barrow's Goldeneye male has purple head and crescent cheek spot. Female very similar but Barrow's has shorter bill.
Common_Goldeneye.Best Ways to Identify: Round white cheek spot on green head (male) or brown head with bright golden eye and high rounded crown (female).

Common_Grackle.Description: Large iridescent blackbird with long keel-shaped tail. Purple- bronze iridescence on head. Pale yellow eye.
Common_Grackle.Behavior: Walks boldly and forages on the ground. Highly gregarious; forms enormous roosts. Loud squeaky gate call.
Common_Grackle.Habitat: Open areas, farms, suburban lawns, and woodland edges across the eastern United States and southern Canada.
Common_Grackle.Similar Looking Birds: Boat-tailed Grackle is larger with a bigger tail, found in coastal areas. Bronzed Cowbird has red eye.
Common_Grackle.Best Ways to Identify: Keel-shaped tail, yellow eye, and iridescent purple-bronze head on male make this the most familiar eastern grackle.

Common_Greenshank.Description: Large sandpiper. Gray-brown above, white below with streaked neck and breast, upturned bill tip, green-gray legs. About 12 inches.
Common_Greenshank.Behavior: Forages by running through shallow water with bill sweeping side to side. Rare vagrant to Atlantic coast from Eurasia.
Common_Greenshank.Habitat: Breeds on Eurasian bogs and moorland. Winters on African and Asian coasts. Rare vagrant to Atlantic coast.
Common_Greenshank.Similar Looking Birds: Greater Yellowlegs similar. Greenshank has slightly upturned bill and green-gray (not yellow) legs.
Common_Greenshank.Best Ways to Identify: Gray-green legs (not yellow). Slightly upturned bill tip. White back visible in flight. Rare vagrant on Atlantic coast.

Common_Ground-Dove.Description: Tiny dove with scaly-patterned head, pinkish bill, and rufous wing patches visible in flight.
Common_Ground-Dove.Behavior: Walks on the ground bobbing head. Forages for seeds. Flushes low with rapid wingbeats and rufous flash in wings.
Common_Ground-Dove.Habitat: Open sandy areas, brush, roadsides, and agricultural fields in the southern United States and Central America.
Common_Ground-Dove.Similar Looking Birds: Inca Dove has scaled back and longer tail with white edges. Ruddy Ground-Dove male is more rufous throughout.
Common_Ground-Dove.Best Ways to Identify: Tiny size, scaly head pattern, and bright rufous wing flash in flight are distinctive. Walks on ground like a mouse.

Common_Gull.Description: Medium gull, pale gray back, white head and body, yellow-green bill without red spot in winter. Gentle dove-like expression. About 16 inches.
Common_Gull.Behavior: Forages on fields and coasts. European counterpart to Ring-billed Gull. Uncommon winter visitor to northeastern North America.
Common_Gull.Habitat: Coasts, fields, and harbors. Regular in winter in western Europe; rare visitor to northeast North America.
Common_Gull.Similar Looking Birds: Ring-billed Gull very similar. Common Gull has smaller bill, darker eye, gentler expression.
Common_Gull.Best Ways to Identify: Small bill without black ring; darker eye than Ring-billed. Rounder head, gentler face. Rare winter visitor to northeast.

Common_Loon.Description: Breeding adult has black-and-white checkered back, black head with red eye, and white necklace. Winter is gray-brown.
Common_Loon.Behavior: Expert diver pursuing fish underwater. Famous yodeling wail and tremolo calls on northern lakes. Awkward on land.
Common_Loon.Habitat: Clear northern lakes for breeding. Winters on coastal waters and large southern lakes across North America.
Common_Loon.Similar Looking Birds: Red-throated Loon is smaller with upturned bill. Yellow-billed Loon is larger with yellow bill. Both rare except in North.
Common_Loon.Best Ways to Identify: Breeding plumage unmistakable. Winter birds identified by large size, flat crown, and dagger-like bill held level.

Common_Merganser.Description: Male has green head, white body, and orange-red serrated bill. Female has rusty head with shaggy crest and gray body.
Common_Merganser.Behavior: Dives and chases fish underwater. Often seen in rivers. Nests in tree cavities near water. Flies in lines low over water.
Common_Merganser.Habitat: Clear rivers and lakes in northern forests for nesting. Winters on large lakes and rivers across North America.
Common_Merganser.Similar Looking Birds: Red-breasted Merganser male has shaggy crest and streaked breast. Hooded Merganser is much smaller.
Common_Merganser.Best Ways to Identify: Large size, green head, white body, and long red serrated bill on male. Female's rusty head with clean white chin is key.

Common_Murre.Description: Large auk with dark brown-black head, back, and wings; white underparts. Thin, pointed bill. About 17.5 inches. "Bridled" form has white eye ring. In winter, white extends up throat with dark line behind eye.
Common_Murre.Behavior: Expert diver, using wings to propel underwater to depths of 600 feet. Breeds in dense colonies on narrow cliff ledges. Lays single pear-shaped egg.
Common_Murre.Habitat: North Pacific and Atlantic oceans. Breeds on sea cliffs; winters offshore and along coasts. Common from Alaska south to California in winter.
Common_Murre.Similar Looking Birds: Thick-billed Murre has white bill stripe and stockier bill. Razorbill has deep, laterally compressed bill. Brünnich's Murre is similar on Atlantic.
Common_Murre.Best Ways to Identify: Large auk, dark above and white below, with thin pointed bill. Dense cliff colonies in summer. Open ocean in winter. Expert diving and underwater flight.

Common_Myna.Description: Medium bird, brown body with black head, yellow bill and eye skin, white wing patch visible in flight. About 9 inches.
Common_Myna.Behavior: Bold and aggressive introduced species. Highly vocal. Competes with native birds for nesting cavities.
Common_Myna.Habitat: Introduced to Hawaii and South Florida. Urban areas, parks, farms, and open country. Invasive pest species.
Common_Myna.Similar Looking Birds: Crested Myna has white crest. No other brown bird with black head and yellow bare skin in range.
Common_Myna.Best Ways to Identify: Black head, brown body, yellow bill, white wing patch. Bold and noisy. Hawaiian and Florida invasive.

Common_Nighthawk.Description: Mottled brown-gray cryptic plumage, long wings with white bar, notched tail. Flies at dusk and dawn.
Common_Nighthawk.Behavior: Aerial insect hunter active at dusk. Distinctive peent call in flight. Males dive and boom with wings at breeding grounds.
Common_Nighthawk.Habitat: Open areas, cities, and grasslands across North America. Winters in South America. Roosts on flat rooftops and branches.
Common_Nighthawk.Similar Looking Birds: Lesser Nighthawk is smaller with wing bar closer to tip. Chuck-will's-widow is much larger and nocturnal only.
Common_Nighthawk.Best Ways to Identify: Erratic buoyant flight with white wing bars on long pointed wings. Nasal peent call and booming dive display.

Common_Pauraque.Description: Large nightjar with intricate brown, black, buff, and gray patterned plumage. Long tail and wings, large dark eyes. About 11 inches.
Common_Pauraque.Behavior: Roosts and nests on ground; active at night catching flying insects. Calls loudly at night. Year-round resident in southern Texas.
Common_Pauraque.Habitat: Brushy woodland and thorny scrub in South Texas and tropical Americas. Common in Lower Rio Grande Valley.
Common_Pauraque.Similar Looking Birds: Chuck-will's-widow and Whip-poor-will similar. Pauraque has distinctive call and longer tail.
Common_Pauraque.Best Ways to Identify: Very long tail and white tail patches visible in flight. Roosts on ground in brush. Distinctive loud night call in South Texas.

Common_Pochard.Description: Medium diving duck. Male has chestnut-red head, black breast, pale gray body. Female brown with paler face. Sloping forehead. About 18 inches.
Common_Pochard.Behavior: Dives for aquatic plants, seeds, and invertebrates. Forms large flocks in Eurasian winters. Rare vagrant to eastern North America.
Common_Pochard.Habitat: Breeds on freshwater lakes and marshes across Eurasia. Winters on European lakes and reservoirs. Vagrant to Atlantic coast.
Common_Pochard.Similar Looking Birds: Redhead very similar. Males nearly identical; distinguished by head shape and bill pattern.
Common_Pochard.Best Ways to Identify: Male's rust-red head with sloping forehead and gray body. Peak-crowned head profile separates from Redhead.

Common_Poorwill.Description: Smallest North American nightjar. Mottled brown-gray, short rounded tail with white corners. Wide flat head.
Common_Poorwill.Behavior: Nocturnal; calls poor-will repeatedly at night. Can enter torpor in winter, the only North American hibernating bird.
Common_Poorwill.Habitat: Dry rocky hillsides, desert scrub, and open pine forests in the western United States and Mexico.
Common_Poorwill.Similar Looking Birds: Chuck-will's-widow and Whip-poor-will are both much larger. Eastern Whip-poor-will has different call and range.
Common_Poorwill.Best Ways to Identify: Smallest nightjar with short rounded tail. Poor-will call at night in western desert scrub. White tail corners visible.

Common_Raven.Description: Large all-black bird with wedge-shaped tail, heavy curved bill, and shaggy throat feathers. Deep glossy iridescence.
Common_Raven.Behavior: Highly intelligent; uses tools and plays. Loud deep cronk call. Soars on thermals. Pairs for life. Caches food.
Common_Raven.Habitat: Mountains, forests, deserts, and tundra across North America and Eurasia. Generalist and adaptable scavenger.
Common_Raven.Similar Looking Birds: American Crow is smaller with rounded tail and higher-pitched caw. Fish Crow and Chihuahuan Raven are both smaller.
Common_Raven.Best Ways to Identify: Massive size, wedge-shaped tail, and deep cronk call. Soaring flight with flat wings distinguishes it from crows.

Common_Redpoll.Description: Small finch with red forehead cap, black chin, and streaked brown body. Male has rosy-pink wash on breast.
Common_Redpoll.Behavior: Highly nomadic; irrupts south in winter following seed crops. Forms large flocks in birch and alder. Acrobatic feeder.
Common_Redpoll.Habitat: Boreal forests and tundra scrub for nesting. Winters in birch forests and weedy fields across northern North America.
Common_Redpoll.Similar Looking Birds: Hoary Redpoll is paler and frostier. Pine Siskin is streaked but lacks the red cap. House Finch is larger and redder.
Common_Redpoll.Best Ways to Identify: Small size with bright red forehead spot and streaked brown plumage. Pink breast on males. Often in flocks in birches.

Common_Redshank.Description: Medium sandpiper. Brown above, white below with streaked breast, distinctive white wing patches in flight, orange-red legs and bill base. About 11 inches.
Common_Redshank.Behavior: Noisy and alert; often the first to call alarm. Forages on mudflats. Rare vagrant to Atlantic coast from Eurasia.
Common_Redshank.Habitat: Breeds on European wet meadows and coasts. Winters on European and African coasts. Rare vagrant to Atlantic coast.
Common_Redshank.Similar Looking Birds: Lesser Yellowlegs similar shape but yellow legs. Redshank's white wing patches distinctive.
Common_Redshank.Best Ways to Identify: Broad white wing patches visible in flight. Orange- red bill base and legs. Noisy alarm calls.

Common_Redstart.Description: Small chat. Male has black face, white forehead, orange-red breast and tail. Female brown. About 5.5 inches.
Common_Redstart.Behavior: Constantly quivers the rufous tail. Flycatches from perch. Very rare vagrant to northeastern North America from Europe.
Common_Redstart.Habitat: Open woodland and gardens in Europe and Asia. Very rare vagrant to North America.
Common_Redstart.Similar Looking Birds: American Redstart has different pattern. Bluethroat has blue throat. No similar bird in range.
Common_Redstart.Best Ways to Identify: Orange-red tail constantly quivering. Male black face with orange-red breast. Very rare European vagrant.

Common_Ringed_Plover.Description: Small plover. Brown above, white below with black breast band, orange bill with black tip, orange legs. About 7.5 inches.
Common_Ringed_Plover.Behavior: Runs and stops to pick invertebrates. Breeds in Arctic; rare vagrant to eastern North America from Eurasia. Visits Atlantic beaches.
Common_Ringed_Plover.Habitat: Sandy and pebbly beaches and tundra. Breeds in Greenland and Eurasia. Rare vagrant to Atlantic coast of North America.
Common_Ringed_Plover.Similar Looking Birds: Semipalmated Plover nearly identical; Common Ringed has complete breast band and different call.
Common_Ringed_Plover.Best Ways to Identify: Extremely similar to Semipalmated Plover. Complete breast band and absence of webbing between toes on Common Ringed Plover.

Common_Rosefinch.Description: Medium finch. Male rosy-red head and breast with streaked brown back. Female streaked brown. About 6 inches.
Common_Rosefinch.Behavior: Forages for seeds and berries. Rare vagrant to western Alaska and Aleutian Islands from Siberia.
Common_Rosefinch.Habitat: Scrub, woodland edges, and gardens of Europe and Asia. Rare vagrant to western Alaska.
Common_Rosefinch.Similar Looking Birds: Purple Finch male more extensive red. House Finch male has streaked flanks.
Common_Rosefinch.Best Ways to Identify: Male rosy-red head and breast. Female streaked brown without distinctive marks. Rare Alaska vagrant from Siberia.

Common_Sandpiper.Description: Small sandpiper. Brown above, white below with brown breast patch. Constantly bobs tail. Horizontal posture. About 8 inches.
Common_Sandpiper.Behavior: Constantly bobs tail while walking. Low flight with stiff shallow wingbeats. Eurasian counterpart of Spotted Sandpiper. Rare vagrant to North America.
Common_Sandpiper.Habitat: Breeds along Eurasian rivers and lakeshores. Winters on Asian and African coasts. Rare vagrant to Atlantic and Pacific coasts.
Common_Sandpiper.Similar Looking Birds: Spotted Sandpiper nearly identical. Common Sandpiper lacks spots in breeding and has longer wing stripe.
Common_Sandpiper.Best Ways to Identify: Nearly identical to Spotted Sandpiper but lacks spots in breeding. Longer white wing stripe in flight. Rare vagrant.

Common_Scoter.Description: Medium sea duck. Male entirely black with yellow-orange knob on bill base. Female dark brown with pale cheeks and dark cap. About 19 inches.
Common_Scoter.Behavior: Dives for mollusks in coastal and offshore waters. Breeds on subarctic lakes. Rare vagrant to North America from Eurasia.
Common_Scoter.Habitat: Breeds on subarctic and boreal lakes in Europe and Asia. Winters on European coastlines. Vagrant to Atlantic and Gulf coasts.
Common_Scoter.Similar Looking Birds: Black Scoter nearly identical; male separated by different bill knob coloring.
Common_Scoter.Best Ways to Identify: Male all-black plumage with yellow-orange bill knob. Female's distinctive pale cheek contrasting with dark cap.

Common_Shelduck.Description: A large, goose-like duck with striking white body, dark green head, broad chestnut breast band, and bright red bill. Males have a knob on bill.
Common_Shelduck.Behavior: Feeds on invertebrates and small fish in estuaries by sweeping bill through mud. Nests in burrows. Gathers in large molting flocks.
Common_Shelduck.Habitat: Coastal estuaries, mudflats, salt marshes, and shallow lakes across Europe and Asia. Prefers sandy or muddy shorelines.
Common_Shelduck.Similar Looking Birds: Distinctive coloration makes it hard to confuse. Egyptian Goose has similar size but very different pattern. Ruddy Shelduck is all-orange.
Common_Shelduck.Best Ways to Identify: Bold tricolor pattern of green head, chestnut chest band, and white body is unique. Red bill and large size separate it from all ducks.

Common_Snipe.Description: Chunky shorebird with extremely long bill, striped brown and buff head, heavily streaked brown back, and barred flanks. Short legs. About 10.5 inches. Cryptic plumage, nearly invisible in marsh grass.
Common_Snipe.Behavior: Probes soft mud and grass for earthworms and invertebrates with sensitive bill. Produces "winnowing" sound with tail feathers during display flight. Flushed birds burst upward in erratic zig-zag flight with rasping call.
Common_Snipe.Habitat: Wet meadows, bogs, and marshes. Breeds across Canada and Alaska; winters in U.S. south. Very similar to Wilson's Snipe; some taxonomists lump them.
Common_Snipe.Similar Looking Birds: Wilson's Snipe is nearly identical (North American species). American Woodcock has different face pattern and rounder body. Long-billed Dowitcher much larger.
Common_Snipe.Best Ways to Identify: Extremely long bill and striped head in wet meadow habitat. Explosive flushing with rasping call. Winnowing display flight overhead. Very similar to Wilson's Snipe.

Common_Swift.Description: Medium swift. All dark sooty brown with pale white throat patch. Long scythe-shaped wings and forked tail. About 6.5 inches.
Common_Swift.Behavior: Almost entirely aerial; lands only to nest. Screaming calls in flight. Rare vagrant to eastern North America from Europe.
Common_Swift.Habitat: Breeds throughout Europe and Asia, often in buildings. Winters in sub-Saharan Africa. Rare vagrant to Atlantic coast of North America.
Common_Swift.Similar Looking Birds: Chimney and Vaux's Swifts similar but smaller. Common Swift paler throat distinguishes it.
Common_Swift.Best Ways to Identify: All dark with pale throat patch. Long scythe-shaped wings. Screaming call. Rare European vagrant on Atlantic coast.

Common_Tern.Description: Gray above, white below, black cap, and orange-red bill with dark tip. Long forked tail and graceful flight.
Common_Tern.Behavior: Dives headfirst for fish. Colonial nester on beaches and islands. Aggressive defender of nest. Migrates long distances.
Common_Tern.Habitat: Coastal beaches, islands, and inland lakes across North America. Winters in South America. Very common coastal tern.
Common_Tern.Similar Looking Birds: Arctic Tern has all-red bill, shorter legs, and longer tail. Forster's Tern has white primaries and orange bill in breeding.
Common_Tern.Best Ways to Identify: Orange-red bill with black tip and black outer primaries in flight. Long tail streamers and graceful buoyant flight.

Common_Waxbill.Description: Tiny finch, brown with fine barring, red face mask, red bill, pinkish-red belly. About 4 inches.
Common_Waxbill.Behavior: Highly gregarious in large flocks. Forages for small seeds in grasslands. Introduced to Hawaii and Puerto Rico.
Common_Waxbill.Habitat: Grasslands, open areas, and roadsides. Introduced to Hawaii and Puerto Rico. Native to sub-Saharan Africa.
Common_Waxbill.Similar Looking Birds: Lavender Waxbill gray without barring. Orange-cheeked Waxbill has orange cheeks.
Common_Waxbill.Best Ways to Identify: Red face mask, finely barred brown body, red bill. Very small. Gregarious flocks in Hawaiian grasslands.

Common_Wood-Pigeon.Description: Large pigeon. Blue-gray overall with white neck patch bordered by iridescent green and pink, white wing bars visible in flight. About 16 inches.
Common_Wood-Pigeon.Behavior: Feeds on crops, berries, and acorns. Forms large flocks outside breeding season. Rare vagrant to North America from Europe.
Common_Wood-Pigeon.Habitat: Farmland, woodland edges, parks, and gardens across Europe. Rare vagrant to Atlantic coast of North America.
Common_Wood-Pigeon.Similar Looking Birds: Band-tailed Pigeon similar size. Common Wood-Pigeon has distinctive white neck patch.
Common_Wood-Pigeon.Best Ways to Identify: Large size, blue-gray plumage, and distinctive white neck patch bordered by iridescent green. White wing bars visible in flight.

Common_Yellowthroat.Description: Male has bright yellow throat, white border above black mask. Female is olive-brown with yellow throat and no mask.
Common_Yellowthroat.Behavior: Skulks in dense marsh vegetation. Male often sings from exposed perch. Song is a distinctive witchety-witchety.
Common_Yellowthroat.Habitat: Marshes, wetland edges, and dense shrubby areas across North America. One of the most common warblers.
Common_Yellowthroat.Similar Looking Birds: Kentucky Warbler has yellow spectacles and no black mask. Nashville Warbler has gray head and no mask. Males unmistakable.
Common_Yellowthroat.Best Ways to Identify: Male's bold black mask with yellow throat is unmistakable. Witchety-witchety song in marshy habitats very distinctive.

Connecticut_Warbler.Description: Complete white eye ring on gray hood, yellow underparts, and olive-green back. Bold complete eye ring is key.
Connecticut_Warbler.Behavior: Walks on ground rather than hops. Very secretive; rarely seen. Pumps tail while walking. Loud chip call.
Connecticut_Warbler.Habitat: Boreal bogs and wet forests for nesting. Migrates through the Midwest. Winters in South America. Rare and secretive.
Connecticut_Warbler.Similar Looking Birds: MacGillivray's Warbler has broken eye ring and is found in the West. Mourning Warbler has no eye ring and darker hood.
Connecticut_Warbler.Best Ways to Identify: Bold complete white eye ring on gray hood and walking gait. One of the most sought-after and difficult warblers to find.

Cooks_Petrel.Description: Small gadfly petrel, pale gray above with dark M-pattern, bright white below, gray cap. About 11 inches.
Cooks_Petrel.Behavior: Breeds on New Zealand islands; migrates through North Pacific. Uncommon offshore California in late summer and fall.
Cooks_Petrel.Habitat: North Pacific Ocean. Offshore California and Pacific coast in migration. Breeds on New Zealand islands.
Cooks_Petrel.Similar Looking Birds: Stejneger's Petrel very similar. Cook's has cleaner white underparts and paler cap.
Cooks_Petrel.Best Ways to Identify: Pale gray above with bold M-pattern, very white below. Small gadfly petrel. Offshore California in late summer.

Coopers_Hawk.Description: Blue-gray above, rusty-orange barred below, rounded tail with white tip. Red eye in adults. Rounded wings.
Coopers_Hawk.Behavior: Agile forest hunter chasing birds through dense cover. Visits bird feeders to catch prey. Flap-flap-glide flight pattern.
Coopers_Hawk.Habitat: Forests, woodland edges, and suburban areas across North America. Increasingly common in cities.
Coopers_Hawk.Similar Looking Birds: Sharp-shinned Hawk is smaller with square tail. Northern Goshawk is much larger with a white eyebrow.
Coopers_Hawk.Best Ways to Identify: Rounded tail (Sharp-shin has square tail) and larger size. Heavier head projection in flight. Red eye on adults.

Corn_Crake.Description: Medium rail. Brown streaked upperparts, gray face and breast, rufous-chestnut wing patches distinctive in flight. About 11 inches.
Corn_Crake.Behavior: Extremely secretive; heard much more often than seen. Loud rasping "crex-crex" call. Rare vagrant to North America from Europe.
Corn_Crake.Habitat: Breeds in European grasslands and hay meadows. Winters in Africa. Rare vagrant to Atlantic coast of North America.
Corn_Crake.Similar Looking Birds: Other rails and crakes. Corn Crake's chestnut wing patches distinctive in flight.
Corn_Crake.Best Ways to Identify: Chestnut wing patches visible in flight distinctive. Loud rasping "crex-crex" call heard from tall grass at night.

Corys_Shearwater.Description: Large shearwater with pale gray-brown upperparts, white underparts, and yellow bill with dark tip. Lacks sharp contrast between dark and light. About 18 inches with 44-inch wingspan. Lazy, arching flight on stiff wings.
Corys_Shearwater.Behavior: Feeds on fish, squid, and offal at sea surface or shallow dives. Follows ships. Breeds on Mediterranean islands; transoceanic migrant. Occurs in flocks.
Corys_Shearwater.Habitat: Open Atlantic Ocean; common off U.S. East Coast in summer and fall. Pelagic, rarely seen from shore except during strong storms.
Corys_Shearwater.Similar Looking Birds: Greater Shearwater has dark cap and white neck collar. Sooty Shearwater is all dark. Cory's pale, uniform coloring and yellow bill are distinctive.
Corys_Shearwater.Best Ways to Identify: Large shearwater with uniform pale brown-gray above and yellow bill. Lazy, banking flight. Atlantic pelagic, common on summer offshore trips. No dark cap.

Costas_Hummingbird.Description: Male has iridescent purple cap and gorget with elongated flared sides. Female is gray-green with white underparts.
Costas_Hummingbird.Behavior: Male performs steep U-shaped dive display with a shrill whistling sound at the bottom. Found year-round in desert.
Costas_Hummingbird.Habitat: Desert washes, Sonoran desert scrub, and chaparral of the southwestern United States and Baja California.
Costas_Hummingbird.Similar Looking Birds: Anna's Hummingbird male has a red-rose gorget and cap. Black-chinned Hummingbird has black chin with purple lower band.
Costas_Hummingbird.Best Ways to Identify: Purple flared gorget and cap on male are unique. Female's small size and desert range help narrow identification.

Couchs_Kingbird.Description: Large flycatcher with gray head, olive-green back, yellow belly, and white throat. Heavy bill. Brown-notched tail (no rufous). About 9.5 inches. Nearly identical to Tropical Kingbird in appearance.
Couchs_Kingbird.Behavior: Perches openly on wires and treetops, sallying out to catch large insects. Very aggressive, chasing larger birds. Loud, distinctive calls.
Couchs_Kingbird.Habitat: Lower Rio Grande Valley of southern Texas and northeastern Mexico. Woodlands, forest edges, and towns. Year-round resident in Texas, some migration.
Couchs_Kingbird.Similar Looking Birds: Tropical Kingbird nearly identical; best distinguished by call. Cassin's Kingbird has darker gray breast. Western Kingbird has white outer tail feathers.
Couchs_Kingbird.Best Ways to Identify: In range (south Texas): gray head, yellow belly, heavy bill, notched brown tail. Voice is critical — Couch's gives a breezy, rolling call; Tropical gives a loud chittering. Both very similar; location and calls separate them.

Crane_Hawk.Description: Slender long-legged gray hawk with two white tail bands. Orange-red eyes. Long double- jointed legs. About 18 inches.
Crane_Hawk.Behavior: Uses long double-jointed legs to probe tree cavities for prey. Rare vagrant to southern Texas from Mexico.
Crane_Hawk.Habitat: Tropical forest of Mexico and Central America. Rare vagrant to southern Texas.
Crane_Hawk.Similar Looking Birds: Mississippi Kite similar gray color but shorter legs. Crane Hawk's very long legs distinctive.
Crane_Hawk.Best Ways to Identify: Very long orange-red legs, slender build. Two white tail bands. Rare vagrant from Mexico to Texas.

Craveris_Murrelet.Description: Small alcid. Black above, white below. Partial white collar, dark partial chin bar. Slightly different from Scripps's. About 9.5 inches.
Craveris_Murrelet.Behavior: Nests on islands in Gulf of California. Post-breeding dispersal brings birds into California waters in late summer.
Craveris_Murrelet.Habitat: Breeds on islands in the Gulf of California, Mexico. Post-breeding dispersal to California coastal waters.
Craveris_Murrelet.Similar Looking Birds: Scripps's and Guadalupe Murrelets similar. Craveri's has partial dark chin bar.
Craveris_Murrelet.Best Ways to Identify: Partial dark chin bar on white throat. Slimmer than Scripps's. Found in California waters in late summer.

Crescent-chested_Warbler.Description: Small warbler, gray above, yellow-orange below with chestnut crescent on breast, bold white supercilium. About 4.5 inches.
Crescent-chested_Warbler.Behavior: Forages actively in pine-oak forest. Rare vagrant to Arizona and New Mexico from Mexico.
Crescent-chested_Warbler.Habitat: Montane pine-oak forests of Mexico. Rare vagrant to southeastern Arizona and New Mexico.
Crescent-chested_Warbler.Similar Looking Birds: Nashville Warbler lacks chestnut crescent. Tennessee Warbler plain below. Chestnut crescent unique.
Crescent-chested_Warbler.Best Ways to Identify: Chestnut crescent on yellow breast distinctive. Gray above, bold white supercilium. Rare Arizona vagrant from Mexico.

Crested_Auklet.Description: Medium auklet. Entirely dark gray with forward-curling orange crest, white facial plume, orange bill. About 10 inches.
Crested_Auklet.Behavior: Breeds in enormous colonies on Alaskan islands. Emits citrus-like odor during breeding. Dives for copepods. Forms massive flocks.
Crested_Auklet.Habitat: Breeds on rocky islands in Bering Sea and Aleutian chain. Winters in adjacent North Pacific waters.
Crested_Auklet.Similar Looking Birds: Whiskered Auklet smaller with different plumes. Crested Auklet's forward-curling crest unmistakable.
Crested_Auklet.Best Ways to Identify: Forward-curling orange-yellow crest unique. All dark gray with orange bill. Citrus scent in breeding season.

Crested_Caracara.Description: Black cap, bare orange-red face, white neck and breast with black barring. Long yellow legs. Bold white wing patches.
Crested_Caracara.Behavior: Walks on the ground foraging for carrion and prey. Often seen with vultures. Aggressive at carcasses.
Crested_Caracara.Habitat: Open grasslands, prairies, and ranchlands in Florida, Texas, Arizona, and Mexico. Expanding range northward.
Crested_Caracara.Similar Looking Birds: No other raptor in North America looks like a Crested Caracara. The bold black, white, and orange-red pattern is unique.
Crested_Caracara.Best Ways to Identify: Bold pied pattern, bare orange-red face, and flat-winged soaring flight. White wing patches flash in flight from above.

Crested_Myna.Description: Medium bird, black throughout with white wing patch, yellow bill, short white feather crest on forehead. About 9.5 inches.
Crested_Myna.Behavior: Formerly established in Vancouver, British Columbia but now nearly or completely extirpated from North America.
Crested_Myna.Habitat: Urban areas, parks, and farms. Introduced from China. Former population in Vancouver essentially gone.
Crested_Myna.Similar Looking Birds: Common Myna brown-bodied. European Starling iridescent green-black with short bill and different shape.
Crested_Myna.Best Ways to Identify: All-black with white wing patch and small frontal crest. Yellow bill. Very rare now in North America.

Crimson-collared_Grosbeak.Description: Medium grosbeak. Male black with crimson collar and underparts. Female olive-green with yellow collar. About 8.5 inches.
Crimson-collared_Grosbeak.Behavior: Forages in dense thorn scrub. Rare vagrant to southern Texas from northeastern Mexico.
Crimson-collared_Grosbeak.Habitat: Dense thorn scrub of northeastern Mexico. Rare vagrant to Rio Grande Valley, Texas.
Crimson-collared_Grosbeak.Similar Looking Birds: No similar black bird with crimson collar in range. Cardinal family relative but unique pattern.
Crimson-collared_Grosbeak.Best Ways to Identify: Black with crimson collar and belly. Very rare Texas vagrant from Mexico. Distinctive crimson collar.

Crissal_Thrasher.Description: Large, long-tailed thrasher, plain gray-brown overall with pale gray underparts. Distinctive chestnut undertail coverts (crissum) visible from below. Very long, strongly decurved bill. About 11.5 inches. Dark malar streak.
Crissal_Thrasher.Behavior: Forages on ground beneath dense desert shrubs, rarely exposing itself. Runs quickly from cover to cover. Rich, melodious song given from shrub tops.
Crissal_Thrasher.Habitat: Dense desert scrub — mesquite thickets, desert washes with dense shrubs in Arizona, New Mexico, California, and Baja California. Secretive resident.
Crissal_Thrasher.Similar Looking Birds: Curve-billed Thrasher has spotted breast and orange eye. LeConte's Thrasher is paler with less obvious crissum. Long bill and chestnut undertail are key.
Crissal_Thrasher.Best Ways to Identify: Long, strongly curved bill. Chestnut undertail coverts (look from behind). Plain gray-brown plumage in dense desert scrub. Rich, varied musical song.

Crowned_Slaty_Flycatcher.Description: Medium flycatcher, slate gray above and below, black crown with orange-yellow crown patch. About 7 inches.
Crowned_Slaty_Flycatcher.Behavior: South American migrant species. Very rare vagrant to North American Atlantic coast.
Crowned_Slaty_Flycatcher.Habitat: Open woodland and cerrado of South America. Very rare vagrant to Atlantic coast.
Crowned_Slaty_Flycatcher.Similar Looking Birds: Kingbirds similar size. Crowned Slaty Flycatcher has slate-gray plumage with orange crown.
Crowned_Slaty_Flycatcher.Best Ways to Identify: Slate-gray plumage with orange-yellow crown patch. Rare South American vagrant to Atlantic coast.

Cuban_Martin.Description: Large swallow endemic to Cuba. Male glossy blue-black. Female brown above with white belly, concealed white bases to feathers. About 7 inches.
Cuban_Martin.Behavior: Forages aerially over open areas. Rare vagrant to Florida. Nests in cliff cavities and buildings in Cuba.
Cuban_Martin.Habitat: Open areas and towns of Cuba. Rare vagrant to Florida.
Cuban_Martin.Similar Looking Birds: Purple Martin male nearly identical. Female Purple Martin distinguished by streaked underparts.
Cuban_Martin.Best Ways to Identify: Female: white belly with concealed white feather bases on breast. Male all-dark. Very rare Florida vagrant from Cuba.

Cuban_Pewee.Description: Small pewee, olive-brown above, grayish white below. Prominent white crescent behind eye. About 6 inches.
Cuban_Pewee.Behavior: Sallies for insects. Caribbean species; rare vagrant to southern Florida from Cuba and Bahamas.
Cuban_Pewee.Habitat: Woodland of Cuba and Bahamas. Rare vagrant to southern Florida.
Cuban_Pewee.Similar Looking Birds: Eastern Wood-Pewee similar but lacks white crescent behind eye.
Cuban_Pewee.Best Ways to Identify: White crescent behind eye. Small olive pewee. Rare vagrant to Florida from Caribbean islands.

Cuban_Vireo.Description: Small vireo, olive-green above, pale below with yellowish sides, white supercilium, no wing bars. About 5 inches.
Cuban_Vireo.Behavior: Caribbean island vireo. Very rare vagrant to southern Florida from Cuba.
Cuban_Vireo.Habitat: Forest and thicket of Cuba. Very rare vagrant to southern Florida.
Cuban_Vireo.Similar Looking Birds: Other vireos have wing bars. Cuban Vireo lacks wing bars with olive plumage.
Cuban_Vireo.Best Ways to Identify: Olive vireo without wing bars. White supercilium. Very rare Florida vagrant from Cuba.

Curlew_Sandpiper.Description: Medium sandpiper with noticeably decurved bill. Breeding adult brick-red below; non-breeding gray above, white below. White rump. About 8 inches.
Curlew_Sandpiper.Behavior: Forages on mudflats wading deeper than Dunlin. Rare but regular vagrant to both coasts from Eurasian breeding grounds.
Curlew_Sandpiper.Habitat: Breeds on Siberian Arctic tundra. Winters on African coasts. Uncommon vagrant to both coasts of North America.
Curlew_Sandpiper.Similar Looking Birds: Dunlin similar with decurved bill. Curlew Sandpiper has white rump and more curved bill.
Curlew_Sandpiper.Best Ways to Identify: Decurved bill longer than Dunlin's. White rump distinctive in flight. Bright reddish breeding plumage unmistakable.

Curve-billed_Thrasher.Description: Gray-brown above, spotted below with orange-yellow eye. Distinctly curved bill. Somewhat cryptic on the ground.
Curve-billed_Thrasher.Behavior: Forages by tossing leaf litter with its bill. Loud two-note whit-wheet call. Sings a complex melodious song.
Curve-billed_Thrasher.Habitat: Desert scrub, cacti, and chaparral of the Sonoran and Chihuahuan deserts in the southwestern United States and Mexico.
Curve-billed_Thrasher.Similar Looking Birds: Bendire's Thrasher has a straighter bill and faint breast spots. California Thrasher has a longer bill and lacks spots.
Curve-billed_Thrasher.Best Ways to Identify: Curved bill, spotted breast, and orange eye in desert habitat. Distinctive two-note whit-wheet whistle call.

Dark-billed_Cuckoo.Description: Slender cuckoo. Brown above, whitish below with buff wash on breast, dark cap. Bill entirely dark. Long tail with white spots. About 11 inches.
Dark-billed_Cuckoo.Behavior: Secretive; forages in dense vegetation for insects and caterpillars. Rare vagrant to North America from South America.
Dark-billed_Cuckoo.Habitat: Breeds in South American forests and woodland. Rare vagrant to North America; most records from eastern US and Caribbean islands.
Dark-billed_Cuckoo.Similar Looking Birds: Yellow-billed and Black-billed Cuckoos similar. Dark- billed has all-dark bill and buffier underparts.
Dark-billed_Cuckoo.Best Ways to Identify: All-dark bill distinguishes from Yellow-billed Cuckoo. Buff wash on underparts. Rare vagrant from South America.

Dark-eyed_Junco.Description: Variable plumage by region; typically dark gray hood and back with white belly and white outer tail feathers.
Dark-eyed_Junco.Behavior: Forages on ground below feeders. Flashes white outer tail feathers in flight. Forms flocks in winter. Twittering call.
Dark-eyed_Junco.Habitat: Conifer forests for breeding. Winters widely across North America in woodlands, suburbs, and gardens.
Dark-eyed_Junco.Similar Looking Birds: Oregon, Slate-colored, Pink-sided, White-winged, and Gray-headed forms vary regionally but all show white outer tail feathers.
Dark-eyed_Junco.Best Ways to Identify: White outer tail feathers flashing in flight are always present. Hooded dark gray head and pink bill identify most forms.

Dark-sided_Flycatcher.Description: Small flycatcher, dark gray-brown above, white below with dark brownish-gray sides and breast patches. About 5 inches.
Dark-sided_Flycatcher.Behavior: Sallies from forest perch for flying insects. Rare vagrant to western Alaska from East Asia.
Dark-sided_Flycatcher.Habitat: Coniferous and mixed forest of Siberia and East Asia. Rare vagrant to western Alaska.
Dark-sided_Flycatcher.Similar Looking Birds: Asian Brown Flycatcher paler, less contrasting sides. Gray-streaked Flycatcher has distinct breast streaking.
Dark-sided_Flycatcher.Best Ways to Identify: Dark smudgy sides contrasting with white center. Dark brown above. Rare Alaska vagrant from Siberia.

Demoiselle_Crane.Description: Medium crane, gray with black head and neck, white ear tufts, long black breast feathers. About 35 inches.
Demoiselle_Crane.Behavior: Migrates in massive flocks over Himalayas. Very rare vagrant to North America, likely from escapes.
Demoiselle_Crane.Habitat: Dry grasslands and wetlands of Central Asia and Africa. Extremely rare vagrant to North America.
Demoiselle_Crane.Similar Looking Birds: Sandhill Crane all gray without black head. Whooping Crane white. Black head and neck distinctive.
Demoiselle_Crane.Best Ways to Identify: Gray crane with black head, neck, and breast feathers. White ear tufts. Very rare vagrant or escaped bird.

Desertas_(Feas)_Petrel.Description: Large gadfly petrel, gray-brown above, gray breast band, white underparts, dark cap. About 16 inches.
Desertas_(Feas)_Petrel.Behavior: Breeds on Desertas and Cape Verde Islands. Migrates into North Atlantic; rare vagrant off Atlantic coast.
Desertas_(Feas)_Petrel.Habitat: North Atlantic Ocean. Rare vagrant offshore Atlantic coast of North America, particularly off Carolinas.
Desertas_(Feas)_Petrel.Similar Looking Birds: Zino's Petrel very similar but smaller. Bermuda Petrel has different head pattern.
Desertas_(Feas)_Petrel.Best Ways to Identify: Large gadfly petrel with gray breast band and white underparts. Dark cap. Rare Atlantic vagrant, particularly off Carolinas.

Dickcissel.Description: Medium sparrow-like bird. Males have yellow breast with black V-shaped bib, gray head with yellow eyebrow stripe, and chestnut wing patch. Females are paler without black bib. About 6 inches. Stout bill.
Dickcissel.Behavior: Males sing incessant "dick-dick-cissel" from grass or weed stalks. Forms huge flocks in migration and on winter grounds. Nomadic; numbers vary by year.
Dickcissel.Habitat: Grasslands, meadows, alfalfa and clover fields in central North America. Breeds in Great Plains and Midwest. Winters in Central and South America savannas.
Dickcissel.Similar Looking Birds: Meadowlarks are larger with different pattern. House Sparrow lacks yellow and black bib. Female Dickcissel resembles large sparrow but has yellow eyebrow.
Dickcissel.Best Ways to Identify: Black bib and yellow breast on male — distinctive. "Dick-cissel" song is unmistakable. Chestnut wing patch. Open grasslands and agricultural fields.

Double-crested_Cormorant.Description: All black with orange-yellow facial skin and throat pouch. Breeding adults develop small double crests on head.
Double-crested_Cormorant.Behavior: Dives for fish from the surface. Holds wings out to dry after diving. Flies in V-formation. Colonial nester.
Double-crested_Cormorant.Habitat: Coastal waters, bays, lakes, and rivers across North America. Most common and widespread cormorant in North America.
Double-crested_Cormorant.Similar Looking Birds: Neotropic Cormorant is smaller with longer tail. Great Cormorant is larger with white flank patches in breeding plumage.
Double-crested_Cormorant.Best Ways to Identify: Orange-yellow facial skin, kinked neck in flight, and wings- spread drying posture. Most common cormorant inland.

Double-striped_Thick-knee.Description: Large wader with long yellow legs, large yellow eye, cryptic brown and buff streaked plumage, two white facial stripes. About 19 inches.
Double-striped_Thick-knee.Behavior: Active at dusk and night. Runs rather than flies. Rare vagrant to Texas from Mexico and Central America. Calls loudly at night.
Double-striped_Thick-knee.Habitat: Dry grasslands, savannas, and open scrub in Mexico and Central America. Rare vagrant to South Texas.
Double-striped_Thick-knee.Similar Looking Birds: No similar large-eyed wader in US range. Double head stripes distinctive.
Double-striped_Thick-knee.Best Ways to Identify: Two bold white facial stripes, large yellow eye, and long yellow legs on large cryptic brown bird.

Double-toothed_Kite.Description: Small kite with two tooth-like notches on bill. Gray above, rufous-streaked below, white throat stripe. About 13 inches.
Double-toothed_Kite.Behavior: Hunts lizards and insects in tropical forest. Very rare vagrant to Texas and Florida from Mexico.
Double-toothed_Kite.Habitat: Tropical forest of Mexico and Central America. Very rare vagrant to southern Texas and Florida.
Double-toothed_Kite.Similar Looking Birds: Sharp-shinned Hawk similar size. Double-toothed Kite has distinctive tooth-notched bill.
Double-toothed_Kite.Best Ways to Identify: Two notches on bill sides. Rufous streaking below, white median throat stripe. Very rare tropical vagrant.

Dovekie.Description: Tiny alcid. Black above, white below, very small round body with stubby bill. About 8 inches.
Dovekie.Behavior: Swims and dives for copepods and small crustaceans. Winters offshore in huge numbers. Occasionally blown onshore during storms.
Dovekie.Habitat: Breeds in enormous colonies on Arctic cliffs. Winters offshore in North Atlantic. Occasional winter visitor to Atlantic coast after storms.
Dovekie.Similar Looking Birds: Much smaller than any puffin or murre. Ancient Murrelet similar tiny size but in Pacific.
Dovekie.Best Ways to Identify: Tiny size, black above and white below, stubby bill. Like a tiny penguin swimming. North Atlantic species.

Downy_Woodpecker.Description: Small woodpecker with black and white pattern, white back stripe, and short stubby bill. Male has red nape spot.
Downy_Woodpecker.Behavior: Forages on small branches and weed stems. Common at feeders. Drums on wood to communicate. High-pitched pik call.
Downy_Woodpecker.Habitat: Deciduous forests, parks, orchards, and suburbs across North America. The most common woodpecker at feeders.
Downy_Woodpecker.Similar Looking Birds: Hairy Woodpecker is larger with a longer bill. Ladder-backed Woodpecker in the West has barred back.
Downy_Woodpecker.Best Ways to Identify: Small size and stubby bill distinguish it from Hairy Woodpecker. White back stripe and small red nape spot on male.

Dunlin.Description: Breeding adult has rufous back, black belly patch, and drooped bill tip. Winter is plain gray-brown above, white below.
Dunlin.Behavior: Forages in tight flocks on mudflats, probing mud with bill. Spectacular murmurations in flight over tidal flats.
Dunlin.Habitat: Tidal mudflats, beaches, and wetlands during migration and winter. Breeds on Arctic tundra. Very common coastal shorebird.
Dunlin.Similar Looking Birds: Western Sandpiper and Sanderling lack drooped bill tip. Curlew Sandpiper has more curved bill and white rump.
Dunlin.Best Ways to Identify: Drooped bill tip is diagnostic. Black belly patch in breeding plumage unique. Common winter shorebird on coastal mudflats.

Dusky-capped_Flycatcher.Description: Small Myiarchus flycatcher, brown above, gray throat, yellow belly, dark cap. No rufous in tail. About 7 inches.
Dusky-capped_Flycatcher.Behavior: Gleans insects and small fruit. Common in oak-pine forest in southeastern Arizona and southwestern New Mexico.
Dusky-capped_Flycatcher.Habitat: Oak and pine-oak woodland canyons in southeastern Arizona. Year-round in some locations, summer visitor in others.
Dusky-capped_Flycatcher.Similar Looking Birds: Ash-throated Flycatcher has rufous in tail. Dusky-capped has dark cap with no rufous tail.
Dusky-capped_Flycatcher.Best Ways to Identify: Dark dusky cap, no rufous in tail. Yellow belly, gray throat. Southeastern Arizona oak woodland.

Dusky_Flycatcher.Description: Small, plain Empidonax flycatcher with olive-gray upperparts, whitish eye ring, two white wing bars, and pale whitish-yellow underparts. About 5.75 inches. Very difficult to distinguish from other Empidonax by sight alone.
Dusky_Flycatcher.Behavior: Perches upright in open areas, sallying out for insects. Often pumps tail. Song is the best identification feature: "chi-bit, p-wit, swee-it."
Dusky_Flycatcher.Habitat: Brushy mountain slopes, chaparral, and open coniferous forest with shrubby understory in western mountains. Winters in Mexico.
Dusky_Flycatcher.Similar Looking Birds: Hammond's Flycatcher is nearly identical; best separated by voice and habitat. Gray Flycatcher pumps tail downward more. Pacific-slope Flycatcher has yellow underparts. All Empidonax require voice for confident identification.
Dusky_Flycatcher.Best Ways to Identify: Voice is essential: song a slow, deliberate series of phrases. Brushy mountain slopes in summer. Eye ring present. When singing, even beginners can identify.

Dusky_Grouse.Description: Large grouse, dark gray overall with fine vermiculations. Males have yellow- orange comb over eye, gray tail with dark subterminal band, and purplish neck sacs inflated during display. Females brown and barred. About 20 inches.
Dusky_Grouse.Behavior: Walks forest floor; males display with deep booming calls. Eats conifer needles in winter, high in trees. Polygynous; males display on ridges. Moves to higher elevations after breeding.
Dusky_Grouse.Habitat: Coniferous and mixed forests of western mountains, from sagebrush foothills to high alpine. Found in Rocky Mountains and Pacific coast ranges.
Dusky_Grouse.Similar Looking Birds: Sooty Grouse (coastal) nearly identical but darker; separated by range. Spruce Grouse has black throat and red comb. Blue Grouse was the old name for both.
Dusky_Grouse.Best Ways to Identify: Large, dark grouse in western mountain conifer forests. Gray overall with yellow comb. Male's deep, resonant hooting display. Dense conifer habitat.

Dusky_Thrush.Description: Medium thrush, dark brown above with rufous wing panel, heavily spotted and scalloped below. White supercilium. About 9 inches.
Dusky_Thrush.Behavior: Forages on ground for invertebrates. Rare vagrant to western Alaska and Aleutian Islands from Asia.
Dusky_Thrush.Habitat: Open woodland and scrub in Siberia and Japan. Rare vagrant to western Alaska.
Dusky_Thrush.Similar Looking Birds: Naumann's Thrush similar but different in belly pattern. Eyebrowed Thrush cleaner pattern.
Dusky_Thrush.Best Ways to Identify: Dark brown with rufous wings, heavily spotted below. Bold white supercilium. Rare Alaska vagrant from Asia.

Dusky_Warbler.Description: Small plain leaf warbler, brown above, buff-white below with brown wash on flanks. Pale supercilium. About 4.5 inches.
Dusky_Warbler.Behavior: Skulks in low dense scrub near ground. Occasional hard tick call. Rare vagrant to western Alaska.
Dusky_Warbler.Habitat: Dense low scrub, willows, and riverine vegetation in Asia. Rare vagrant to western Alaska and Aleutians.
Dusky_Warbler.Similar Looking Birds: Chiffchaff has more olive tones. Radde's Warbler larger and buffer below. Separation can be very difficult.
Dusky_Warbler.Best Ways to Identify: Uniformly brown above without green or olive tones. Skulks near ground. Hard tick call note. Alaska vagrant.

Eared_Grebe.Description: Breeding adult has black neck and back, red eye, and golden fan-shaped ear tufts. Winter is dusky gray and white.
Eared_Grebe.Behavior: Dives for aquatic invertebrates. Masses in enormous flocks on alkaline lakes during molt. Rarely flies during migration.
Eared_Grebe.Habitat: Prairie lakes and alkaline wetlands in the western United States for nesting. Winters on bays and coastal waters.
Eared_Grebe.Similar Looking Birds: Horned Grebe has flat golden ear tufts, not fan-shaped. Black-necked Grebe is the same species name worldwide.
Eared_Grebe.Best Ways to Identify: Breeding adult's golden ear fans on black head unmistakable. Winter birds show dusky neck and high rounded crown.

Eared_Quetzal.Description: Large trogon, brilliant metallic green above, red belly. Male has no tail plumes unlike Resplendent Quetzal. About 14 inches.
Eared_Quetzal.Behavior: Forages for fruit and insects in mountain pine-oak forest. Rare and irregular visitor to southeastern Arizona.
Eared_Quetzal.Habitat: Mountain pine-oak forest. Rare irruptive visitor to Chiricahua and other mountain ranges in southeastern Arizona.
Eared_Quetzal.Similar Looking Birds: Elegant Trogon has copper-green back. Eared Quetzal brighter metallic green with ear tufts.
Eared_Quetzal.Best Ways to Identify: Brilliant metallic green with red belly, ear tufts. Rare irruptive visitor to Arizona mountain pine-oak forest.

Eastern_Bluebird.Description: Male is brilliant blue above with rusty-orange breast and white belly. Female is gray-blue with washed orange breast.
Eastern_Bluebird.Behavior: Perches on wires and fences, dropping to ground for insects. Nests in cavities. Soft musical warbling song.
Eastern_Bluebird.Habitat: Open woodlands, farmlands, and meadows with scattered trees across the eastern United States. Nests in tree cavities.
Eastern_Bluebird.Similar Looking Birds: Western Bluebird male has blue throat and orange on back. Mountain Bluebird male lacks orange and is all sky blue.
Eastern_Bluebird.Best Ways to Identify: Brilliant blue back and wings with rusty-orange breast on male are unmistakable. Female shows blue tones in wings and tail.

Eastern_Cattle-Egret.Description: Small white egret, orange-buff breeding plumes on head and neck. Very similar to Western Cattle-Egret. About 20 inches.
Eastern_Cattle-Egret.Behavior: Follows large animals. East Asian counterpart to Western Cattle-Egret. Vagrant to western Alaska.
Eastern_Cattle-Egret.Habitat: Pastures and open areas of East and Southeast Asia. Vagrant to western Alaska and Pacific coast.
Eastern_Cattle-Egret.Similar Looking Birds: Western Cattle-Egret nearly identical. Eastern has more orange on head and neck in breeding.
Eastern_Cattle-Egret.Best Ways to Identify: Nearly identical to Western Cattle-Egret. More extensive orange-buff head and neck in breeding. East Asian species.

Eastern_Kingbird.Description: Black above with white underparts and white-tipped black tail. Concealed orange-red crown stripe rarely visible.
Eastern_Kingbird.Behavior: Very aggressive toward large birds and raptors. Sallies from exposed perches to catch flying insects. Buzzy calls.
Eastern_Kingbird.Habitat: Open country, forest edges, and orchards across the eastern United States and Canada. Winters in South America.
Eastern_Kingbird.Similar Looking Birds: Western Kingbird has yellow belly and gray breast. Gray Kingbird lacks white tail tip and is found only coastally.
Eastern_Kingbird.Best Ways to Identify: Bold black-and-white pattern with white tail tip is distinctive. No other common flycatcher has this crisp pied coloring.

Eastern_Meadowlark.Description: Yellow breast with black V-shaped necklace, streaked brown back, white outer tail feathers visible in flight.
Eastern_Meadowlark.Behavior: Walks through grass probing for insects. Males sing from fence posts. Loud flute-like spring-of-the-year song.
Eastern_Meadowlark.Habitat: Grasslands, meadows, and farm fields of the eastern United States. Declining due to agricultural changes.
Eastern_Meadowlark.Similar Looking Birds: Western Meadowlark is nearly identical but has a different song. Both have yellow breast with black V.
Eastern_Meadowlark.Best Ways to Identify: Yellow breast with black V is unmistakable in open fields. Song is the best way to distinguish from Western Meadowlark.

Eastern_Phoebe.Description: Sooty-brown above, dirty white below with darker breast. No eye ring or wingbars. Constantly pumps tail downward.
Eastern_Phoebe.Behavior: Tail-pumping is distinctive. Often nests on bridges and eaves. One of the first spring migrants. Fee-bee song.
Eastern_Phoebe.Habitat: Woodland edges, farms, and areas near water across the eastern United States. Often nests under bridges.
Eastern_Phoebe.Similar Looking Birds: Eastern Wood-Pewee is similar but has wingbars. Empidonax flycatchers have eye rings and wingbars.
Eastern_Phoebe.Best Ways to Identify: Constant downward tail pumping is unique among eastern flycatchers. Fee-bee song and lack of wingbars or eye ring.

Eastern_Screech-Owl.Description: Small owl with ear tufts, yellow eyes, and streaked-and-barred plumage in either gray or rufous color morphs. About 8.5 inches. White-spotted scapulars. Streaked underparts. Camouflaged against tree bark.
Eastern_Screech-Owl.Behavior: Nocturnal hunter of insects, small rodents, birds, and earthworms. Roosts in tree cavities by day, resembling broken branch. Descending whinny call and long, even trill are distinctive.
Eastern_Screech-Owl.Habitat: Forests, woodlands, suburban parks, and orchards throughout eastern North America. Very adaptable; uses nest boxes readily. Year-round resident.
Eastern_Screech-Owl.Similar Looking Birds: Western Screech-Owl nearly identical but gray only, different call. Long-eared Owl much larger. Northern Saw-whet Owl lacks ear tufts. Flammulated Owl smaller.
Eastern_Screech-Owl.Best Ways to Identify: Small, tufted owl in Eastern woodlands. Two color morphs (gray and rufous). Descending whinny call at night. Often seen roosting in tree cavities by day.

Eastern_Spot-billed_Duck.Description: Large dabbling duck resembling female Mallard. Brown body, dark crown and eye stripe, yellow-tipped dark bill with orange-red spots at base. About 23 inches.
Eastern_Spot-billed_Duck.Behavior: Dabbles in shallow freshwater for plants, invertebrates, and seeds. Gregarious outside breeding season. Rare vagrant to western Alaska from East Asia.
Eastern_Spot-billed_Duck.Habitat: Breeds across East Asia in freshwater wetlands, lakes, and rivers. Winters in eastern China and Japan. Vagrant to Aleutian Islands.
Eastern_Spot-billed_Duck.Similar Looking Birds: Female Mallard nearly identical. Chinese Spot-billed Duck very similar. Distinguished by bill pattern.
Eastern_Spot-billed_Duck.Best Ways to Identify: Yellow bill tip with red basal spots distinctive. Dark body with pale face and prominent eye stripe.

Eastern_Towhee.Description: Male has black hood, rufous sides, white belly, and white wing spots. Female is brown where male is black.
Eastern_Towhee.Behavior: Scratches in leaf litter with both feet simultaneously. Drink-your-tea song and chewink call note. Secretive in brush.
Eastern_Towhee.Habitat: Dense shrubby forest understory and thickets across the eastern United States. Common in brushy habitats.
Eastern_Towhee.Similar Looking Birds: Spotted Towhee is nearly identical but has white spots on back. Range overlaps slightly in the Great Plains.
Eastern_Towhee.Best Ways to Identify: Rufous sides and black hood on male. Drink-your-tea song and two-footed scratch in leaf litter are behavioral clues.

Eastern_Warbling-Vireo.Description: Small plain vireo, olive-gray above, whitish below with faint yellowish wash on sides. No wing bars. About 5 inches.
Eastern_Warbling-Vireo.Behavior: Males sing a distinctive rambling warble almost continuously. Forages in canopy for caterpillars and insects.
Eastern_Warbling-Vireo.Habitat: Deciduous forests, orchards, parks, and suburban trees across eastern and central North America.
Eastern_Warbling-Vireo.Similar Looking Birds: Western Warbling-Vireo nearly identical but western range. Red-eyed Vireo has bold eye stripe.
Eastern_Warbling-Vireo.Best Ways to Identify: Plain vireo with no wing bars. Persistent warbling song. Eastern range. Faint supercilium but no bold eye stripe.

Eastern_Wood-Pewee.Description: Olive-gray above, pale below with two whitish wingbars and no eye ring. Flat crown and medium-sized bill.
Eastern_Wood-Pewee.Behavior: Sallies from mid-canopy perch to catch insects in flight. Returns to same perch. Mournful pee-a-wee song.
Eastern_Wood-Pewee.Habitat: Deciduous and mixed forests across the eastern United States. Winters in South America.
Eastern_Wood-Pewee.Similar Looking Birds: Eastern Phoebe lacks wingbars and pumps tail. Empidonax flycatchers have eye rings. Western Wood-Pewee identical.
Eastern_Wood-Pewee.Best Ways to Identify: Wingbars with no eye ring in forest interior. Distinctive mournful pee-a-wee song heard throughout summer.

Eastern_Yellow_Wagtail.Description: Small wagtail, olive-green above, bright yellow below, gray or olive head. Long tail constantly wagging. About 6.5 inches.
Eastern_Yellow_Wagtail.Behavior: Bobs tail up and down constantly. Forages in open wet areas. Breeds in western Alaska.
Eastern_Yellow_Wagtail.Habitat: Wet meadows, marshes, and tundra in western Alaska. Winters in Southeast Asia.
Eastern_Yellow_Wagtail.Similar Looking Birds: Citrine Wagtail has yellow head. White Wagtail gray above without yellow. Gray Wagtail has gray back.
Eastern_Yellow_Wagtail.Best Ways to Identify: Yellow underparts with olive or grayish head. Constant tail wagging. Western Alaska breeder on wet tundra.

Egyptian_Goose.Description: A large, long-legged waterfowl with brown body, conspicuous brown eye patches, and a pink bill. Shows white wing patches in flight.
Egyptian_Goose.Behavior: Grazes on grass and grain. Highly territorial and aggressive. Often seen perching on trees and buildings, unusual for a goose.
Egyptian_Goose.Habitat: Native to Africa and the Nile Valley. Introduced and established in Europe and North America near lakes, rivers, and parks.
Egyptian_Goose.Similar Looking Birds: Could be confused with Ruddy Shelduck in flight. The large white wing patches and brown eye patches are distinctive features.
Egyptian_Goose.Best Ways to Identify: Brown eye patches (spectacles), pink bill, white wing patches visible in flight, and long pink legs make this species unmistakable.

Elegant_Tern.Description: Large tern. White with gray back, shaggy black crest, long slender orange bill. About 17 inches.
Elegant_Tern.Behavior: Dives for fish. Breeds in small colonies in Baja California. Post-breeding dispersal north along Pacific coast in late summer.
Elegant_Tern.Habitat: Breeds on islands in Gulf of California. Post-breeding dispersal to California coast. Winters along South American Pacific coast.
Elegant_Tern.Similar Looking Birds: Royal Tern larger with stouter bill. Elegant Tern slimmer with longer drooping bill.
Elegant_Tern.Best Ways to Identify: Slender drooping orange bill. Shaggy black crest. Post-breeding flocks on California beaches in late summer.

Elegant_Trogon.Description: Male has metallic green head and back, red belly, white breast band, and long barred tail. Female is brown with red belly.
Elegant_Trogon.Behavior: Sits motionless in forest, hard to spot despite bright colors. Croaking kow-kow-kow call. Nests in woodpecker holes.
Elegant_Trogon.Habitat: Riparian canyon forests in southeastern Arizona, especially sycamore canyons. Winters in Mexico. Highly sought by birders.
Elegant_Trogon.Similar Looking Birds: No other bird in the United States has the same combination. Eared Quetzal is extremely rare visitor to Arizona.
Elegant_Trogon.Best Ways to Identify: Brilliant red belly, green back, and long barred tail are unmistakable in Arizona canyon forests.

Elf_Owl.Description: World's smallest owl. Tiny, brown streaked, pale eyebrows, no ear tufts, very short tail. About 5 inches.
Elf_Owl.Behavior: Nocturnal insect hunter. Nests in saguaro cactus cavities and tree holes. Summer resident in desert Southwest.
Elf_Owl.Habitat: Saguaro desert, oak woodland, and riparian canyons of Arizona, New Mexico, and Texas. Summer resident.
Elf_Owl.Similar Looking Birds: Pygmy-owls larger with longer tail. Elf Owl tiny with very short tail.
Elf_Owl.Best Ways to Identify: Tiny size with very short tail. Nocturnal. Nests in saguaro cactus holes. Desert Southwest summer resident.

Emperor_Goose.Description: Medium-sized goose with blue-gray body, white head and hindneck, orange-yellow legs. Black throat and foreneck. Adults have distinctly scaly patterned plumage.
Emperor_Goose.Behavior: Feeds on intertidal invertebrates, algae, and plant material. Forms large flocks during migration. Nests in low tundra vegetation near coastal areas.
Emperor_Goose.Habitat: Breeds along western Alaska coast and Siberia. Winters on Aleutian Islands and Alaska Peninsula shorelines in shallow coastal waters.
Emperor_Goose.Similar Looking Birds: Greater White-fronted Goose has similar size but lacks the white head. Snow Goose has all-white body. Cackling Goose is smaller with different head coloring.
Emperor_Goose.Best Ways to Identify: Look for the distinctive white head contrasting with dark body. The scaly blue-gray plumage pattern and orange legs are unique among North American geese.

Erckels_Spurfowl.Description: Large francolin from East Africa. Brown with chestnut- streaked underparts and distinctive chestnut crown. Males have leg spurs. About 16 inches.
Erckels_Spurfowl.Behavior: Found in dense forest understory. Forages for seeds, berries, and invertebrates on ground. Introduced to Hawaii in 1957 for hunting.
Erckels_Spurfowl.Habitat: Dense montane forest and woodland. In Hawaii found on Big Island and Maui in forested slopes and areas.
Erckels_Spurfowl.Similar Looking Birds: Other Hawaiian francolins. Erckel's larger with distinctive chestnut streaking on breast.
Erckels_Spurfowl.Best Ways to Identify: Large size, chestnut streaking on breast and flanks, chestnut crown. Loud calls in Hawaiian forest habitat.

Eskimo_Curlew.Description: Small curlew, possibly extinct. Brown streaked plumage, slightly downcurved bill, cinnamon wing lining. About 12 inches.
Eskimo_Curlew.Behavior: Migrated in huge flocks historically; hunted nearly to extinction. Last confirmed sighting 1987. May still survive but probably extinct.
Eskimo_Curlew.Habitat: Bred on Arctic tundra of northwest Canada. Wintered in South America. Once very common; now possibly extinct.
Eskimo_Curlew.Similar Looking Birds: Whimbrel and Little Curlew similar. Eskimo Curlew smaller with cinnamon wing linings.
Eskimo_Curlew.Best Ways to Identify: Possibly extinct; last confirmed 1987. Small curlew with cinnamon underwing. Any sighting would be extraordinary.

Eurasian_(Common)_Hoopoe.Description: Unmistakable bird with large fan-shaped crest, long curved bill, black-and-white barred wings and tail, pinkish-buff body. About 11 inches.
Eurasian_(Common)_Hoopoe.Behavior: Probes soil for insects and grubs with long curved bill. Common in Europe; rare vagrant to Alaska and Atlantic coast.
Eurasian_(Common)_Hoopoe.Habitat: Open woodland and farmland of Europe and Asia. Rare vagrant to Alaska and eastern North America.
Eurasian_(Common)_Hoopoe.Similar Looking Birds: No other North American bird resembles Hoopoe. Fan crest, barred wings completely distinctive.
Eurasian_(Common)_Hoopoe.Best Ways to Identify: Unmistakable: fan crest, curved bill, black-and-white barred wings. Cannot be confused with any other bird.

Eurasian_(Common)_Moorhen.Description: Medium waterbird. Dark blackish with brown back, white flank stripe, distinctive red frontal shield and bill with yellow tip. About 13 inches.
Eurasian_(Common)_Moorhen.Behavior: Swims and walks along water edges. Nods head while swimming. Common in Europe and Asia; rare vagrant to northeastern North America.
Eurasian_(Common)_Moorhen.Habitat: Freshwater ponds, marshes, and slow rivers with emergent vegetation. Common in Europe; rare vagrant to North America.
Eurasian_(Common)_Moorhen.Similar Looking Birds: Common Moorhen (North American race) nearly identical. American Coot lacks white flank stripes.
Eurasian_(Common)_Moorhen.Best Ways to Identify: Red frontal shield and yellow-tipped red bill. White flank stripe on dark body. Head- bobbing swim motion.

Eurasian_Blackbird.Description: Male entirely black with yellow bill and eye ring. Female brown with spotted breast. About 10 inches.
Eurasian_Blackbird.Behavior: Common garden bird in Europe. Bold forager on ground. Very rare vagrant to eastern North America.
Eurasian_Blackbird.Habitat: Gardens, parks, woodland, and scrub in Europe and Asia. Very rare vagrant to Atlantic coast of North America.
Eurasian_Blackbird.Similar Looking Birds: American Robin similar body shape but has red breast. Rusty Blackbird lacks yellow bill.
Eurasian_Blackbird.Best Ways to Identify: Male: entirely black with yellow bill and eye ring. Female: brown with spotted breast. European vagrant.

Eurasian_Bullfinch.Description: Stocky finch. Male bright pink-red breast, black cap, gray back, white rump. Female similar with brownish-pink. About 6 inches.
Eurasian_Bullfinch.Behavior: Eats buds and seeds. Rare vagrant to western Alaska and Aleutian Islands from Asia.
Eurasian_Bullfinch.Habitat: Woodland and scrub of Europe and Asia. Rare vagrant to western Alaska.
Eurasian_Bullfinch.Similar Looking Birds: Purple Finch male pinkish-red but streaked. No similar black-capped red finch in Alaska range.
Eurasian_Bullfinch.Best Ways to Identify: Pink-red breast, black cap, gray back, white rump. Stocky shape. Rare Alaska vagrant from Siberia.

Eurasian_Collared-Dove.Description: Pale grayish-tan dove with narrow black half-collar on nape. Squared tail with white corners and dark base.
Eurasian_Collared-Dove.Behavior: Coos a repetitive coo-COO-coo. Very common around human settlements. Aggressive toward other dove species.
Eurasian_Collared-Dove.Habitat: Towns, suburbs, farms, and urban areas across North America. Introduced from Europe; rapidly expanding continent-wide.
Eurasian_Collared-Dove.Similar Looking Birds: Mourning Dove is slimmer with a pointed tail and no collar. Ringed Turtle-Dove is similar but paler and less common.
Eurasian_Collared-Dove.Best Ways to Identify: Black half-collar on nape and square tail with white corners. Repetitive three-note coo-COO-coo call in urban areas.

Eurasian_Coot.Description: Medium waterbird. Entirely sooty black with brilliant white bill and white frontal shield. Red eye. About 15 inches.
Eurasian_Coot.Behavior: Swims in open water; dives for aquatic plants. Aggressive and quarrelsome. Rare vagrant to eastern North America from Eurasia.
Eurasian_Coot.Habitat: Freshwater and coastal lakes and ponds across Eurasia. Rare vagrant to Atlantic coast and interior North America.
Eurasian_Coot.Similar Looking Birds: American Coot nearly identical; nearly impossible to tell apart. Both black with white bill and shield.
Eurasian_Coot.Best Ways to Identify: Nearly identical to American Coot. Eurasian has slightly different bill and frontal shield shape. Rare vagrant from Eurasia.

Eurasian_Curlew.Description: Very large curlew. Brown streaked plumage, white rump, very long strongly downcurved bill. About 22 inches.
Eurasian_Curlew.Behavior: Forages on mudflats and grasslands for invertebrates and worms. Loud "cur-lee" call. Rare vagrant to Atlantic coast from Eurasia.
Eurasian_Curlew.Habitat: Breeds on European and Asian moorland and wet meadows. Winters on European coasts. Rare vagrant to North America.
Eurasian_Curlew.Similar Looking Birds: Whimbrel smaller. Far Eastern Curlew has dark rump. White rump distinguishes Eurasian Curlew.
Eurasian_Curlew.Best Ways to Identify: Very large curlew with white rump and lower back visible in flight. Loud "cur-lee" call distinctive.

Eurasian_Dotterel.Description: Medium plover. Breeding adult has rusty-orange breast with white breast band, gray-brown upperparts, bold white supercilium. About 9 inches.
Eurasian_Dotterel.Behavior: Feeds on insects and invertebrates. Tame and approachable. Female more colorful; roles reversed in breeding. Rare vagrant to western Alaska from Siberia.
Eurasian_Dotterel.Habitat: Breeds on high Arctic tundra in Eurasia. Rare vagrant to western Alaska and Pacific coast of North America.
Eurasian_Dotterel.Similar Looking Birds: Other Charadrius plovers. Eurasian Dotterel's white breast band and supercilium distinctive.
Eurasian_Dotterel.Best Ways to Identify: Bold white supercilium and white breast band across orange-rufous breast. Tame behavior. Rare vagrant in western Alaska.

Eurasian_Hobby.Description: Elegant small falcon, dark gray above, white below with heavy black streaks, rufous thighs and vent. Long pointed wings. About 12 inches.
Eurasian_Hobby.Behavior: Swift aerial hunter catching swallows and large insects in flight. Common in Europe; rare vagrant to Alaska and Atlantic coast.
Eurasian_Hobby.Habitat: Open country with scattered trees in Europe and Asia. Rare vagrant to Alaska and eastern North America.
Eurasian_Hobby.Similar Looking Birds: Merlin similar size. Eurasian Hobby has rufous thighs and more elegant shape.
Eurasian_Hobby.Best Ways to Identify: Rufous thighs and undertail, heavy streaking below. Long slender wings. Rare vagrant from Europe and Asia.

Eurasian_Jackdaw.Description: Small crow, glossy black with gray nape and sides of head. Pale eye distinctive. About 13 inches.
Eurasian_Jackdaw.Behavior: Highly social, nests in chimneys and cliff cavities. Uses tools and solves complex problems. Rare vagrant to North America.
Eurasian_Jackdaw.Habitat: Open farmland, cliffs, urban areas across Europe and Asia. Very rare vagrant to northeastern North America.
Eurasian_Jackdaw.Similar Looking Birds: American Crow all black without gray nape. Common Raven much larger. No similar crow in North America.
Eurasian_Jackdaw.Best Ways to Identify: Small crow with gray nape and pale silvery eye. Very rare vagrant from Europe. Distinctive two-tone pattern.

Eurasian_Kestrel.Description: Small falcon, male with rufous back and gray head and tail, spots below. Female brown barred throughout. About 13 inches.
Eurasian_Kestrel.Behavior: Hovers while hunting small mammals and insects in open areas. Common in Europe; rare vagrant to Alaska and Atlantic coast.
Eurasian_Kestrel.Habitat: Open grassland and farmland of Europe and Asia. Rare vagrant to Atlantic coast and Alaska.
Eurasian_Kestrel.Similar Looking Birds: American Kestrel similar but smaller and more colorful. Eurasian Kestrel larger with less colorful face.
Eurasian_Kestrel.Best Ways to Identify: Hovering kestrel behavior. Male's gray head with rufous back. Larger and less colorful than American Kestrel.

Eurasian_Oystercatcher.Description: Large black and white shorebird with long orange- red bill, pink legs, and orange eye ring. About 17 inches.
Eurasian_Oystercatcher.Behavior: Pries open mollusks and probes for worms on rocky shores and mudflats. Rare vagrant to eastern North America from Europe.
Eurasian_Oystercatcher.Habitat: Rocky and sandy coasts of Eurasia. Rare vagrant to northeastern North America, mostly Atlantic maritime provinces.
Eurasian_Oystercatcher.Similar Looking Birds: American Oystercatcher nearly identical; has brown back rather than black.
Eurasian_Oystercatcher.Best Ways to Identify: All-black upperparts with white underparts and orange- red bill. Rare vagrant; American Oystercatcher has brown back.

Eurasian_Siskin.Description: Small finch, yellow-green with black crown and chin on male, streaked olive on female, yellow wing bars. About 4.5 inches.
Eurasian_Siskin.Behavior: Forages in alders and birches for seeds. Gregarious in flocks. Rare vagrant to western Alaska.
Eurasian_Siskin.Habitat: Coniferous and mixed forest of Europe and Asia. Rare vagrant to western Alaska and Aleutians.
Eurasian_Siskin.Similar Looking Birds: Pine Siskin streaked without black crown. American Goldfinch larger without streaking.
Eurasian_Siskin.Best Ways to Identify: Male black crown and chin with yellow-green. Yellow wing bars. Rare Alaska vagrant from Asia.

Eurasian_Skylark.Description: Medium lark, streaked brown above, pale below with streaked breast, small crest. Long hind claw. About 7 inches.
Eurasian_Skylark.Behavior: Delivers prolonged song while hovering high over open fields. Introduced to Vancouver Island, British Columbia.
Eurasian_Skylark.Habitat: Open grasslands, agricultural fields, meadows. Small introduced population on southern Vancouver Island, British Columbia.
Eurasian_Skylark.Similar Looking Birds: Horned Lark has bold face pattern with no crest. Pipits lack crest and are slimmer.
Eurasian_Skylark.Best Ways to Identify: Small crest, streaked brown plumage, song-flight hovering high over open fields. Vancouver Island introduced population.

Eurasian_Sparrowhawk.Description: Small accipiter. Male blue-gray above with orange- barred underparts; female brown above, brown-barred below. About 13 inches.
Eurasian_Sparrowhawk.Behavior: Dashes through woodland to catch small birds. Common in Europe; rare vagrant to Alaska and Atlantic Canada.
Eurasian_Sparrowhawk.Habitat: Woodland and forest of Europe and Asia. Rare vagrant to Alaska and Atlantic Canada.
Eurasian_Sparrowhawk.Similar Looking Birds: Sharp-shinned Hawk very similar. Eurasian Sparrowhawk male has orange barring below.
Eurasian_Sparrowhawk.Best Ways to Identify: Male: blue-gray above with orange-barred underparts. Old World counterpart to Sharp-shinned. Rare vagrant to Alaska.

Eurasian_Tree_Sparrow.Description: Small sparrow similar to House Sparrow. Brown above with chestnut cap, white cheeks with black spot. About 5.5 inches.
Eurasian_Tree_Sparrow.Behavior: Nests in cavities and crevices. Forages for seeds in flocks. Introduced population in St. Louis, Missouri area.
Eurasian_Tree_Sparrow.Habitat: Farmland, villages, and open areas. Small introduced population in Missouri and adjacent states.
Eurasian_Tree_Sparrow.Similar Looking Birds: House Sparrow lacks chestnut cap and cheek spot. Male House Sparrow has gray crown.
Eurasian_Tree_Sparrow.Best Ways to Identify: Chestnut cap and black spot on white cheek distinctive. Missouri area introduced population. Similar size to House Sparrow.

Eurasian_Whimbrel.Description: Large curlew with downcurved bill, striped crown, brown streaked plumage, white lower back and rump. About 17 inches.
Eurasian_Whimbrel.Behavior: Forages on mudflats and rocky shores for crabs and invertebrates. Rare vagrant to North America; white rump distinguishes it from Hudsonian Whimbrel.
Eurasian_Whimbrel.Habitat: Breeds on Eurasian tundra. Winters on African and Asian coasts. Rare vagrant to Atlantic coast of North America.
Eurasian_Whimbrel.Similar Looking Birds: Hudsonian Whimbrel nearly identical but has dark rump. White rump is key.
Eurasian_Whimbrel.Best Ways to Identify: White rump and lower back visible in flight distinguishes from Hudsonian Whimbrel. Otherwise nearly identical curlew.

Eurasian_Wigeon.Description: Medium dabbling duck. Male has chestnut head with creamy-yellow forehead, gray body, pink breast, and white belly. White wing patch. Female is brown, similar to American Wigeon female. About 20 inches.
Eurasian_Wigeon.Behavior: Grazes on grass and aquatic vegetation in flocks. Often mixes with American Wigeons. Male gives distinctive whistling call. Dives occasionally.
Eurasian_Wigeon.Habitat: Eurasian breeder; regular winter visitor to both U.S. coasts, especially Pacific coast. Found in estuaries, marshes, ponds, and flooded fields. Rare inland.
Eurasian_Wigeon.Similar Looking Birds: American Wigeon male has green eye patch and white crown. Female Eurasian Wigeon extremely similar to female American; head color and axillary feathers differ subtly. Often only one or two Eurasian in a mixed wigeon flock.
Eurasian_Wigeon.Best Ways to Identify: Male's chestnut head with cream forehead (not white crown of American). Look carefully through wigeon flocks on Pacific coast. Whistling male call differs.

Eurasian_Woodcock.Description: Large cryptic woodland bird. Reddish-brown plumage with complex pattern, long bill, large eye positioned high on head. About 13 inches.
Eurasian_Woodcock.Behavior: Feeds on earthworms by probing in forest floor. Nocturnal. Males perform "roding" display flights at dusk. Rare vagrant to North America.
Eurasian_Woodcock.Habitat: Deciduous woodland in Eurasia. Rare vagrant to Atlantic coast of North America, mostly in fall.
Eurasian_Woodcock.Similar Looking Birds: American Woodcock similar but smaller and shorter billed.
Eurasian_Woodcock.Best Ways to Identify: Larger than American Woodcock with stronger, bolder barring. Very similar; best identified by size and subtle plumage details.

Eurasian_Wryneck.Description: Cryptically patterned woodpecker relative, gray-brown mottled plumage with dark back stripe. About 7 inches.
Eurasian_Wryneck.Behavior: Eats ants; twists neck dramatically when threatened. Rare vagrant to Alaska and Atlantic coast from Eurasia.
Eurasian_Wryneck.Habitat: Open woodland and gardens of Europe and Asia. Rare vagrant to Alaska and coastal eastern North America.
Eurasian_Wryneck.Similar Looking Birds: Nightjars have similar cryptic plumage. Wryneck has woodpecker-like feet and ant-eating habits.
Eurasian_Wryneck.Best Ways to Identify: Cryptic mottled brown-gray, no red on head. Unusual neck-twisting behavior. Rare vagrant from Europe and Asia.

European_Golden-Plover.Description: Medium plover. Golden-speckled brown upperparts, breeding male has black face and underparts bordered white. About 11 inches.
European_Golden-Plover.Behavior: Forages on fields and moorland for invertebrates and berries. Forms large winter flocks. Rare vagrant to eastern North America from Europe.
European_Golden-Plover.Habitat: Breeds on European moorland and tundra. Winters on European farmland and grasslands. Rare vagrant to Atlantic coast of North America.
European_Golden-Plover.Similar Looking Birds: American Golden-Plover very similar. European lacks axillar markings; white underwing.
European_Golden-Plover.Best Ways to Identify: White underwing coverts distinguish from American Golden-Plover in flight. Rare vagrant on Atlantic coast of North America.

European_Goldfinch.Description: Small finch, red face, black-and-white head, brown body, bright yellow wing band. About 5 inches.
European_Goldfinch.Behavior: Forages for seeds especially thistles and teasel. Gregarious in flocks. Small introduced populations in North America.
European_Goldfinch.Habitat: Open areas, gardens, and woodland edges. Small introduced populations in New York and possibly other areas.
European_Goldfinch.Similar Looking Birds: American Goldfinch lacks red face and different pattern. No other bird has red face plus yellow wing band.
