European_Goldfinch.Best Ways to Identify: Red face, black-and-white head, bright yellow wing band. Unmistakable. Small introduced North American populations.

European_Herring_Gull.Description: Large gull, pale gray back, pink legs, yellow bill with red spot, pale eye. White head and underparts. About 24 inches.
European_Herring_Gull.Behavior: Very common gull in Europe. Rare vagrant to Atlantic coast of North America. Scavenges in harbors and coastal areas.
European_Herring_Gull.Habitat: Atlantic and North Sea coasts of Europe. Rare vagrant to northeastern North America especially in winter.
European_Herring_Gull.Similar Looking Birds: American Herring Gull nearly identical. European Herring Gull often indistinguishable in the field.
European_Herring_Gull.Best Ways to Identify: Very similar to American Herring Gull. Differences subtle in wing tip pattern. Rare Atlantic vagrant best identified carefully.

European_Robin.Description: Small round bird with orange-red face and breast, brown above, white belly. About 5.5 inches.
European_Robin.Behavior: Bold and tame in gardens. Sings year-round from prominent perch. Very rare vagrant to northeastern North America.
European_Robin.Habitat: Woodland, gardens, and parks across Europe. Very rare vagrant to northeastern North America.
European_Robin.Similar Looking Birds: American Robin much larger. No similar bird with orange-red face in North America.
European_Robin.Best Ways to Identify: Bright orange-red face and breast distinctive. Round shape. Very rare European vagrant to East Coast.

European_Starling.Description: Medium bird, iridescent black with green and purple gloss, yellow bill in summer, spotted in winter. About 8.5 inches.
European_Starling.Behavior: Introduced from Europe in 1890; now extremely abundant. Forms massive murmurations. Aggressive nest competitor.
European_Starling.Habitat: Cities, suburbs, farms, parks, and open areas throughout North America. One of commonest birds in the continent.
European_Starling.Similar Looking Birds: Grackles have longer tails and different bill shape. Blackbirds lack iridescence. Short tail distinctive.
European_Starling.Best Ways to Identify: Short tail, iridescent black, yellow bill in summer. Heavy spotting in winter. Walking gait, not hopping.

European_Storm-Petrel.Description: Tiny dark storm-petrel with white rump, square tail, weak fluttery flight. Smallest seabird in Europe. About 6 inches.
European_Storm-Petrel.Behavior: Breeds on European Atlantic islands. Very rare vagrant to North American Atlantic coast. Fluttery butterfly-like flight.
European_Storm-Petrel.Habitat: North Atlantic and Mediterranean. Very rare vagrant to offshore North American Atlantic coast.
European_Storm-Petrel.Similar Looking Birds: Wilson's Storm-Petrel has longer legs, more direct flight. European is smaller and fluttery.
European_Storm-Petrel.Best Ways to Identify: Tiny size, fluttery flight, white rump, square tail. Very rare Atlantic vagrant. Smallest ocean seabird.

European_Turtle-Dove.Description: Small dove with orange-brown scaly upperparts, pink breast, and black and white striped neck patch. Long graduated tail. About 11 inches.
European_Turtle-Dove.Behavior: Feeds on seeds and plant material on ground. Long- distance migrant. Rare vagrant to North America; most records from Atlantic coast islands.
European_Turtle-Dove.Habitat: Breeds in European farmland, hedgerows, and open woodland. Winters in sub-Saharan Africa. Rare vagrant to eastern North America.
European_Turtle-Dove.Similar Looking Birds: Oriental Turtle-Dove larger and darker. Mourning Dove slimmer without neck patch.
European_Turtle-Dove.Best Ways to Identify: Orange-brown scaly back with striped neck patch. Small size and purring flight call. Rare vagrant in eastern North America.

Evening_Grosbeak.Description: Large finch with massive pale yellow-green bill. Male is yellow with black wings and white wing patch.
Evening_Grosbeak.Behavior: Nomadic; irrupts south following cone crops. Very loud call. Cracks large seeds with powerful bill. Visits feeders.
Evening_Grosbeak.Habitat: Conifer and mixed forests of the western mountains and boreal north. Winters irregularly across North America.
Evening_Grosbeak.Similar Looking Birds: American Goldfinch is much smaller. Yellow Grosbeak is similar but found only in Mexico and is rare in the US.
Evening_Grosbeak.Best Ways to Identify: Massive pale bill, bold yellow-and-black pattern, and white wing patch on male. Very loud ringing call in flocks.

Eyebrowed_Thrush.Description: Medium thrush, brown above with bold white supercilium, orange-buff breast and flanks, white belly. About 9 inches.
Eyebrowed_Thrush.Behavior: Forages on ground for earthworms and berries. Rare vagrant to western Alaska and Aleutian Islands from Asia.
Eyebrowed_Thrush.Habitat: Forests of Siberia and East Asia. Rare vagrant to western Alaska and occasionally farther into North America.
Eyebrowed_Thrush.Similar Looking Birds: Dusky Thrush has more complex pattern. American Robin has red breast without bold supercilium.
Eyebrowed_Thrush.Best Ways to Identify: Bold white supercilium on brown thrush. Orange-buff breast contrasting with white belly. Rare Asia vagrant.

Falcated_Duck.Description: Medium dabbling duck. Male has iridescent green and chestnut head, white throat patch, long sickle-shaped tertial feathers. Female mottled brown. About 20 inches.
Falcated_Duck.Behavior: Dabbles and grazes on aquatic vegetation. Migrates through East Asia. Rare vagrant to western Alaska and Pacific Coast.
Falcated_Duck.Habitat: Breeds near rivers and lakes in East Asian forests. Winters in East Asian coastal bays, estuaries, and rice fields.
Falcated_Duck.Similar Looking Birds: Gadwall somewhat similar in female plumage. Male's long drooping tertials unique among ducks.
Falcated_Duck.Best Ways to Identify: Male's elaborate head pattern and long curved tertial feathers unmistakable. Female's finely barred plumage with dark bill.

Fan-tailed_Warbler.Description: Large ground warbler, dark gray above, bright orange-rufous below, white-tipped tail fanned and bobbed. About 6 inches.
Fan-tailed_Warbler.Behavior: Forages on or near ground, constantly fanning white-tipped tail. Rare vagrant to Arizona from Mexico.
Fan-tailed_Warbler.Habitat: Rocky canyon streams in western Mexico. Rare vagrant to southeastern Arizona.
Fan-tailed_Warbler.Similar Looking Birds: No similar bird fans tail like this. Orange-rufous below with white tail tips unique.
Fan-tailed_Warbler.Best Ways to Identify: White-tipped tail constantly fanned and bobbed. Orange-rufous below. Dark gray above. Rare Arizona vagrant.

Far_Eastern_Curlew.Description: Largest curlew in the world. Brown streaked plumage, very long strongly downcurved bill, brownish rump. About 24 inches.
Far_Eastern_Curlew.Behavior: Forages on mudflats for crabs and invertebrates. Rare vagrant to Pacific coast from East Asian wintering grounds.
Far_Eastern_Curlew.Habitat: Breeds on Siberian and Alaskan tundra. Winters on Australian and East Asian coasts. Rare vagrant to western North America.
Far_Eastern_Curlew.Similar Looking Birds: Eurasian Curlew similar but has white rump. Far Eastern has dark rump.
Far_Eastern_Curlew.Best Ways to Identify: Enormous size and very long curved bill. Dark brownish rump in flight. Rare vagrant on Pacific coast.

Ferruginous_Hawk.Description: Largest North American buteo. Rusty-orange back and legs form dark V against white belly in flight. Pale form common.
Ferruginous_Hawk.Behavior: Hunts prairie dogs and ground squirrels. Soars on long wings with wrist patches. Nests on the ground or in trees.
Ferruginous_Hawk.Habitat: Open grasslands and prairies of the western Great Plains and intermountain basins. Winters in southwestern grasslands.
Ferruginous_Hawk.Similar Looking Birds: Red-tailed Hawk lacks the rusty leg feathering. Rough-legged Hawk has dark belly band and black wrist patches.
Ferruginous_Hawk.Best Ways to Identify: Rusty leg feathers forming V shape against white belly in flight. Largest buteo with very long broad wings.

Ferruginous_Pygmy-Owl.Description: Tiny owl, rufous-brown streaked below. False eyespots on nape, streaked crown. Rufous tail with dark bars. About 7 inches.
Ferruginous_Pygmy-Owl.Behavior: Diurnal and crepuscular. Hunts birds and lizards. Rare resident in southern Texas and southern Arizona.
Ferruginous_Pygmy-Owl.Habitat: Saguaro desert and mesquite in southern Arizona; riparian thickets in southern Texas. Rare resident.
Ferruginous_Pygmy-Owl.Similar Looking Birds: Northern Pygmy-Owl at higher elevation. Ferruginous Pygmy-Owl in lowland desert and thorn forest.
Ferruginous_Pygmy-Owl.Best Ways to Identify: Tiny rufous-brown owl active by day. Rufous tail. Southern Texas and Arizona lowlands. False nape eyespots.

Field_Sparrow.Description: Small sparrow with plain face, pink bill, rufous cap, rufous-gray back, and buffy-white underparts. White eye ring, rufous eye line. About 5.75 inches. No breast streaking. Clean, plain face is distinctive.
Field_Sparrow.Behavior: Forages on ground for seeds and insects. Males sing a distinctive song of accelerating notes ending in a trill — a "bouncing ball" pattern. Pairs are territorial in open brushy areas.
Field_Sparrow.Habitat: Brushy fields, shrubby grasslands, forest edges, and overgrown pastures in eastern North America. Prefers areas with shrubs for singing perches.
Field_Sparrow.Similar Looking Birds: American Tree Sparrow has central breast spot and bicolored bill. Chipping Sparrow has white eye stripe over black line. Field Sparrow's pink bill and plain face are key.
Field_Sparrow.Best Ways to Identify: Pink bill, rufous cap, plain unstreaked face, and white eye ring. Bouncing- ball accelerating song in shrubby fields. Eastern brushy habitats.

Fieldfare.Description: Large thrush, gray head and rump, chestnut back, spotted orange-buff breast, white underwings. About 10 inches.
Fieldfare.Behavior: Forages in flocks on open ground. Rare vagrant to northeastern North America and Greenland from Europe.
Fieldfare.Habitat: Open woodland, farmland, and berry-bearing hedges in Europe. Rare vagrant to North America.
Fieldfare.Similar Looking Birds: Mistle Thrush lacks gray head and chestnut back. American Robin lacks spotted pattern with chestnut back.
Fieldfare.Best Ways to Identify: Gray head and rump contrasting with chestnut back. Bold spotted breast. Rare European vagrant. Flocks in open.

Fish_Crow.Description: All black; nearly identical to American Crow but slightly smaller. Best identified by voice.
Fish_Crow.Behavior: Coastal and riparian scavenger. Voice is a nasal uh-uh or ca-ha instead of the American Crow's caw.
Fish_Crow.Habitat: Coastal areas, riverbanks, and tidal wetlands in the eastern United States. Increasingly common inland along rivers.
Fish_Crow.Similar Looking Birds: American Crow is nearly identical. Separating them requires hearing the voice - Fish Crow gives a nasal two-note call.
Fish_Crow.Best Ways to Identify: Nasal two-note uh-uh call is the only reliable field mark. Size difference too subtle to use in the field alone.

Five-striped_Sparrow.Description: Distinctive sparrow, gray above, white below with black breast spot, five white stripes on face. About 6 inches.
Five-striped_Sparrow.Behavior: Skulks in dense steep canyon vegetation. Difficult to observe. Rare bird in extreme southeast Arizona.
Five-striped_Sparrow.Habitat: Dense brushy slopes in canyon systems of extreme southeast Arizona. Very localized.
Five-striped_Sparrow.Similar Looking Birds: No other sparrow has the distinctive five-stripe face pattern. Unique and unmistakable.
Five-striped_Sparrow.Best Ways to Identify: Five white facial stripes distinctive. Black breast spot. Gray above, white below. Steep canyon scrub Arizona.

Flame-colored_Tanager.Description: Medium tanager. Male flame-orange with black-streaked back, white wing bars. Female olive with wing bars. About 7.5 inches.
Flame-colored_Tanager.Behavior: Forages in pine-oak forest canopy. Rare vagrant to Arizona mountains from Mexico.
Flame-colored_Tanager.Habitat: Pine-oak forests of Mexico and Central America. Rare vagrant to southeastern Arizona.
Flame-colored_Tanager.Similar Looking Birds: Western Tanager has black back without streaks. Hepatic Tanager darker red-orange. Streaked back distinctive.
Flame-colored_Tanager.Best Ways to Identify: Flame-orange with streaked black back. White wing bars. Rare Arizona vagrant from Mexico.

Flammulated_Owl.Description: Tiny owl with cryptic gray-brown mottled plumage and rusty facial disc. Small size and dark eyes.
Flammulated_Owl.Behavior: Strictly nocturnal, feeds almost entirely on insects. Migrates to Central America in winter.
Flammulated_Owl.Habitat: Dry ponderosa pine forests in western mountains at mid to high elevations.
Flammulated_Owl.Similar Looking Birds: Much smaller than other owls. Western Screech-Owl has yellow eyes and streaked underparts.
Flammulated_Owl.Best Ways to Identify: Tiny size, dark eyes, moth-like flight, and insect-focused diet in pine forests.

Flesh-footed_Shearwater.Description: All dark brown shearwater with distinctive pale pink-flesh colored bill and feet. About 19 inches.
Flesh-footed_Shearwater.Behavior: Breeds in Australia and New Zealand. Uncommon visitor to Pacific coast of North America in summer and fall.
Flesh-footed_Shearwater.Habitat: North Pacific Ocean. Uncommon offshore Pacific coast. Breeds in Southern Hemisphere.
Flesh-footed_Shearwater.Similar Looking Birds: Sooty Shearwater similar but has dark bill. Flesh-footed's pale pink bill distinctive.
Flesh-footed_Shearwater.Best Ways to Identify: All-dark body with pale pink bill and feet diagnostic. No other dark shearwater combines all-dark plumage with pale bill.

Florida_Scrub-Jay.Description: Blue and white jay with no crest. Blue wings, tail, and head collar; gray back and underparts.
Florida_Scrub-Jay.Behavior: Cooperative breeder living in family groups. Caches acorns and forages on the ground.
Florida_Scrub-Jay.Habitat: Florida scrub habitat — open sandy areas with low oaks and saw palmetto.
Florida_Scrub-Jay.Similar Looking Birds: Similar to other scrub-jays but range is unique; Florida is the only state it lives in.
Florida_Scrub-Jay.Best Ways to Identify: Only jay in Florida scrub habitat. Lacks crest. Blue head, white forehead stripe.

Fork-tailed_Flycatcher.Description: Unmistakable flycatcher with enormously long forked black tail. Black above, white below, gray head. About 15 inches with tail.
Fork-tailed_Flycatcher.Behavior: Migratory South American tyrant flycatcher. Rare but regular vagrant along Atlantic coast during fall migration.
Fork-tailed_Flycatcher.Habitat: Open grassland and savanna of South America. Regular vagrant to Atlantic coast particularly in fall.
Fork-tailed_Flycatcher.Similar Looking Birds: No other North American flycatcher has such long forked tail.
Fork-tailed_Flycatcher.Best Ways to Identify: Enormously long forked black tail. Black cap, white below. Regular fall vagrant to Atlantic coast.

Fork-tailed_Storm-Petrel.Description: Pale gray storm-petrel, gray above and below, darker eye patch, forked tail. Only gray storm-petrel in North America. About 8 inches.
Fork-tailed_Storm-Petrel.Behavior: Breeds on North Pacific islands off California, Oregon, Washington, and Alaska. Common offshore North Pacific seabird.
Fork-tailed_Storm-Petrel.Habitat: North Pacific Ocean. Breeds on offshore islands; forages over North Pacific, particularly common in Pacific Northwest.
Fork-tailed_Storm-Petrel.Similar Looking Birds: All other North American storm-petrels are dark. Gray color unique among storm-petrels.
Fork-tailed_Storm-Petrel.Best Ways to Identify: Gray plumage unique among storm-petrels. Forked tail, darker gray eye patch. North Pacific coast seabird.

Forsters_Tern.Description: Medium tern with white plumage, pale gray back, and deeply forked tail. Orange-red bill with black tip.
Forsters_Tern.Behavior: Hovers and plunge-dives for fish. Often seen over marshes and coastal waters.
Forsters_Tern.Habitat: Coastal bays, marshes, and inland lakes throughout North America.
Forsters_Tern.Similar Looking Birds: Common Tern very similar; Forster's has frosted wingtips and in winter has eye patch not cap.
Forsters_Tern.Best Ways to Identify: Orange bill, frosted wingtips, isolated black eye patch in winter — not a dark cap.

Fox_Sparrow.Description: Large chunky sparrow with rusty-red streaked plumage. Heavy bill and large size distinguish it.
Fox_Sparrow.Behavior: Scratches vigorously in leaf litter with both feet to uncover seeds and invertebrates.
Fox_Sparrow.Habitat: Dense thickets and shrubby areas; breeds in boreal and mountain forests.
Fox_Sparrow.Similar Looking Birds: Song Sparrow is smaller and less rusty. Fox Sparrow is largest of the streaked sparrows.
Fox_Sparrow.Best Ways to Identify: Large size, heavy reddish streaking, and vigorous leaf-scratching behavior.

Franklins_Gull.Description: Medium gull with black hood in summer, partial hood in winter. Red bill, red legs. Gray back, white underparts. White eye crescents. Black wingtips with white spots. About 14.5 inches. Rosy flush on breast in breeding.
Franklins_Gull.Behavior: Follows farm equipment to catch insects. Breeds in large colonies on prairie marshes. Migrates in spectacular flocks. Plunge-dives for fish occasionally.
Franklins_Gull.Habitat: Prairie marshes for breeding; migrates through Great Plains. Winters on Pacific coast of South America. Rare on East Coast and Gulf Coast in fall.
Franklins_Gull.Similar Looking Birds: Laughing Gull has longer wings with more black and no white in wingtips in flight. Bonaparte's Gull is smaller. Franklin's hood is more complete in summer.
Franklins_Gull.Best Ways to Identify: Black hood with white eye crescents. Red bill and legs. White spots in black wingtips. Prairie migrant following plows. Smaller and rounder than Laughing Gull.

Fulvous_Whistling-Duck.Description: Tawny-buff duck with dark brown back, white flank streaks, and white rump band. Long dark legs trailing in flight. Upright posture. About 20 inches. Whistling calls in flight. No wing patch.
Fulvous_Whistling-Duck.Behavior: Wades and dives for seeds and aquatic plants in shallow water. Highly nocturnal. Forms flocks, often with other whistling ducks. Perches readily in trees.
Fulvous_Whistling-Duck.Habitat: Freshwater marshes, flooded rice fields, and shallow lakes in southern Texas, Louisiana, California, and Florida. Widespread in tropics. Uncommon and local.
Fulvous_Whistling-Duck.Similar Looking Birds: Black-bellied Whistling-Duck has black belly, orange bill, and white wing patch. Fulvous is uniformly tawny with no wing patch.
Fulvous_Whistling-Duck.Best Ways to Identify: Uniform tawny-buff plumage with white flank streaks and white rump band. No wing patch in flight. Trailing legs. Whistling calls. Southern U.S. marshes.

Gadwall.Description: Medium dabbling duck. Male has intricate gray-brown vermiculated pattern with black rump; female resembles female Mallard.
Gadwall.Behavior: Dabbles in shallow water for aquatic vegetation. Often found with other diving ducks.
Gadwall.Habitat: Freshwater marshes, ponds, and lakes across North America.
Gadwall.Similar Looking Birds: Female similar to female Mallard but slimmer with orange-sided bill and white speculum.
Gadwall.Best Ways to Identify: Male's gray-brown body with black rump and white speculum patch in wing.

Gambels_Quail.Description: Plump quail with bold black-and-white face pattern, chestnut flanks, and teardrop-shaped black head plume.
Gambels_Quail.Behavior: Runs rapidly on the ground in coveys. Rarely flies, preferring to run from danger.
Gambels_Quail.Habitat: Desert scrub and brushy areas of the southwestern United States.
Gambels_Quail.Similar Looking Birds: California Quail has scaly belly; Gambel's has chestnut flanks and plain belly.
Gambels_Quail.Best Ways to Identify: Teardrop head plume, chestnut sides, and plain cream belly in dry desert habitat.

Garganey.Description: Small dabbling duck. Male has brown head with bold white supercilium, blue-gray wing patch. Female mottled brown with striped face. About 15 inches.
Garganey.Behavior: Feeds by dabbling in shallow water. Long-distance migrant wintering in Africa. Rare vagrant to North America from Eurasia.
Garganey.Habitat: Breeds in European and Asian freshwater wetlands. Winters in sub-Saharan Africa. Seen in North American marshes as a rare vagrant.
Garganey.Similar Looking Birds: Blue-winged Teal very similar. Female also resembles other small dabbling duck females.
Garganey.Best Ways to Identify: Male's bold white head stripe from eye to nape diagnostic. Female separated from Blue-winged Teal by face pattern and bill shape.

Gila_Woodpecker.Description: Medium woodpecker with barred black-and-white back. Male has red cap; both sexes have plain tan face and underparts.
Gila_Woodpecker.Behavior: Excavates nest cavities in saguaro cacti. Eats cactus fruit, insects, and small lizards.
Gila_Woodpecker.Habitat: Sonoran Desert with saguaro cacti in Arizona and northwestern Mexico.
Gila_Woodpecker.Similar Looking Birds: Similar to Golden-fronted Woodpecker but ranges don't overlap; Gila lacks yellow nape.
Gila_Woodpecker.Best Ways to Identify: Barred back, plain tan face, red cap on male, in saguaro cactus habitat.

Gilded_Flicker.Description: Large woodpecker with bright golden-yellow wing and tail linings, barred brown back, and spotted underparts.
Gilded_Flicker.Behavior: Excavates nest holes in saguaro cacti. Feeds on ants and other ground insects.
Gilded_Flicker.Habitat: Sonoran Desert with saguaro cacti in Arizona and California.
Gilded_Flicker.Similar Looking Birds: Northern Flicker overlaps but has red or yellow shaft color; Gilded has yellow only.
Gilded_Flicker.Best Ways to Identify: Yellow wing linings, spotted breast, red mustache stripe on male, saguaro desert.

Glaucous-winged_Gull.Description: Large gull with gray wingtips matching mantle color, pink bill, and pale eye. Wingtips are gray not black.
Glaucous-winged_Gull.Behavior: Omnivorous scavenger along Pacific coast. Nests colonially on rocky islands.
Glaucous-winged_Gull.Habitat: Pacific Northwest coast from Alaska to California.
Glaucous-winged_Gull.Similar Looking Birds: Western Gull has dark gray back and black wingtips; Glaucous-winged has pale gray wingtips.
Glaucous-winged_Gull.Best Ways to Identify: Gray wingtips matching mantle color on the Pacific coast — unique among large gulls.

Glaucous_Gull.Description: Very large pale gull with white wingtips, pale gray mantle, and pink bill with yellow tip. No black in wings.
Glaucous_Gull.Behavior: Scavenges along coastlines and at landfills. Aggressive and dominant over other gulls.
Glaucous_Gull.Habitat: Arctic coasts in breeding season; winters on coasts and large lakes.
Glaucous_Gull.Similar Looking Birds: Iceland Gull is smaller; Herring Gull has black wingtips. Glaucous has all-white wingtips.
Glaucous_Gull.Best Ways to Identify: Largest pale gull with completely white wingtips and massive pink bill.

Glossy_Ibis.Description: Medium wading ibis, dark chestnut and glossy green-purple plumage, downturned bill, no facial skin in non-breeding. About 23 inches.
Glossy_Ibis.Behavior: Forages in marshes and rice fields. Expanding breeding range northward along Atlantic coast. Flocks in migration.
Glossy_Ibis.Habitat: Coastal and inland wetlands. Breeds Atlantic coast marshes; expanding range northward. Winters in Gulf Coast.
Glossy_Ibis.Similar Looking Birds: White-faced Ibis very similar. Glossy Ibis lacks white feathering bordering facial skin.
Glossy_Ibis.Best Ways to Identify: Dark chestnut-green ibis without white face feather border. Compare to White-faced Ibis. Atlantic coast species.

Golden-cheeked_Warbler.Description: Male has black crown and back, bright yellow cheeks and forehead, black eye line, black throat, and white underparts with black streaks. Female is duller with olive-green back. About 4.75 inches. Endangered species.
Golden-cheeked_Warbler.Behavior: Forages in Ashe juniper and oaks, gleaning insects from bark. Males sing a distinctive buzzy song. Nests made of juniper bark strips. Very site-faithful.
Golden-cheeked_Warbler.Habitat: Ashe juniper and oak woodlands on the Edwards Plateau of central Texas — the only place this species breeds. Winters in pine-oak highlands of Central America.
Golden-cheeked_Warbler.Similar Looking Birds: Black-throated Green Warbler has green back, yellow-green cheeks. Townsend's Warbler has yellow face with dark cheek. Golden-cheeked is endemic to Texas.
Golden-cheeked_Warbler.Best Ways to Identify: Male's combination of black crown, yellow cheeks, and black eye line is unique. Only in central Texas cedar-oak hills during breeding. Buzzy, ascending song.

Golden-crowned_Kinglet.Description: Tiny bird with olive-green plumage, white eyebrow, and brilliant golden-orange crown patch.
Golden-crowned_Kinglet.Behavior: Constantly flicks wings while foraging in coniferous foliage for tiny insects and eggs.
Golden-crowned_Kinglet.Habitat: Coniferous forests; breeds in boreal and mountain forests, winters widely.
Golden-crowned_Kinglet.Similar Looking Birds: Ruby-crowned Kinglet has bold white eye-ring and red crown; Golden-crowned has striped face.
Golden-crowned_Kinglet.Best Ways to Identify: Striped black-and-white head with gold-orange crown; constant wing-flicking.

Golden-crowned_Sparrow.Description: Large sparrow with bold yellow patch on forehead bordered by black stripes. Brownish body.
Golden-crowned_Sparrow.Behavior: Scratches on the ground for seeds and berries. Forms flocks with White-crowned Sparrows.
Golden-crowned_Sparrow.Habitat: Breeds in subalpine shrubs; winters in chaparral and brushy areas of Pacific coast.
Golden-crowned_Sparrow.Similar Looking Birds: White-crowned Sparrow has white crown stripes; Golden-crowned has a yellow forehead patch.
Golden-crowned_Sparrow.Best Ways to Identify: Yellow forehead patch with black border, large size, Pacific coast in winter.

Golden-crowned_Warbler.Description: Small warbler, olive-green above, yellow below, golden-yellow crown stripe bordered by black. About 5 inches.
Golden-crowned_Warbler.Behavior: Forages low in forest understory. Rare vagrant to Texas from Mexico and Central America.
Golden-crowned_Warbler.Habitat: Forest understory of Mexico and Central America. Rare vagrant to southern Texas.
Golden-crowned_Warbler.Similar Looking Birds: Rufous-capped Warbler has rufous cap. Nashville Warbler yellow below without crown stripe.
Golden-crowned_Warbler.Best Ways to Identify: Golden-yellow crown stripe bordered by black stripes. Olive above, yellow below. Rare Texas vagrant.

Golden-fronted_Woodpecker.Description: Medium woodpecker with barred black-and-white back. Male has yellow-orange nape and red cap; female lacks red.
Golden-fronted_Woodpecker.Behavior: Forages on cactus, trees, and ground for insects, acorns, and cactus fruit.
Golden-fronted_Woodpecker.Habitat: Dry woodlands and mesquite brush in Texas and Oklahoma.
Golden-fronted_Woodpecker.Similar Looking Birds: Gila Woodpecker has plain face with no yellow nape. Red-bellied has red extending to forehead.
Golden-fronted_Woodpecker.Best Ways to Identify: Yellow nape, barred back, in Texas woodlands — combination unique to this species.

Golden-winged_Warbler.Description: Distinctive warbler with golden wing patch, gray body, and bold black-and-white head pattern.
Golden-winged_Warbler.Behavior: Forages in shrubby forest edges, probing dead leaves and bark for insects.
Golden-winged_Warbler.Habitat: Breeding in early successional habitats in northeastern and Appalachian regions.
Golden-winged_Warbler.Similar Looking Birds: Blue-winged Warbler has white wing bars and yellow body; hybrids are common.
Golden-winged_Warbler.Best Ways to Identify: Gray body, golden wing patch, black throat, and bold black mask.

Golden_Eagle.Description: Large dark eagle with golden-brown nape and upper wing coverts. Long tail with narrow bands.
Golden_Eagle.Behavior: Hunts rabbits, ground squirrels, and other mammals. Soars on flat wings.
Golden_Eagle.Habitat: Open and mountainous terrain across western North America; uncommon in east.
Golden_Eagle.Similar Looking Birds: Immature Bald Eagle has white mottling; Golden Eagle shows golden nape and uniform dark wings.
Golden_Eagle.Best Ways to Identify: Golden nape, dark brown body, long banded tail, and soaring flat-winged profile.

Golden_Pheasant.Description: Large pheasant. Male spectacular with golden crown, orange ruff, red underparts, long barred tail. About 40 inches.
Golden_Pheasant.Behavior: Forages in dense woodland. Small introduced populations in British Columbia and possibly elsewhere. Shy despite bright colors.
Golden_Pheasant.Habitat: Dense woodland and scrub. Small introduced populations in parts of North America. Native to China.
Golden_Pheasant.Similar Looking Birds: No other bird approaches male Golden Pheasant's combination of gold, orange, and red. Unmistakable.
Golden_Pheasant.Best Ways to Identify: Male unmistakable with golden crown and red underparts. Brilliantly colorful. Introduced North American populations.

Graces_Warbler.Description: Small warbler, gray above, yellow throat and breast, white belly, two white wing bars. About 5 inches.
Graces_Warbler.Behavior: Forages high in pine canopy. Gleans insects from pine needles. Mountain pine forest specialist.
Graces_Warbler.Habitat: Yellow pine forests in mountains of Arizona, New Mexico, and Mexico.
Graces_Warbler.Similar Looking Birds: Yellow-throated Warbler has black-and-white face, different habitat. Virginia's Warbler lacks yellow throat.
Graces_Warbler.Best Ways to Identify: Gray above, yellow throat and breast, white belly. Ponderosa pine forest in Arizona mountains.

Grasshopper_Sparrow.Description: Small flat-headed sparrow with buffy orange wash on face and breast, streaked back, and short tail.
Grasshopper_Sparrow.Behavior: Sings a high insect-like buzz. Walks or runs through grass rather than flushing.
Grasshopper_Sparrow.Habitat: Grasslands, meadows, and hay fields across North America.
Grasshopper_Sparrow.Similar Looking Birds: Henslow's Sparrow has larger head and olive nape; Grasshopper has orange face.
Grasshopper_Sparrow.Best Ways to Identify: Flat-headed appearance, orange-buff face, insect-like buzzy song in grasslands.

Gray-backed_Tern.Description: Medium tern. Gray back, black cap with white forehead, white underparts, forked tail. Similar to Bridled Tern. About 14 inches.
Gray-backed_Tern.Behavior: Picks fish from ocean surface. Breeds on Hawaiian and Pacific island atolls. Forages over warm tropical waters.
Gray-backed_Tern.Habitat: Tropical Pacific islands and atolls. Breeds in Hawaii (Midway Atoll) and other central Pacific islands.
Gray-backed_Tern.Similar Looking Birds: Bridled Tern has darker back and different head pattern. Gray-backed paler gray.
Gray-backed_Tern.Best Ways to Identify: Pale gray back with black cap and white forehead. White collar separating cap from back. Tropical Pacific species.

Gray-breasted_Martin.Description: Large swallow, glossy blue above, gray throat and breast, white belly. No purple gloss of Purple Martin. About 7 inches.
Gray-breasted_Martin.Behavior: Colonial nester in gourds and buildings in Latin America. Rare vagrant to southern Texas.
Gray-breasted_Martin.Habitat: Open areas, towns, and forest edges from Mexico to Argentina. Rare vagrant to southern Texas.
Gray-breasted_Martin.Similar Looking Birds: Purple Martin female more streaked below. Female distinction complex. Check breast pattern carefully.
Gray-breasted_Martin.Best Ways to Identify: Gray throat and breast contrasting with white belly. Blue gloss above. Larger than Bank Swallow. Rare Texas vagrant.

Gray-cheeked_Thrush.Description: Olive-brown thrush with spotted breast, gray cheeks, and faint eye ring. Very plain-faced.
Gray-cheeked_Thrush.Behavior: Forages quietly on the ground for insects and berries during migration.
Gray-cheeked_Thrush.Habitat: Breeds in boreal forests; migrates through eastern North America.
Gray-cheeked_Thrush.Similar Looking Birds: Swainson's Thrush has buffy eye ring and cheek; Veery is more rusty; Hermit has rufous tail.
Gray-cheeked_Thrush.Best Ways to Identify: Plain gray-cheeked face with no distinct eye ring — subtler look than other Catharus thrushes.

Gray-collared_Becard.Description: Medium flycatcher-like bird, male gray with black cap and gray collar, female brown with pale underparts. About 6 inches.
Gray-collared_Becard.Behavior: Gleans insects from forest canopy. Very rare vagrant to southern Arizona from Mexico.
Gray-collared_Becard.Habitat: Pine-oak forest of Mexico and Central America. Very rare vagrant to mountain canyons of southeastern Arizona.
Gray-collared_Becard.Similar Looking Birds: Rose-throated Becard has rose-pink throat on male. Gray-collared has gray collar.
Gray-collared_Becard.Best Ways to Identify: Male: gray with black cap, gray collar. No pink on throat. Very rare Arizona vagrant from Mexican mountains.

Gray-crowned_Rosy-Finch.Description: Dark brown finch with gray crown, pink-washed wings and belly, and black forehead.
Gray-crowned_Rosy-Finch.Behavior: Forages on snowfields for wind-blown seeds and insects. Forms large winter flocks.
Gray-crowned_Rosy-Finch.Habitat: High mountain summits and alpine tundra; descends to lower elevations in winter.
Gray-crowned_Rosy-Finch.Similar Looking Birds: Black Rosy-Finch has black body; Brown-capped has brown crown without gray.
Gray-crowned_Rosy-Finch.Best Ways to Identify: Gray crown patch, pink-washed wings, dark brown body at high elevations.

Gray-crowned_Yellowthroat.Description: Medium warbler. Male has gray crown and face, broken black loral mask, bright yellow underparts. About 5 inches.
Gray-crowned_Yellowthroat.Behavior: Skulks in tall dense grass. Rare vagrant to extreme southern Texas from Mexico.
Gray-crowned_Yellowthroat.Habitat: Dense tall grass, weedy fields, and rank vegetation of Mexico. Rare vagrant to southern Texas.
Gray-crowned_Yellowthroat.Similar Looking Birds: Common Yellowthroat has solid black mask. Yellow-breasted Chat larger. Gray crown with broken mask.
Gray-crowned_Yellowthroat.Best Ways to Identify: Gray crown with broken black loral area. Bright yellow below. Rare Texas vagrant from Mexico.

Gray-faced_Petrel.Description: Large dark gadfly petrel with gray face and forehead. Dark brown overall with pale gray face patch. About 16 inches.
Gray-faced_Petrel.Behavior: Breeds on New Zealand islands; forages over Southern and South Pacific Oceans. Very rare vagrant to North America.
Gray-faced_Petrel.Habitat: Southern Pacific Ocean. Very rare vagrant to North American Pacific coast.
Gray-faced_Petrel.Similar Looking Birds: Other large dark Pterodroma petrels similar. Gray face patch distinguishes this species.
Gray-faced_Petrel.Best Ways to Identify: Gray face patch on otherwise dark brown petrel. Large gadfly petrel from Southern Pacific Ocean.

Gray-headed_(Purple)_Swamphen.Description: Large rail-like bird. Brilliant iridescent purple- blue body, red bill and frontal shield, white undertail coverts. About 18 inches.
Gray-headed_(Purple)_Swamphen.Behavior: Walks through marsh vegetation. Highly visible and bold. Established feral population in southern Florida from escaped cage birds.
Gray-headed_(Purple)_Swamphen.Habitat: Freshwater marshes with dense vegetation in Florida. Native to southern Asia. Feral breeding population established in South Florida.
Gray-headed_(Purple)_Swamphen.Similar Looking Birds: Purple Gallinule similar but smaller with yellow-green legs. Swamphen much larger.
Gray-headed_(Purple)_Swamphen.Best Ways to Identify: Very large size, brilliant purple-blue plumage, and red bill unmistakable. White undertail conspicuous when walking.

Gray-headed_Chickadee.Description: Medium chickadee with gray-brown cap (not black), dirty white cheeks, pale brownish sides. About 5.5 inches.
Gray-headed_Chickadee.Behavior: Inhabits dense boreal willow and alder thickets. One of least-known birds in North America. Rarely observed.
Gray-headed_Chickadee.Habitat: Dense willow and alder scrub along rivers in Arctic Alaska and Yukon. Very difficult to access habitat.
Gray-headed_Chickadee.Similar Looking Birds: Boreal Chickadee has chestnut sides and brown cap. Black-capped Chickadee has blacker cap and cleaner white cheeks.
Gray-headed_Chickadee.Best Ways to Identify: Dull brown-gray cap, dirty white cheeks, pale sides. Far northern willow scrub. Very rare and seldom observed.

Gray-hooded_Gull.Description: Medium gull. Breeding adult has pale gray hood, deep red bill and legs, gray back, white underparts. About 16 inches.
Gray-hooded_Gull.Behavior: Found on coasts and inland waters. Rare vagrant to eastern North America from South America and Africa.
Gray-hooded_Gull.Habitat: Coastal and inland waters of South America and Africa. Rare vagrant to Atlantic coast of North America.
Gray-hooded_Gull.Similar Looking Birds: Laughing Gull similar size. Gray-hooded has pale gray (not black) hood.
Gray-hooded_Gull.Best Ways to Identify: Pale gray hood (not dark) with red bill and legs. Rare vagrant from South America or Africa.

Gray-streaked_Flycatcher.Description: Small flycatcher, gray-brown above, white below with distinct gray-brown streaking on breast. About 5.5 inches.
Gray-streaked_Flycatcher.Behavior: Sallies from perch to catch flying insects. Rare vagrant to western Alaska from East Asia.
Gray-streaked_Flycatcher.Habitat: Forest edges and woodland in East Asia. Rare vagrant to western Alaska and Aleutian Islands.
Gray-streaked_Flycatcher.Similar Looking Birds: Asian Brown Flycatcher lacks streaking below. Dark-sided Flycatcher has dark sides without streaking.
Gray-streaked_Flycatcher.Best Ways to Identify: Distinct streaking on white underparts. Gray-brown above. Rare Alaska vagrant from East Asia.

Gray-tailed_Tattler.Description: Medium sandpiper. Uniform gray above, white below with gray breast. Barred underparts in breeding. Yellow legs. Short nasal groove. About 10 inches.
Gray-tailed_Tattler.Behavior: Forages on rocky shorelines bobbing tail. Rare vagrant to Pacific coast from Asian breeding grounds.
Gray-tailed_Tattler.Habitat: Breeds in Siberian and Alaskan mountain streams. Winters on Pacific island coasts. Rare vagrant to Pacific coast of North America.
Gray-tailed_Tattler.Similar Looking Birds: Wandering Tattler nearly identical. Gray-tailed has shorter nasal groove and different call.
Gray-tailed_Tattler.Best Ways to Identify: Nearly identical to Wandering Tattler. Shorter nasal groove (tricky field mark). Call different from Wandering Tattler.

Gray_Bunting.Description: Medium bunting. Male slaty gray throughout. Female streaked brown with rusty rump. About 6.5 inches.
Gray_Bunting.Behavior: Skulks in dense undergrowth. Rare vagrant to western Alaska and Aleutian Islands from Japan.
Gray_Bunting.Habitat: Dense forest undergrowth of Japan. Rare vagrant to western Alaska.
Gray_Bunting.Similar Looking Birds: No other all-gray bunting in range. Dark-eyed Junco has white outer tail feathers.
Gray_Bunting.Best Ways to Identify: Male all slaty gray. Female streaked brown with rusty rump. Rare Alaska vagrant from Japan.

Gray_Catbird.Description: Slate-gray bird with black cap and rusty undertail. Slender build with long tail.
Gray_Catbird.Behavior: Hides in dense thickets and mimics other birds. Named for mewing cat-like call.
Gray_Catbird.Habitat: Dense shrubs and thickets at forest edges across eastern North America.
Gray_Catbird.Similar Looking Birds: Northern Mockingbird is larger with white wing patches; Catbird is plain gray with rusty vent.
Gray_Catbird.Best Ways to Identify: Solid gray with black cap and rusty undertail coverts; mewing call.

Gray_Flycatcher.Description: Plain gray Empidonax with long bill, white eye ring, and distinctive downward tail dip.
Gray_Flycatcher.Behavior: Unique among Empidonax for slowly dipping tail downward rather than flicking it up.
Gray_Flycatcher.Habitat: Sagebrush and pinyon-juniper desert scrub in the Great Basin.
Gray_Flycatcher.Similar Looking Birds: Dusky Flycatcher very similar but shorter bill; Gray Flycatcher dips tail down distinctively.
Gray_Flycatcher.Best Ways to Identify: Slow downward tail dip — the key behavior distinguishing it from other Empidonax.

Gray_Francolin.Description: Medium-sized partridge. Brown and gray streaked plumage, buff face with chestnut-streaked throat outlined in black. About 14 inches.
Gray_Francolin.Behavior: Runs rather than flies when alarmed. Noisy with loud cackling calls. Forages for seeds, berries, and insects on ground. Introduced to Hawaii.
Gray_Francolin.Habitat: Dry grasslands, scrubland, and agricultural areas. Established on Hawaiian Islands, particularly on Lanai and Maui, after introduction.
Gray_Francolin.Similar Looking Birds: Black Francolin in same Hawaiian range. Gray Francolin paler overall.
Gray_Francolin.Best Ways to Identify: Buff-orange face with black-bordered throat. Streaked gray-brown plumage. Loud rattling call distinctive in Hawaiian dry grasslands.

Gray_Gull.Description: Medium gull. Uniform gray plumage with white head in breeding, dark tips on wings, yellow bill. About 18 inches.
Gray_Gull.Behavior: Breeds in Atacama Desert of South America; commutes to Pacific coast to feed on fish. Rare vagrant to California.
Gray_Gull.Habitat: Breeds in Atacama Desert, Chile/Peru. Forages along Pacific coast of South America. Rare vagrant to California.
Gray_Gull.Similar Looking Birds: Heermann's Gull similar gray coloring. Gray Gull paler with white head.
Gray_Gull.Best Ways to Identify: Uniform pale gray with white head. Breeding in Atacama Desert unique among gulls. Rare vagrant to California.

Gray_Hawk.Description: Small buteo, plain gray above and finely barred gray and white below. Two white tail bands. About 17 inches.
Gray_Hawk.Behavior: Hunts lizards in riparian forest. Regular summer resident in southeastern Arizona and southwestern New Mexico canyons.
Gray_Hawk.Habitat: Riparian cottonwood-willow forest in southeastern Arizona and southwestern New Mexico. Winters in Mexico.
Gray_Hawk.Similar Looking Birds: Broad-winged Hawk has brown streaking below. Gray Hawk all-gray with fine barring.
Gray_Hawk.Best Ways to Identify: Fine gray barring below, plain gray above. Two white tail bands. Riparian specialist in southeastern Arizona.

Gray_Heron.Description: Large gray heron, white head with black stripe and crest, yellow bill, gray body. About 38 inches.
Gray_Heron.Behavior: Stands motionless waiting for fish. Common across Europe and Asia. Rare vagrant to Atlantic coast and Alaska.
Gray_Heron.Habitat: Wetlands, rivers, and coasts of Europe and Asia. Rare vagrant to Atlantic coast and Alaska.
Gray_Heron.Similar Looking Birds: Great Blue Heron very similar. Gray Heron has white neck without rusty tones.
Gray_Heron.Best Ways to Identify: White neck without rusty color; black-and-white head. Old World counterpart to Great Blue Heron. Rare vagrant.

Gray_Kingbird.Description: Large gray-and-white flycatcher with large heavy bill and notched gray tail. No yellow in plumage.
Gray_Kingbird.Behavior: Perches conspicuously and sallies after large insects; also eats lizards and small fruit.
Gray_Kingbird.Habitat: Coastal Florida, Caribbean islands, and mangroves; rare vagrant northward.
Gray_Kingbird.Similar Looking Birds: Eastern Kingbird has black-and-white pattern with white tail tip; Gray Kingbird is all gray.
Gray_Kingbird.Best Ways to Identify: All-gray and white with large bill, notched tail, and coastal Florida habitat.

Gray_Nightjar.Description: Medium nightjar. Gray-brown cryptic plumage with intricate patterning. White spots in wings and tail. About 11 inches.
Gray_Nightjar.Behavior: Nocturnal insect catcher. Roosts on forest floor or branches during day. Rare vagrant to western Alaska from East Asia.
Gray_Nightjar.Habitat: Breeds in South and East Asian forests. Winters in Southeast Asia. Very rare vagrant to western Aleutian Islands and Alaska.
Gray_Nightjar.Similar Looking Birds: Other nightjars similar. Gray Nightjar has distinctive call and Asian origin distinguishes it.
Gray_Nightjar.Best Ways to Identify: Large size among nightjars with distinctive gray-brown plumage. Very rare vagrant in western Alaska. Wing and tail spots visible in flight.

Gray_Partridge.Description: Rotund ground bird with orange-buff face, gray breast, and chestnut bars on flanks. Short rufous tail.
Gray_Partridge.Behavior: Coveys walk through agricultural fields foraging for seeds and grain.
Gray_Partridge.Habitat: Open farmland, grasslands, and grain fields of the northern United States and Canada.
Gray_Partridge.Similar Looking Birds: Chukar has bold black-and-white face stripes; Gray Partridge has plain orange face.
Gray_Partridge.Best Ways to Identify: Orange face, gray breast with horseshoe mark on belly, chestnut flank bars in farmland.

Gray_Silky-flycatcher.Description: Medium sleek bird with long tail. Male gray with yellow undertail coverts and crest. About 8 inches.
Gray_Silky-flycatcher.Behavior: Perches prominently in fruiting trees like mistletoe. Very rare vagrant to southwestern United States from Mexico.
Gray_Silky-flycatcher.Habitat: Pine-oak forests and high-elevation scrub in Mexico. Very rare vagrant to California, Arizona, and Texas.
Gray_Silky-flycatcher.Similar Looking Birds: Phainopepla similar silky-flycatcher but all black or dark gray with red eye and white wing patch.
Gray_Silky-flycatcher.Best Ways to Identify: Gray plumage with yellow undertail coverts, long tail, upright crest. Rare vagrant from Mexico. Phainopepla relative.

Gray_Thrasher.Description: Medium thrasher, gray above, white below with bold dark spots, long decurved bill, yellow eye. About 11 inches.
Gray_Thrasher.Behavior: Forages on ground in desert scrub. Rare vagrant to California from Baja California peninsula.
Gray_Thrasher.Habitat: Desert scrub of Baja California peninsula. Very rare vagrant to southern California.
Gray_Thrasher.Similar Looking Birds: Curve-billed Thrasher more brownish. Le Conte's Thrasher plain without spots. Bold spots with gray above.
Gray_Thrasher.Best Ways to Identify: Gray above with bold dark spots below. Long decurved bill, yellow eye. Very rare California vagrant from Baja.

Gray_Vireo.Description: Plain gray vireo with single thin white wing bar, faint eye ring, and long tail frequently pumped.
Gray_Vireo.Behavior: Actively pumps tail while foraging in dense shrubs. Song repeated frequently.
Gray_Vireo.Habitat: Arid scrub, pinyon-juniper, and chaparral in the southwestern United States.
Gray_Vireo.Similar Looking Birds: Plumbeous Vireo has two bold wing bars and white spectacles; Gray Vireo is plainer.
Gray_Vireo.Best Ways to Identify: Plain gray with single wing bar, tail pumping, and arid southwestern habitat.

Gray_Wagtail.Description: Slender wagtail, gray above, yellow rump and undertail, white supercilium. Very long tail. About 7 inches.
Gray_Wagtail.Behavior: Wagtail behavior with especially long tail constantly wagging. Frequents rocky streams. Rare vagrant to western Alaska.
Gray_Wagtail.Habitat: Fast-flowing rocky streams in Europe and Asia. Rare vagrant to western Alaska and Aleutians.
Gray_Wagtail.Similar Looking Birds: Eastern Yellow Wagtail yellow throughout below. White Wagtail black-and-white pattern.
Gray_Wagtail.Best Ways to Identify: Gray back with yellow rump and undertail. Extremely long tail. Rocky stream association. Rare Alaska vagrant.

Graylag_Goose.Description: A large, bulky grey-brown goose with a heavy orange-pink bill and pale grey head and neck. Adults weigh 2.5-4 kg.
Graylag_Goose.Behavior: Grazes on grass, roots, and grains. Highly social, flying in V-formations. Forms strong pair bonds and is very vocal.
Graylag_Goose.Habitat: Breeds near lakes, marshes, and rivers across Europe and Asia. Winters in open farmland and estuaries.
Graylag_Goose.Similar Looking Birds: Often confused with other grey geese like Bean Goose and Pink-footed Goose, which share similar plumage patterns.
Graylag_Goose.Best Ways to Identify: Look for the distinctive large orange-pink bill, pale grey forewing in flight, and pink legs to distinguish from similar species.

Great-tailed_Grackle.Description: Large grackle. Male iridescent purple-black with huge keel-shaped tail, yellow eye. Female brown. About 18 inches (male).
Great-tailed_Grackle.Behavior: Extremely common and expanding range. Roosts in huge numbers in urban areas. Very loud, varied vocalizations.
Great-tailed_Grackle.Habitat: Agricultural areas, urban and suburban areas, marshes across the southwest and increasingly spreading eastward and northward.
Great-tailed_Grackle.Similar Looking Birds: Boat-tailed Grackle very similar. Great-tailed has yellow eye (in both sexes).
Great-tailed_Grackle.Best Ways to Identify: Yellow eye distinctive. Huge keel-shaped tail. Expanding inland urban and agricultural range. Very noisy.

Great_Auk.Description: EXTINCT large flightless alcid. Black above, white below, large grooved bill, white facial patch in breeding. About 30 inches.
Great_Auk.Behavior: Swam expertly; dove for fish. Flightless. Hunted to extinction by 1844. Last pair killed June 3, 1844 in Iceland.
Great_Auk.Habitat: Rocky North Atlantic islands. Bred on Funk Island, Newfoundland, and other islands. Extinct since 1844.
Great_Auk.Similar Looking Birds: Razorbill is closest living relative but much smaller.
Great_Auk.Best Ways to Identify: Only known from museum specimens. Extinct since June 3, 1844. Large flightless alcid of North Atlantic.

Great_Black-backed_Gull.Description: Enormous gull with jet-black back and wings, white body, pink legs, and yellow bill with red spot.
Great_Black-backed_Gull.Behavior: Dominant scavenger that pirates food from other birds and eats almost anything.
Great_Black-backed_Gull.Habitat: Atlantic coast of North America; also Great Lakes in winter.
Great_Black-backed_Gull.Similar Looking Birds: Lesser Black-backed Gull has yellow legs and smaller size; Great Black-backed is massive.
Great_Black-backed_Gull.Best Ways to Identify: Largest gull in North America — jet-black back, massive size, and pink legs.

Great_Black_Hawk.Description: Large all-black hawk with one broad white tail band. Yellow cere and legs. About 22 inches.
Great_Black_Hawk.Behavior: Hunts reptiles and amphibians near water. Rare vagrant to southern Texas from Mexico and Central America.
Great_Black_Hawk.Habitat: Riparian forest near water of Mexico and Central America. Rare vagrant to southern Texas.
Great_Black_Hawk.Similar Looking Birds: Common Black Hawk similar but has two tail bands. Great Black Hawk has one wide tail band.
Great_Black_Hawk.Best Ways to Identify: Large all-black hawk with single broad white tail band. Yellow cere. Larger than Common Black Hawk.

Great_Blue_Heron.Description: Very large blue-gray heron with white face, black plumes above eye, and rusty thighs.
Great_Blue_Heron.Behavior: Stands motionless in water waiting to spear fish and frogs with long bill.
Great_Blue_Heron.Habitat: Almost any wetland — marshes, ponds, rivers, and coasts across North America.
Great_Blue_Heron.Similar Looking Birds: Little Blue Heron is much smaller; Sandhill Crane flies with neck extended not folded.
Great_Blue_Heron.Best Ways to Identify: Largest heron — flies with neck folded in S-shape, blue-gray body, and massive wingspan.

Great_Cormorant.Description: Large cormorant, dark black-green plumage, white cheek patch, orange-yellow throat pouch. About 36 inches.
Great_Cormorant.Behavior: Large diving cormorant. Breeds in northeastern North America; winters on rocky Atlantic coasts and inland.
Great_Cormorant.Habitat: Atlantic coast rocky shores, harbors, and coastal freshwater. Winters south to mid-Atlantic coast.
Great_Cormorant.Similar Looking Birds: Double-crested Cormorant has orange throat without white cheek patch.
Great_Cormorant.Best Ways to Identify: Large size with white cheek patch and orange-yellow throat. Larger than Double-crested. Atlantic coast cormorant.

Great_Crested_Flycatcher.Description: Large flycatcher with bright yellow belly, rufous tail, gray breast, and brown crest.
Great_Crested_Flycatcher.Behavior: Nests in tree cavities; often incorporates shed snake skin into nest.
Great_Crested_Flycatcher.Habitat: Deciduous forests and forest edges across eastern North America.
Great_Crested_Flycatcher.Similar Looking Birds: Ash-throated Flycatcher is paler with less yellow; Brown-crested is larger but western.
Great_Crested_Flycatcher.Best Ways to Identify: Bright yellow belly, rufous tail, gray throat, crest, and loud wheep call.

Great_Crested_Tern.Description: Large tern. White with gray back, black crest, yellow bill. Large size and shaggy crest. About 18 inches.
Great_Crested_Tern.Behavior: Dives for fish. Breeds on tropical Pacific islands. Rare vagrant to Hawaii and occasionally Pacific coast.
Great_Crested_Tern.Habitat: Tropical Indian and Pacific ocean islands and coasts. Rare in Hawaii; extremely rare on mainland Pacific coast.
Great_Crested_Tern.Similar Looking Birds: Elegant Tern smaller. Royal Tern has orange bill. Great Crested has yellow bill.
Great_Crested_Tern.Best Ways to Identify: Large size with yellow bill and black shaggy crest. Gray back. Rare in Hawaii and Pacific coast.

Great_Egret.Description: Large all-white heron with yellow-orange bill, black legs and feet, and long white plumes in breeding.
Great_Egret.Behavior: Wades slowly in water to spear fish. Nests colonially in trees with other herons.
Great_Egret.Habitat: Wetlands, marshes, ponds, and coastal areas across North America.
Great_Egret.Similar Looking Birds: Snowy Egret has black bill and yellow feet; Great Egret has yellow bill and black feet.
Great_Egret.Best Ways to Identify: Large all-white with yellow-orange bill, black legs — no yellow feet like Snowy Egret.

Great_Frigatebird.Description: Large black frigatebird, male with red throat pouch, female with white throat and breast. Long forked tail. About 37 inches.
Great_Frigatebird.Behavior: Kleptoparasite like other frigatebirds. Breeds on Hawaiian Northwestern Islands; forages widely in Pacific.
Great_Frigatebird.Habitat: Tropical Pacific and Indian Oceans. Breeds on Hawaiian Northwestern Islands; forages in Hawaiian waters.
Great_Frigatebird.Similar Looking Birds: Magnificent Frigatebird nearly identical. Great Frigatebird female has red eye ring and white throat.
Great_Frigatebird.Best Ways to Identify: Female has red eye ring, white throat and breast. Male indistinguishable in field from Magnificent Frigatebird without range context.

Great_Gray_Owl.Description: Huge owl with enormous round facial disc, yellow eyes, and no ear tufts. Gray-brown mottled plumage.
Great_Gray_Owl.Behavior: Hunts voles by sound through deep snow, plunging feet-first to catch prey.
Great_Gray_Owl.Habitat: Dense boreal and mountain coniferous forests of the northern and western regions.
Great_Gray_Owl.Similar Looking Birds: Great Horned Owl has prominent ear tufts; Barred Owl is smaller with dark eyes.
Great_Gray_Owl.Best Ways to Identify: Largest owl by length — enormous facial disc, yellow eyes, and no ear tufts.

Great_Horned_Owl.Description: Large owl with prominent ear tufts, bright yellow eyes, white throat bib, and barred underparts.
Great_Horned_Owl.Behavior: Apex predator that hunts everything from mice to skunks to other raptors.
Great_Horned_Owl.Habitat: Almost every habitat across North America — forests, deserts, suburbs, and cities.
Great_Horned_Owl.Similar Looking Birds: Long-eared Owl has longer ear tufts closer together; Great Horned has wide-set tufts.
Great_Horned_Owl.Best Ways to Identify: Prominent wide-set ear tufts, yellow eyes, white throat bib, and deep hooting call.

Great_Kiskadee.Description: Large flycatcher with bold black-and-white striped head, yellow underparts, and rufous wings.
Great_Kiskadee.Behavior: Dives into water for fish like a kingfisher. Eats insects, fruit, lizards, and fish.
Great_Kiskadee.Habitat: Woodland edges, stream corridors, and parks in southern Texas.
Great_Kiskadee.Similar Looking Birds: Boat-billed Flycatcher similar but more restricted to tropics; range barely overlaps.
Great_Kiskadee.Best Ways to Identify: Striped head, bright yellow belly, rufous wings — loud kis-ka-dee call in southern Texas.

Great_Knot.Description: Large sandpiper. Breeding adult has chestnut-streaked back, heavily spotted breast. Non-breeding gray above and white below. About 11 inches.
Great_Knot.Behavior: Forages on mudflats for mollusks. Rare vagrant to Pacific coast from Asian wintering areas. Migrates in large flocks in Asia.
Great_Knot.Habitat: Breeds in Siberia. Winters on Australian and East Asian coasts. Rare vagrant to Pacific coast of North America.
Great_Knot.Similar Looking Birds: Red Knot similar but smaller. Great Knot larger with spotted breast in breeding.
Great_Knot.Best Ways to Identify: Larger than Red Knot with spotted breast in breeding plumage. Non-breeding gray back with streaked breast.

Great_Shearwater.Description: Large shearwater, brown back, black cap, white collar, white below with dark belly patch, pink bill with black tip. About 19 inches.
Great_Shearwater.Behavior: Breeds on Tristan da Cunha and Falkland Islands. Very common in North Atlantic in summer on migration.
Great_Shearwater.Habitat: North Atlantic Ocean in summer migration. Very common offshore Atlantic coast from spring through fall.
Great_Shearwater.Similar Looking Birds: Cory's Shearwater lacks dark cap. Sooty Shearwater darker without black cap and collar.
Great_Shearwater.Best Ways to Identify: Black cap with white collar, dark belly patch, pink bill. Common Atlantic shearwater. Summer migrant from South Atlantic.

Great_Skua.Description: Large powerful seabird. All dark brown with white wing flash, broad wings, short tail. Heavily built. About 22 inches.
Great_Skua.Behavior: Aggressively pirates food from other seabirds. Breeds in North Atlantic. Seen offshore during migration on Atlantic coast.
Great_Skua.Habitat: Breeds on North Atlantic islands (Iceland, Scotland, Norway). Pelagic outside breeding. Seen offshore on Atlantic coast.
Great_Skua.Similar Looking Birds: South Polar Skua similar. Great Skua browner and heavier built.
Great_Skua.Best Ways to Identify: Very large dark seabird with white wing flash. Heavy-bodied compared to jaegers. Aggressive food pirating behavior.

Great_Spotted_Woodpecker.Description: Medium woodpecker, black and white with large white shoulder patches, red nape on male, red undertail. About 9 inches.
Great_Spotted_Woodpecker.Behavior: Common woodpecker across Europe and Asia. Rare vagrant to Alaska. Drums loudly on trees.
Great_Spotted_Woodpecker.Habitat: Woodland and forest of Europe and Asia. Rare vagrant to western Alaska.
Great_Spotted_Woodpecker.Similar Looking Birds: Hairy and Downy Woodpeckers similar but lack large shoulder patches and red undertail.
Great_Spotted_Woodpecker.Best Ways to Identify: Large white shoulder patches, red undertail coverts. Common European species, rare Alaska vagrant.

Great_Tit.Description: Medium tit, black head with white cheeks, green back, yellow underparts with black stripe. About 5.5 inches.
Great_Tit.Behavior: Bold and intelligent, solves complex problems. Regular feeder visitor. Very rare vagrant to Alaska from Asia.
Great_Tit.Habitat: Woodland, gardens, and parks across Europe and Asia. Very rare vagrant to western Alaska.
Great_Tit.Similar Looking Birds: Black-capped Chickadee has different pattern. Tufted Titmouse lacks yellow underparts. No similar bird in Alaska.
Great_Tit.Best Ways to Identify: Black head, white cheeks, yellow underparts with black stripe. Bold and active. Very rare Alaska vagrant.

Great_White_Pelican.Description: Very large pelican, white with black flight feathers, pink bill pouch, yellow facial skin. About 63 inches.
Great_White_Pelican.Behavior: Cooperative feeder, herds fish in groups. Soars on thermals. Very rare vagrant to North America, usually escaped birds.
Great_White_Pelican.Habitat: Large lakes and wetlands of Europe, Asia, and Africa. Extremely rare vagrant to North America.
Great_White_Pelican.Similar Looking Birds: American White Pelican very similar. Yellow pouch vs. orange in American White. Essentially identical in field.
Great_White_Pelican.Best Ways to Identify: Enormous white pelican with pink bill and yellow facial skin. Very rare; likely escaped from captivity.

Greater_Amakihi.Description: Medium Hawaiian honeycreeper, olive-green throughout, larger size than other amakihi, straight bill. About 6 inches.
Greater_Amakihi.Behavior: Fed on insects in native forest. Extinct since approximately 1901 from the Big Island of Hawaii.
Greater_Amakihi.Habitat: Native forests of Big Island. Extinct due to deforestation and introduced avian diseases.
Greater_Amakihi.Similar Looking Birds: Other amakihi smaller. Hawaii Creeper similar habits. No similar large olive honeycreeper survives.
Greater_Amakihi.Best Ways to Identify: Extinct. Large olive-green honeycreeper with straight bill. Big Island. Last recorded approximately 1901.

Greater_Koa-Finch.Description: Large Hawaiian honeycreeper, male with orange head and breast, olive-green back, massive koa-seed bill. About 8 inches.
Greater_Koa-Finch.Behavior: Fed on hard koa pods. Extinct since approximately 1896 on Big Island.
Greater_Koa-Finch.Habitat: Native koa forests of the Big Island of Hawaii. Extinct due to deforestation.
Greater_Koa-Finch.Similar Looking Birds: Lesser Koa-Finch smaller. Palila has yellow head. No similar birds survive.
Greater_Koa-Finch.Best Ways to Identify: Extinct species. Largest koa-finch. Orange head, massive bill. No longer exists in Hawaiian koa forest.

Greater_Necklaced_Laughingthrush.Description: Large thrush-like bird, brown above, white below with bold black necklace across breast. Black facial markings. About 11 inches.
Greater_Necklaced_Laughingthrush.Behavior: Forages in noisy flocks through dense undergrowth. Introduced to Hawaii. Loud, raucous calls.
Greater_Necklaced_Laughingthrush.Habitat: Dense forest undergrowth. Introduced to Oahu, Hawaii. Native to forests of India and Southeast Asia.
Greater_Necklaced_Laughingthrush.Similar Looking Birds: Lesser Necklaced Laughingthrush similar but smaller. No other large thrush-like bird in Hawaiian forest undergrowth.
Greater_Necklaced_Laughingthrush.Best Ways to Identify: Bold black necklace across white breast. Brown above. Large size. Noisy flocks in Oahu forest.

Greater_Pewee.Description: Large pewee, olive-gray above, pale below with darker sides. Prominent crest. Orange-yellow lower mandible. About 8 inches.
Greater_Pewee.Behavior: Sallies from high exposed perch; loud whistle song. Summer resident in mountain pine forest of southeastern Arizona.
Greater_Pewee.Habitat: Pine and pine-oak forest in mountain ranges of southeastern Arizona and southwestern New Mexico. Summer resident.
Greater_Pewee.Similar Looking Birds: Eastern and Western Wood-Pewees smaller without crest. Greater Pewee's size and crest distinct.
Greater_Pewee.Best Ways to Identify: Large pewee with prominent crest, orange lower mandible. Loud "Jose Maria" whistle. Southeastern Arizona mountain pine forest.

Greater_Prairie-Chicken.Description: Stocky grouse with heavily barred brown plumage, orange eye combs, and pinnate feathers on neck.
Greater_Prairie-Chicken.Behavior: Males gather on leks to perform elaborate booming displays with inflated orange neck sacs.
Greater_Prairie-Chicken.Habitat: Tallgrass prairie remnants in the central United States.
Greater_Prairie-Chicken.Similar Looking Birds: Lesser Prairie-Chicken is smaller and paler; Sharp-tailed Grouse has pointed tail.
Greater_Prairie-Chicken.Best Ways to Identify: Booming lek displays, orange neck sacs, and pinnate neck feathers in tallgrass prairie.

Greater_Roadrunner.Description: Large ground-dwelling cuckoo with long tail, streaked brown plumage, and blue-red eye patch.
Greater_Roadrunner.Behavior: Runs rapidly on the ground to catch lizards, snakes, and large insects.
Greater_Roadrunner.Habitat: Desert scrub, chaparral, and dry open areas of the southwestern United States.
Greater_Roadrunner.Similar Looking Birds: Lesser Roadrunner is smaller and restricted to Mexico; Greater Roadrunner is larger.
Greater_Roadrunner.Best Ways to Identify: Long tail, runs on ground, blue-red eye patch, and streaked brown plumage.

Greater_Sand-Plover.Description: Medium plover with heavy bill. Breeding adult has rufous breast band, gray-brown back. Similar to Siberian Sand-Plover but larger. About 9 inches.
Greater_Sand-Plover.Behavior: Forages on mudflats and sandy beaches. Rare vagrant to Pacific coast from Asian breeding grounds.
Greater_Sand-Plover.Habitat: Breeds in central Asian steppes and deserts. Winters on Asian and African coasts. Rare vagrant to Pacific coast of North America.
Greater_Sand-Plover.Similar Looking Birds: Siberian Sand-Plover smaller with thinner bill.
Greater_Sand-Plover.Best Ways to Identify: Larger size and heavier bill than Siberian Sand- Plover. Rufous breast band in breeding. Rare vagrant on Pacific coast.

Greater_Scaup.Description: Diving duck with rounded head, blue-gray bill, and black-and-white body on males. Greenish gloss on head.
Greater_Scaup.Behavior: Dives deeply for mollusks, crustaceans, and aquatic plants in open water.
Greater_Scaup.Habitat: Coastal bays and large lakes; breeds in Arctic and boreal regions.
Greater_Scaup.Similar Looking Birds: Lesser Scaup has peaked head and purple gloss; Greater has rounder head and green gloss.
Greater_Scaup.Best Ways to Identify: Rounded head with green gloss, and white wing stripe extends further into primaries.

Greater_White-fronted_Goose.Description: Medium goose with orange bill, white forehead patch, pinkish-orange legs, and black belly bars.
Greater_White-fronted_Goose.Behavior: Grazes on grasses and grains in flocks. Loud laughing call given in flight.
Greater_White-fronted_Goose.Habitat: Breeds in Arctic tundra; winters in central and western North America.
Greater_White-fronted_Goose.Similar Looking Birds: Canada Goose is larger with black neck; White-fronted has orange bill and black belly blotches.
Greater_White-fronted_Goose.Best Ways to Identify: White forehead patch, orange bill, and black bars on belly — laughing call in flight.

Greater_Yellowlegs.Description: Large shorebird with bright yellow legs, long gray-and-white barred bill, and white-spotted upperparts.
Greater_Yellowlegs.Behavior: Wades actively in water chasing fish and invertebrates. Loud three-note call.
Greater_Yellowlegs.Habitat: Wetlands, mudflats, and marshes across North America during migration.
Greater_Yellowlegs.Similar Looking Birds: Lesser Yellowlegs is smaller with shorter bill and softer two-note call.
Greater_Yellowlegs.Best Ways to Identify: Large size, yellow legs, long upturned bill, and loud three-note tu-tu-tu call.

Green-breasted_Mango.Description: Large hummingbird. Male dark metallic green with black throat and purple-bordered tail. Female green above, white below with dark central stripe. About 4.5 inches.
Green-breasted_Mango.Behavior: Feeds on nectar from large flowers. Flies with direct, fast flight. Rare vagrant to Texas and southern US from Mexico and Central America.
Green-breasted_Mango.Habitat: Tropical forest edges, gardens, and plantations in Mexico and Central America. Rare visitor to Texas and occasionally other southern states.
Green-breasted_Mango.Similar Looking Birds: Black-throated Mango in Caribbean. Female similar to other large female hummingbirds.
Green-breasted_Mango.Best Ways to Identify: Male's entirely green body with black throat and dark purple-edged tail. Female's white underparts with bold dark central stripe.

Green-tailed_Towhee.Description: Ground-dwelling sparrow with olive-green tail and wings, gray body, white throat, and rufous cap.
Green-tailed_Towhee.Behavior: Scratches vigorously in leaf litter under dense shrubs. Rarely seen in open.
Green-tailed_Towhee.Habitat: Mountain shrublands and sagebrush of the western United States.
Green-tailed_Towhee.Similar Looking Birds: Spotted Towhee has rufous sides and spotted wings; Green-tailed is plain gray with green tail.
Green-tailed_Towhee.Best Ways to Identify: Rufous cap, green tail, white throat patch in mountain shrubland habitat.

Green-winged_Teal.Description: Smallest dabbling duck. Male has chestnut head with green ear patch; both sexes have green wing speculum.
Green-winged_Teal.Behavior: Feeds on seeds and invertebrates in shallow water. Forms large migrating flocks.
Green-winged_Teal.Habitat: Shallow marshes, ponds, and wetlands across North America.
Green-winged_Teal.Similar Looking Birds: Blue-winged Teal is slightly larger with blue forewing patch; Green-winged has green speculum.
Green-winged_Teal.Best Ways to Identify: Smallest dabbling duck — male's chestnut head with green stripe is distinctive.

Green_Heron.Description: Small stocky heron with dark green back, chestnut neck, orange-yellow legs, and dark cap.
Green_Heron.Behavior: Perches and waits motionlessly, sometimes using bait to lure fish to the surface.
Green_Heron.Habitat: Wooded wetlands, ponds, and stream edges across North America.
Green_Heron.Similar Looking Birds: Black-crowned Night-Heron is heavier with gray wings; Green Heron is slender with dark back.
Green_Heron.Best Ways to Identify: Small size, dark greenish back, chestnut neck, and habit of using lures to catch fish.

Green_Jay.Description: Colorful jay with green body, blue head, yellow outer tail feathers, black bib. Vivid pattern. About 10 inches.
Green_Jay.Behavior: Moves through thorny scrub in family groups. Uses tools to extract insects. Raucous with varied vocalizations.
Green_Jay.Habitat: Dense thorn scrub, woodland, and forest edge in southern Texas and from Mexico to South America.
Green_Jay.Similar Looking Birds: Unmistakable within its range. No other jay combines green body with blue head and yellow tail feathers.
Green_Jay.Best Ways to Identify: Green and blue combination unmistakable. Yellow outer tail feathers. Black bib. Rio Grande Valley, Texas resident.

Green_Kingfisher.Description: Small kingfisher, dark green above with white spots, male has rufous breast band, female has green breast bands. About 8 inches.
Green_Kingfisher.Behavior: Perches low over streams, plunges for small fish. Rare resident along clear streams in southern Texas and Arizona.
Green_Kingfisher.Habitat: Clear rocky streams in southern Texas and southeastern Arizona. Uncommon resident of Rio Grande region.
Green_Kingfisher.Similar Looking Birds: Belted Kingfisher larger with gray-blue plumage. Green Kingfisher tiny and dark green.
Green_Kingfisher.Best Ways to Identify: Tiny kingfisher, dark green above. Male rufous breast band. Perches low over clear streams in southern Texas.

Green_Parakeet.Description: Large all-green parakeet, long pointed tail, orange bill. Some scattered red feathers on head. About 13 inches.
Green_Parakeet.Behavior: Established feral population in the Rio Grande Valley of Texas. Loud flocks in urban areas.
Green_Parakeet.Habitat: Established feral flocks in southernmost Texas, particularly McAllen and Brownsville area of Rio Grande Valley.
Green_Parakeet.Similar Looking Birds: Other green parakeets in Texas. Green Parakeet largest of the feral Texas parakeets.
Green_Parakeet.Best Ways to Identify: Large all-green parakeet. Orange bill. Feral in Rio Grande Valley, Texas. Scattered red feathers on head.

Green_Sandpiper.Description: Medium sandpiper. Very dark greenish-brown back, white underparts with streaked breast, white rump, black and white barred tail. About 9 inches.
Green_Sandpiper.Behavior: Bobs rear end up and down. Flies with erratic twisting flight. Rare vagrant to North America from Eurasia.
Green_Sandpiper.Habitat: Breeds in European and Asian boreal forests near water. Winters in African wetlands. Rare vagrant to North America.
Green_Sandpiper.Similar Looking Birds: Solitary Sandpiper nearly identical. Green has darker back and less distinct eye ring.
Green_Sandpiper.Best Ways to Identify: Very dark back contrasting with white rump in flight. Black and white barred tail. Nearly identical to Solitary Sandpiper.

Greenish_Elaenia.Description: Small flycatcher, olive-green above with whitish eye ring, pale yellow underparts, white wing bars. About 5 inches.
Greenish_Elaenia.Behavior: Gleans insects in forest. Very rare vagrant from Mexico to southern Texas.
Greenish_Elaenia.Habitat: Forest and woodland from Mexico to South America. Very rare vagrant to southern Texas.
Greenish_Elaenia.Similar Looking Birds: Empidonax flycatchers similar. Greenish Elaenia more green-olive without eye ring.
Greenish_Elaenia.Best Ways to Identify: Olive-green flycatcher with pale yellow underparts. White wing bars. Very rare Texas vagrant from Mexico.

Groove-billed_Ani.Description: All-black bird with grooved heavy bill, long floppy tail, and glossy blue-black plumage.
Groove-billed_Ani.Behavior: Lives in groups that share nesting duties. Walks on the ground eating insects stirred up by cattle.
Groove-billed_Ani.Habitat: Open country, forest edges, and brush in southern Texas and Central America.
Groove-billed_Ani.Similar Looking Birds: Smooth-billed Ani has smooth bill without grooves; range barely overlaps in Florida.
Groove-billed_Ani.Best Ways to Identify: All-black with deeply grooved bill, floppy tail flight, and social family groups.

Guadalupe_Murrelet.Description: Small alcid. Black above, white below. Less white on face than Scripps's Murrelet; dark extends more around eye. About 10 inches.
Guadalupe_Murrelet.Behavior: Nests only on Guadalupe Island, Mexico. Critically endangered; population under 1,000 birds. Dives for fish offshore.
Guadalupe_Murrelet.Habitat: Breeds only on Guadalupe Island, Baja California. Forages in nearshore Pacific waters. Critically endangered species.
Guadalupe_Murrelet.Similar Looking Birds: Scripps's Murrelet nearly identical. Guadalupe has less white on face.
Guadalupe_Murrelet.Best Ways to Identify: Less white on face than Scripps's Murrelet; dark cap extends further down. Only breeds on Guadalupe Island.

Gull-billed_Tern.Description: Medium tern with thick black bill, pale gray upperparts, black cap, and white underparts.
Gull-billed_Tern.Behavior: Hawks insects over marshes rather than plunge-diving for fish like other terns.
Gull-billed_Tern.Habitat: Coastal marshes, beaches, and agricultural fields; breeds colonially.
Gull-billed_Tern.Similar Looking Birds: Other terns have thinner red or orange bills; Gull-billed Tern has a thick all-black bill.
Gull-billed_Tern.Best Ways to Identify: Thick all-black bill — hunts insects over land, unusual for a tern.

Gunnison_Sage-Grouse.Description: Smaller sage-grouse found only in Gunnison Basin, Colorado. Male has white chest tufts, long spiky tail feathers, yellow air sacs. About 22 inches.
Gunnison_Sage-Grouse.Behavior: Males gather at leks to perform elaborate strutting displays. Feeds almost exclusively on sagebrush. Critically endangered species.
Gunnison_Sage-Grouse.Habitat: Sagebrush steppe only in Gunnison Basin, Colorado, and a few isolated Utah populations. Critically dependent on big sagebrush.
Gunnison_Sage-Grouse.Similar Looking Birds: Greater Sage-Grouse nearly identical but noticeably larger. Only reliably separated by range.
Gunnison_Sage-Grouse.Best Ways to Identify: Smaller than Greater Sage-Grouse; only found in Gunnison Basin, CO. Filoplumes on neck more prominent during display.

Gyrfalcon.Description: Largest falcon. Variable plumage from all-white to dark gray. Massive size, broad-based wings. About 22 inches.
Gyrfalcon.Behavior: Hunts ptarmigan and waterfowl in Arctic. Rare winter visitor to northern US from Arctic breeding grounds.
Gyrfalcon.Habitat: Arctic tundra breeding grounds; winters south irregularly. Open areas, airports, and coastal regions.
Gyrfalcon.Similar Looking Birds: Peregrine Falcon much smaller. Gyrfalcon's massive size and broad wings distinctive.
Gyrfalcon.Best Ways to Identify: Enormous falcon, broader wings than Peregrine. Variable white to dark morphs. Rare Arctic visitor in winter.

Hairy_Woodpecker.Description: Medium black-and-white woodpecker with long chisel-like bill, white back stripe, and red nape on males.
Hairy_Woodpecker.Behavior: Excavates deeply into wood for bark beetles and wood-boring insects.
Hairy_Woodpecker.Habitat: Forests and woodlands across North America from Alaska to Florida.
Hairy_Woodpecker.Similar Looking Birds: Downy Woodpecker is smaller with short bill and black spots on outer tail feathers.
Hairy_Woodpecker.Best Ways to Identify: Larger than Downy with a much longer bill relative to head size.

Hammonds_Flycatcher.Description: Small Empidonax with short bill, large head, bold eye ring, and gray-olive plumage. Long primary projection.
Hammonds_Flycatcher.Behavior: Flicks tail and wings frequently. Breeds in tall coniferous forests.
Hammonds_Flycatcher.Habitat: Mature coniferous forests of western mountains during breeding; various habitats in migration.
Hammonds_Flycatcher.Similar Looking Birds: Dusky Flycatcher has longer bill and shorter primary projection; habitat differs.
Hammonds_Flycatcher.Best Ways to Identify: Short bill, bold eye ring, long primary projection, and tall coniferous forest breeding habitat.

Harlequin_Duck.Description: Striking small duck. Male has blue-gray plumage with white crescents, spots, and chestnut flanks.
Harlequin_Duck.Behavior: Breeds along fast-flowing mountain streams; winters on rocky surf-pounded coasts.
Harlequin_Duck.Habitat: Rocky coastlines in winter; swift mountain streams in summer.
Harlequin_Duck.Similar Looking Birds: Surf Scoter is all black with colorful bill; Harlequin Duck has unique white markings.
Harlequin_Duck.Best Ways to Identify: Male's unique blue-gray plumage with white geometric markings is unmistakable.

Harriss_Hawk.Description: Large dark hawk with chestnut shoulders, thighs, and wing lining. Bold white rump and tail base.
Harriss_Hawk.Behavior: Hunts cooperatively in family groups — unique among North American raptors.
Harriss_Hawk.Habitat: Desert scrub, cactus flats, and mesquite in the southwestern United States.
Harriss_Hawk.Similar Looking Birds: Dark phase Red-tailed lacks chestnut wing patches and white rump. Harris's is unique.
Harriss_Hawk.Best Ways to Identify: Chestnut shoulders and thighs, white rump patch, and cooperative hunting in groups.

Harriss_Sparrow.Description: Large sparrow with black crown, face, and bib surrounding a pink bill. Brown streaked back.
Harriss_Sparrow.Behavior: Breeds in boreal forest-tundra transition; winters in central North American grasslands.
Harriss_Sparrow.Habitat: Winters in brushy grasslands and hedgerows of the Great Plains.
Harriss_Sparrow.Similar Looking Birds: White-crowned and White-throated Sparrows lack black face and bib of Harris's Sparrow.
Harriss_Sparrow.Best Ways to Identify: Largest native sparrow — black crown, face, and bib with a distinctive pink bill.

Hawaii_Akepa.Description: Small Hawaiian honeycreeper, male bright orange-red, female olive-green, slightly crossed bill tips. About 4.5 inches.
Hawaii_Akepa.Behavior: Uses crossed bill to twist open ohia buds for nectar and insects. Endangered; declining on Big Island.
Hawaii_Akepa.Habitat: Native ohia forests of the Big Island above 4,000 feet.
Hawaii_Akepa.Similar Looking Birds: Apapane brighter red with curved bill. No other orange-red small bird with crossed bill on Big Island.
