Olive-sided_Flycatcher.Similar Looking Birds: Wood-Pewees lack the dark vest; Olive-sided has distinctive vest and rump tufts.
Olive-sided_Flycatcher.Best Ways to Identify: Dark olive vest framing white belly, white rump tufts, and quick-THREE-beers song.

Olive_Sparrow.Description: Medium sparrow, olive-green above, pale below, bold brown crown stripes, no wing bars. About 6 inches.
Olive_Sparrow.Behavior: Forages on ground under dense brush by scratching with both feet. Secretive. Resident in south Texas.
Olive_Sparrow.Habitat: Dense thorn scrub and brushy woodland of south Texas and eastern Mexico.
Olive_Sparrow.Similar Looking Birds: Green-tailed Towhee has rufous crown. Lincoln's Sparrow streaked below. Olive color distinctive.
Olive_Sparrow.Best Ways to Identify: Olive-green above, plain below, bold crown stripes. South Texas thorn scrub. Ground-scratching forager.

Olive_Warbler.Description: Medium wood warbler. Male has orange head with black mask, olive-gray back, white wing bars. About 5 inches.
Olive_Warbler.Behavior: Forages high in pine canopy for insects. Mountain specialist in Arizona and New Mexico pine forests.
Olive_Warbler.Habitat: High-elevation pine and mixed pine-oak forests of Arizona, New Mexico, and Mexico.
Olive_Warbler.Similar Looking Birds: Hermit Warbler has yellow head but no black mask. Virginia's Warbler lacks orange and mask.
Olive_Warbler.Best Ways to Identify: Orange head with black mask unique. White wing bars. High-elevation pine forest. Arizona and New Mexico.

Olomao.Description: Medium Hawaiian thrush, brown above with gray underparts. Island endemic of Lanai and Molokai. About 8 inches.
Olomao.Behavior: Foraged for fruit in native forest. Very few if any individuals likely remain. Song melodious.
Olomao.Habitat: Native forests of Lanai and Molokai. Lanai population extinct; Molokai population possibly persists.
Olomao.Similar Looking Birds: Omao similar but on Big Island. Kamao similar but Kauai only.
Olomao.Best Ways to Identify: Possibly extinct Hawaiian thrush. Brown above, gray below. Lanai and Molokai native forest habitat.

Omao.Description: Medium Hawaiian thrush, dark brown above, gray below, white eye ring. Upright posture. About 7 inches.
Omao.Behavior: Forages for fruit and insects in native forest. The most common surviving Hawaiian thrush. Melodious song.
Omao.Habitat: Native forests of the Big Island of Hawaii. Found primarily above 4,000 feet in ohia and koa forest.
Omao.Similar Looking Birds: Puaiohi smaller with pink legs. Other Hawaiian thrushes on different islands.
Omao.Best Ways to Identify: White eye ring on dark brown thrush. Big Island of Hawaii native forest. Most common surviving Hawaiian thrush.

Orange-billed_Nightingale-Thrush.Description: Small thrush, gray-brown above, gray below with orange bill and orange eye ring. About 6.5 inches.
Orange-billed_Nightingale-Thrush.Behavior: Forages on ground in dense forest. Melodious song. Rare vagrant to extreme southern Texas from Mexico.
Orange-billed_Nightingale-Thrush.Habitat: Dense humid forest understory from Mexico to South America. Rare vagrant to southern Texas.
Orange-billed_Nightingale-Thrush.Similar Looking Birds: Russet Nightingale-Thrush more russet. Spotted thrushes have spotted breasts. Orange bill distinctive.
Orange-billed_Nightingale-Thrush.Best Ways to Identify: Orange bill and orange eye ring on gray-brown thrush. Rare Texas vagrant from Mexico. Melodious song.

Orange-cheeked_Waxbill.Description: Tiny finch, brown above, gray below, bright orange cheek patches, red bill. About 4 inches.
Orange-cheeked_Waxbill.Behavior: Highly gregarious in small flocks. Forages for small seeds. Introduced to Puerto Rico and possibly Hawaii.
Orange-cheeked_Waxbill.Habitat: Open grasslands and scrub. Introduced to Puerto Rico. Native to West Africa.
Orange-cheeked_Waxbill.Similar Looking Birds: Common Waxbill has red face mask. Lavender Waxbill gray-lavender. Orange cheeks distinctive.
Orange-cheeked_Waxbill.Best Ways to Identify: Bright orange cheek patches distinctive. Gray below. Red bill. Tiny size. Puerto Rico introduced.

Orange-crowned_Warbler.Description: Dull olive-green warbler with obscure streaking, yellow undertail, and rarely seen orange crown patch.
Orange-crowned_Warbler.Behavior: One of the earliest spring migrants. Forages low in brushy vegetation.
Orange-crowned_Warbler.Habitat: Dense brush, willows, and chaparral across western North America.
Orange-crowned_Warbler.Similar Looking Birds: Nashville Warbler has white eye ring and gray head; Orange-crowned is plain dull olive.
Orange-crowned_Warbler.Best Ways to Identify: Dull olive with no wing bars, no eye ring, and faint streaking — often identified by elimination.

Orange-winged_Parrot.Description: Large parrot, green with blue and yellow forehead stripes, orange wing patch in flight. About 13 inches.
Orange-winged_Parrot.Behavior: Gregarious in large flocks. Very noisy. Small feral populations in Florida.
Orange-winged_Parrot.Habitat: Tropical forest and woodland of South America. Feral populations in Florida. Native to South America.
Orange-winged_Parrot.Similar Looking Birds: Other Amazon parrots lack orange wing patch. Wing patch visible only in flight.
Orange-winged_Parrot.Best Ways to Identify: Orange wing patch visible in flight distinctive. Blue and yellow forehead stripes. Green parrot. Florida feral.

Orchard_Oriole.Description: Smallest oriole. Male has chestnut and black body; female is greenish-yellow with white wing bars.
Orchard_Oriole.Behavior: Builds hanging nest in orchards and open woodlands. Eats nectar, insects, and fruit.
Orchard_Oriole.Habitat: Open woodlands, orchards, and suburban areas of eastern North America.
Orchard_Oriole.Similar Looking Birds: Baltimore Oriole male is bright orange; Orchard Oriole male is darker chestnut.
Orchard_Oriole.Best Ways to Identify: Chestnut and black male — darkest of the North American orioles.

Oriental_Cuckoo.Description: Medium slender cuckoo. Gray above, barred below, yellow orbital ring. Nearly identical to Common Cuckoo. About 13 inches.
Oriental_Cuckoo.Behavior: Brood parasite like Common Cuckoo. Rare vagrant to western Alaska from Siberia and East Asia. Best identified by call.
Oriental_Cuckoo.Habitat: Breeds in Siberian and East Asian forests. Winters in Southeast Asia and Australia. Rare vagrant to western Aleutian Islands.
Oriental_Cuckoo.Similar Looking Birds: Common Cuckoo nearly identical. Field separation requires careful attention to call and slight size differences.
Oriental_Cuckoo.Best Ways to Identify: Nearly identical to Common Cuckoo; best separated by call (lower, less clear "cuck-oo"). Rare vagrant to western Alaska.

Oriental_Greenfinch.Description: Medium finch, olive-green with yellow-green in wings, yellow-green rump, short pale bill. About 5.5 inches.
Oriental_Greenfinch.Behavior: Forages for seeds in trees and on ground. Rare vagrant to western Alaska and Aleutian Islands from Asia.
Oriental_Greenfinch.Habitat: Woodland, scrub, and gardens in East Asia. Rare vagrant to western Alaska.
Oriental_Greenfinch.Similar Looking Birds: Eurasian Siskin has black crown and streaking. Pine Siskin heavily streaked. Yellow-green color distinctive.
Oriental_Greenfinch.Best Ways to Identify: Olive-green with yellow-green wing flashes. Short pale bill. Rare Alaska vagrant from Japan and Siberia.

Oriental_Honey-buzzard.Description: Medium hawk, long tail, small pigeon-like head, variable brown plumage. Long neck and small head distinctive. About 22 inches.
Oriental_Honey-buzzard.Behavior: Raids wasp and bee nests for larvae. Variable plumage with many color morphs. Rare vagrant to Alaska from Asia.
Oriental_Honey-buzzard.Habitat: Forest and woodland of East and Southeast Asia. Rare vagrant to western Alaska.
Oriental_Honey-buzzard.Similar Looking Birds: Broad-winged and other buteos similar. Oriental Honey- buzzard's small head and long neck distinctive.
Oriental_Honey-buzzard.Best Ways to Identify: Small pigeon-like head with long neck. Variable brown plumage. Rare Alaska vagrant from East Asia.

Oriental_Pratincole.Description: Swallow-like wader. Brown above, buff throat outlined in black, red bill base, deeply forked tail, rusty underwings. About 9 inches.
Oriental_Pratincole.Behavior: Catches insects in flight like a swallow but walks on ground too. Rare vagrant to Pacific coast from Asian breeding grounds.
Oriental_Pratincole.Habitat: Breeds on Asian grasslands and fields. Winters in Africa and Australia. Rare vagrant to Pacific coast of North America.
Oriental_Pratincole.Similar Looking Birds: No similar bird in range. Swallow-like flight and forked tail distinctive.
Oriental_Pratincole.Best Ways to Identify: Swallow-like flight with forked tail. Brown above, buff throat with black border. Rusty underwing in flight.

Oriental_Scops-Owl.Description: Small scops owl with ear tufts. Brown streaked plumage, yellow eyes. Similar to other scops owls. About 7 inches.
Oriental_Scops-Owl.Behavior: Nocturnal insect hunter. Migratory; rare vagrant to western Alaska from East Asia.
Oriental_Scops-Owl.Habitat: Forest and woodland of East and South Asia. Rare vagrant to western Alaska.
Oriental_Scops-Owl.Similar Looking Birds: Western Screech-Owl similar. Oriental Scops-Owl found only in western Alaska as vagrant.
Oriental_Scops-Owl.Best Ways to Identify: Small ear-tufted owl in western Alaska. Brown streaked plumage, yellow eyes. Very rare vagrant from Asia.

Oriental_Turtle-Dove.Description: Medium dove. Reddish-brown upperparts with dark scaly pattern, pinkish-gray underparts, and black and white striped neck patch. About 13 inches.
Oriental_Turtle-Dove.Behavior: Forages on ground for seeds and berries. Migrates long distances through East Asia. Rare vagrant to western Alaska from Siberia.
Oriental_Turtle-Dove.Habitat: Breeds in forests and woodland of East Asia and Siberia. Winters in South and Southeast Asia. Rare vagrant to Aleutian Islands.
Oriental_Turtle-Dove.Similar Looking Birds: European Turtle-Dove similar. Oriental larger with more heavily scaled upperparts.
Oriental_Turtle-Dove.Best Ways to Identify: Scaly reddish-brown upperparts with striped neck patch. Larger and darker than European Turtle-Dove. Rare vagrant in western Alaska.

Osprey.Description: Large raptor with white underparts, dark brown back, dark eye stripe, and reversible outer toe for gripping fish.
Osprey.Behavior: Dives feet-first into water to catch fish. Often hovers before diving.
Osprey.Habitat: Near water — lakes, rivers, coasts, and reservoirs across North America.
Osprey.Similar Looking Birds: Bald Eagle is much larger and all dark; Osprey has distinctive white belly and dark wrist patches.
Osprey.Best Ways to Identify: White belly, dark wrist patches, and feet-first dives into water for fish.

Ou.Description: Medium Hawaiian honeycreeper, male yellow-green head and breast, olive-green back, hooked parrot-like bill. About 6.5 inches.
Ou.Behavior: Fed on fruit, seeds, and buds. Possibly extinct; no confirmed records since the 1980s.
Ou.Habitat: Native forests throughout Hawaiian Islands. Possibly extinct due to avian disease and introduced species.
Ou.Similar Looking Birds: Palila has yellow head and heavy bill. No other bird in Hawaii has a hooked parrot-like bill.
Ou.Best Ways to Identify: Hooked parrot-like bill distinctive. Yellow-green head, olive back. Possibly extinct. No confirmed modern records.

Ovenbird.Description: Warbler with orange crown stripe bordered by black, olive back, heavily streaked white underparts.
Ovenbird.Behavior: Walks on the forest floor. Loud tea-CHER tea-CHER song. Builds domed oven-shaped nest.
Ovenbird.Habitat: Mature deciduous forests with open understory in eastern North America.
Ovenbird.Similar Looking Birds: Waterthrushes bob tail; Ovenbird walks slowly with tail cocked. Orange crown is unique.
Ovenbird.Best Ways to Identify: Orange-striped crown, walks on forest floor, and loud ringing tea-CHER song.

Pacific-slope_Flycatcher.Description: Olive-green Empidonax with teardrop-shaped eye ring, yellow-green wash on underparts, and almond eye ring.
Pacific-slope_Flycatcher.Behavior: Gives distinctive upslurred pseet call. Breeds in moist coniferous forests.
Pacific-slope_Flycatcher.Habitat: Moist forests and canyons of the Pacific Coast.
Pacific-slope_Flycatcher.Similar Looking Birds: Cordilleran Flycatcher is nearly identical but found inland; best separated by call.
Pacific-slope_Flycatcher.Best Ways to Identify: Almond-shaped eye ring, yellow-green wash, and upslurred pseet call in Pacific Coast forests.

Pacific_(Fork-tailed)_Swift.Description: Large swift. Dark sooty brown with distinct white rump patch and deeply forked tail. White throat patch. About 7 inches.
Pacific_(Fork-tailed)_Swift.Behavior: Aerial insect feeder. Forms large flocks. Migrates long distances. Rare vagrant to western Alaska and Pacific coast from Asia.
Pacific_(Fork-tailed)_Swift.Habitat: Breeds across Siberia and East Asia. Migrates to Australia. Rare vagrant to western Alaska and Pacific coast.
Pacific_(Fork-tailed)_Swift.Similar Looking Birds: Common Swift lacks forked tail and white rump. Fork-tailed Swift's white rump distinctive.
Pacific_(Fork-tailed)_Swift.Best Ways to Identify: Distinctive white rump patch and deeply forked tail unique. Dark body and white throat. Rare vagrant to western Alaska.

Pacific_Golden-Plover.Description: Medium plover. Golden-speckled brown upperparts, black face and underparts in breeding plumage. Smaller and slimmer than American Golden-Plover. About 10 inches.
Pacific_Golden-Plover.Behavior: Forages on beaches, mudflats, and grasslands for invertebrates. Migrates between Arctic Alaska and Pacific islands to wintering areas.
Pacific_Golden-Plover.Habitat: Breeds on Arctic tundra of Alaska and Siberia. Winters on Pacific islands, Hawaii, and Southeast Asian coasts.
Pacific_Golden-Plover.Similar Looking Birds: American Golden-Plover similar; Pacific is smaller and slightly yellower overall.
Pacific_Golden-Plover.Best Ways to Identify: Smaller and slimmer than American Golden-Plover. Pacific migrants through Hawaii distinctive in grassland habitat.

Pacific_Loon.Description: Medium loon with gray nape, black throat patch, and white-checkered back in breeding plumage.
Pacific_Loon.Behavior: Migrates in long lines over the Pacific coast. Dives for fish.
Pacific_Loon.Habitat: Pacific Ocean and large lakes; breeds on Arctic lakes.
Pacific_Loon.Similar Looking Birds: Common Loon is larger with heavier bill; Red-throated has upturned bill.
Pacific_Loon.Best Ways to Identify: Gray nape and black throat with fine white striping in breeding — Common Loon has heavier bill.

Pacific_Wren.Description: Tiny dark brown wren, heavily barred throughout, very short stubby tail, pale buff supercilium. About 4 inches.
Pacific_Wren.Behavior: Creeps through dense forest undergrowth. Extraordinarily loud song for its tiny size. Typically keeps very low.
Pacific_Wren.Habitat: Dense moist forests of Pacific Coast, primarily in old-growth coniferous forest. Prefers fallen logs and root tangles.
Pacific_Wren.Similar Looking Birds: Winter Wren nearly identical but different range. House Wren larger, less barred, longer tail.
Pacific_Wren.Best Ways to Identify: Tiny dark wren with very short tail. Heavy barring throughout. Pacific Coast old-growth forest habitat.

Paint-billed_Crake.Description: Small secretive rail. Brown and gray plumage, short bright red and yellow bill. Gray face, brownish back. About 7 inches.
Paint-billed_Crake.Behavior: Very secretive; rarely seen in dense marsh grass. Rare vagrant to North America from South America.
Paint-billed_Crake.Habitat: Dense freshwater marshes and wet grasslands in South America. Very rare vagrant to southern US, mainly Texas.
Paint-billed_Crake.Similar Looking Birds: Yellow-breasted Crake similar. Paint-billed has colorful red and yellow bill distinctive.
Paint-billed_Crake.Best Ways to Identify: Short red and yellow bill diagnostic. Secretive brown and gray plumage. Dense wet marsh habitat.

Painted_Bunting.Description: Male is the most colorful North American bird: blue head, red underparts, and green back.
Painted_Bunting.Behavior: Males are highly territorial. Often secretive despite brilliant colors.
Painted_Bunting.Habitat: Brushy areas and forest edges; breeds in south-central and southeastern United States.
Painted_Bunting.Similar Looking Birds: No other North American bird has the combination of blue, red, and green.
Painted_Bunting.Best Ways to Identify: Male's combination of blue head, red body, and green back — most colorful NA bird.

Painted_Redstart.Description: Striking black warbler with red breast, white wing patch, and white outer tail feathers.
Painted_Redstart.Behavior: Fans tail and droops wings to flush insects. Active and acrobatic forager.
Painted_Redstart.Habitat: Montane pine-oak forests of southeastern Arizona and New Mexico.
Painted_Redstart.Similar Looking Birds: American Redstart is orange-and-black; Painted Redstart is red-and-black with white patches.
Painted_Redstart.Best Ways to Identify: Black warbler with brilliant red breast and white wing and tail patches.

Palila.Description: Medium Hawaiian finch, yellow head and breast, gray back, white belly, heavy seed-cracking bill. About 6 inches.
Palila.Behavior: Feeds almost exclusively on unripe mamane seeds. Critically endangered. Found only on high slopes of Mauna Kea.
Palila.Habitat: Subalpine mamane-naio woodland on Mauna Kea, Hawaii. Range restricted to small area above 6,500 feet.
Palila.Similar Looking Birds: Yellow head and heavy bill distinctive. Hawaii Amakihi smaller with curved bill. No similar finch in range.
Palila.Best Ways to Identify: Yellow head and breast with heavy finch bill. Mauna Kea mamane forest only. Critically endangered endemic.

Pallass_Bunting.Description: Small bunting. Male has black head and throat, white collar, brown back, white outer tail feathers. About 5.5 inches.
Pallass_Bunting.Behavior: Forages on ground in open areas and wet meadows. Rare vagrant to western Alaska from Siberia.
Pallass_Bunting.Habitat: Wet meadows and marshy areas of Siberia. Rare vagrant to western Alaska and Aleutians.
Pallass_Bunting.Similar Looking Birds: Reed Bunting similar but larger with different bill. Lapland Longspur has chestnut nape.
Pallass_Bunting.Best Ways to Identify: Small bunting with black head, white collar. Rare Alaska vagrant from Siberia. Pale lesser wing coverts.

Pallass_Grasshopper_Warbler.Description: Small warbler, heavily streaked brown above, whitish below with spotted breast band. Rounded tail. About 5 inches.
Pallass_Grasshopper_Warbler.Behavior: Skulks in dense grass and sedge. Rare vagrant to western Alaska. Creeps mouse-like through vegetation.
Pallass_Grasshopper_Warbler.Habitat: Wet grasslands, sedge meadows, and marshes in Asia. Rare vagrant to Aleutian and Pribilof Islands, Alaska.
Pallass_Grasshopper_Warbler.Similar Looking Birds: Lanceolated Warbler similar but smaller and more heavily streaked below. Grasshopper Warbler has unspotted rump.
Pallass_Grasshopper_Warbler.Best Ways to Identify: Streaked above with spotted breast, rufous-tinged rump. Western Alaska vagrant. Skulks in dense wet vegetation.

Pallass_Gull.Description: Very large gull. Black hood, heavy yellow bill with red and black markings, pale gray back, large size. About 27 inches.
Pallass_Gull.Behavior: Largest hooded gull. Feeds on fish and other water life. Very rare vagrant to western Alaska and Pacific coast from Central Asia.
Pallass_Gull.Habitat: Central Asian lakes and Caspian Sea region. Winters on Indian Ocean coast. Very rare vagrant to western North America.
Pallass_Gull.Similar Looking Birds: Great Black-backed Gull similar size. Pallas's has black hood and different bill pattern.
Pallass_Gull.Best Ways to Identify: Very large size with black hood. Heavy yellow bill with red and black marks. Rare vagrant from Central Asia.

Pallass_Leaf_Warbler.Description: Tiny leaf warbler, green above with yellow crown stripe, two yellow wing bars, yellow rump. About 3.5 inches.
Pallass_Leaf_Warbler.Behavior: Extremely active, hovers to pick insects from leaves. Rare vagrant to western Alaska. Often hangs upside-down like tit.
Pallass_Leaf_Warbler.Habitat: Coniferous and mixed forests in Asia. Rare vagrant to western Alaska and Aleutian Islands.
Pallass_Leaf_Warbler.Similar Looking Birds: Yellow-browed Warbler lacks crown stripe and rump patch. Goldcrest has orange crown but different shape.
Pallass_Leaf_Warbler.Best Ways to Identify: Yellow crown stripe, yellow rump, and two yellow wing bars. Tiny size. Very active hovering forager.

Pallass_Rosefinch.Description: Medium finch. Male pale pink with white wing bars, white spots on wing coverts. Female streaked brown. About 6.5 inches.
Pallass_Rosefinch.Behavior: Forages for seeds and berries in forest and scrub. Very rare vagrant to western Alaska from Siberia.
Pallass_Rosefinch.Habitat: Forests and scrub of Siberia and East Asia. Very rare vagrant to western Alaska.
Pallass_Rosefinch.Similar Looking Birds: Common Rosefinch less pale, more rosy-red. Long-tailed Rosefinch has very long tail. Other rosefinches rare in range.
Pallass_Rosefinch.Best Ways to Identify: Pale pink male with white wing spots. Larger than Common Rosefinch. Very rare Alaska vagrant from Siberia.

Palm_Warbler.Description: Brown-and-yellow warbler with rufous cap, yellow undertail, and constant tail-bobbing habit.
Palm_Warbler.Behavior: Constantly bobs tail while walking on ground. One of earliest fall migrants.
Palm_Warbler.Habitat: Breeds in boreal bogs; winters in southeastern states near beaches and palms.
Palm_Warbler.Similar Looking Birds: Prairie Warbler bobs tail but has facial markings; Palm Warbler has rufous cap.
Palm_Warbler.Best Ways to Identify: Rufous cap, yellow undertail, and incessant tail-bobbing on the ground.

Parakeet_Auklet.Description: Medium auklet. Black above, white below, distinctive round orange bill, white eye plume. About 10 inches.
Parakeet_Auklet.Behavior: Dives for jellyfish and copepods. Breeds on Alaskan and Siberian cliff islands. Winters in North Pacific offshore.
Parakeet_Auklet.Habitat: Breeds on rocky islands in Bering Sea and Gulf of Alaska. Winters offshore in North Pacific.
Parakeet_Auklet.Similar Looking Birds: Other auklets. Parakeet Auklet's round orange bill and white eye plume distinctive.
Parakeet_Auklet.Best Ways to Identify: Round orange bill unique among auklets. White eye plume. Black above, white below. Aleutian Islands species.

Parasitic_Jaeger.Description: Medium jaeger. Dark and light morphs. Pointed central tail projection in breeding. Slender and falcon- like. About 19 inches.
Parasitic_Jaeger.Behavior: Aggressively pursues terns and gulls to steal food. Most commonly seen jaeger from shore. Regular migrant on both coasts.
Parasitic_Jaeger.Habitat: Breeds on Arctic tundra. Pelagic outside breeding. Regular migrant on both coasts; most often seen from shore.
Parasitic_Jaeger.Similar Looking Birds: Pomarine Jaeger larger with different tail projection. Long-tailed Jaeger slimmer.
Parasitic_Jaeger.Best Ways to Identify: Medium size and pointed (not blunt) tail projection. Most commonly seen jaeger from coastal promontories.

Parkinsons_Petrel.Description: Large black petrel with pale ivory-yellow bill with dark culmen. All black otherwise. About 18 inches.
Parkinsons_Petrel.Behavior: Breeds on Great Barrier Island, New Zealand. Migrates into North Pacific; rare visitor off California and Pacific coast.
Parkinsons_Petrel.Habitat: Eastern North Pacific in non-breeding season. Rare visitor off California; breeds on New Zealand islands.
Parkinsons_Petrel.Similar Looking Birds: White-chinned Petrel similar but may show white chin. Parkinson's all black with pale bill.
Parkinsons_Petrel.Best Ways to Identify: All-black body with pale bill with dark culmen. Large petrel in eastern North Pacific. New Zealand breeder, Pacific migrant.

Passenger_Pigeon.Description: EXTINCT North American pigeon. Male blue-gray above, reddish below, long pointed tail. Female duller. Billions once existed. Last died September 1, 1914.
Passenger_Pigeon.Behavior: Formed enormous flocks that darkened the sky for hours. Nested in massive colonies. Hunted to extinction by 1914 due to commercial hunting.
Passenger_Pigeon.Habitat: Deciduous forests of eastern North America, particularly beech and oak forests. Migratory; moved with food sources. Now extinct.
Passenger_Pigeon.Similar Looking Birds: Mourning Dove similar in shape; smaller and lighter in color.
Passenger_Pigeon.Best Ways to Identify: Only known from museum specimens and historical photos of last captive bird "Martha" (1914). Extinct since September 1, 1914.

Pechora_Pipit.Description: Small pipit, heavily streaked brown above with white stripes on back, buff-white below with dark streaks. About 5.5 inches.
Pechora_Pipit.Behavior: Skulks in dense grass, difficult to see. Short flight when flushed. Rare vagrant to western Alaska.
Pechora_Pipit.Habitat: Wet meadows and scrub in Siberia. Rare vagrant to western Alaska and Aleutian Islands.
Pechora_Pipit.Similar Looking Birds: Olive-backed Pipit more olive above. Red-throated Pipit has reddish throat. Two white stripes on back helpful.
Pechora_Pipit.Best Ways to Identify: Two white stripes visible on back. Heavily streaked above. Skulks in grass. Rare Alaska vagrant from Siberia.

Pectoral_Sandpiper.Description: Medium sandpiper with abrupt contrast between heavily streaked brown breast and white belly.
Pectoral_Sandpiper.Behavior: Often found in grassy or flooded fields. Long-distance migrant from Arctic to South America.
Pectoral_Sandpiper.Habitat: Wet meadows, marshes, and mudflats during migration across North America.
Pectoral_Sandpiper.Similar Looking Birds: White-rumped Sandpiper has white rump; Pectoral has sharp breast-belly contrast.
Pectoral_Sandpiper.Best Ways to Identify: Sharply demarcated streaked breast and white belly — like wearing a bib.

Pelagic_Cormorant.Description: Small cormorant with iridescent green-and-purple plumage, slender neck, thin bill, and red facial skin.
Pelagic_Cormorant.Behavior: Nests on narrow cliff ledges. Dives for fish in rocky inshore waters.
Pelagic_Cormorant.Habitat: Rocky Pacific coast from Alaska to California.
Pelagic_Cormorant.Similar Looking Birds: Brandt's Cormorant is larger with blue throat pouch; Pelagic is slender with red face.
Pelagic_Cormorant.Best Ways to Identify: Smallest Pacific cormorant — iridescent plumage, slender neck, and thin bill on rocky cliffs.

Peregrine_Falcon.Description: Powerful falcon with slate-blue back, dark hood with thick mustache stripe, and barred underparts.
Peregrine_Falcon.Behavior: Stoops at 200+ mph to strike birds in flight — fastest animal on Earth.
Peregrine_Falcon.Habitat: Coastal cliffs, skyscrapers, and open country across North America.
Peregrine_Falcon.Similar Looking Birds: Prairie Falcon is sandy-brown with black axillaries; Peregrine is slate-blue with dark hood.
Peregrine_Falcon.Best Ways to Identify: Slate-blue back, heavy mustache stripe, and fastest stoop of any animal.

Phainopepla.Description: Silky flycatcher. Male is glossy black with red eyes and white wing patches; female is gray.
Phainopepla.Behavior: Eats mistletoe berries and disperses seeds. Flies with moth-like wing flicks.
Phainopepla.Habitat: Desert mistletoe groves, riparian areas, and chaparral of the southwestern United States.
Phainopepla.Similar Looking Birds: No other bird has the male's glossy black plumage with white wing patches and red eyes.
Phainopepla.Best Ways to Identify: Glossy black male with red eyes and white wing patches — eats mistletoe berries.

Philadelphia_Vireo.Description: Small vireo with pale yellow underparts, gray cap, dark eye line, and whitish supercilium.
Philadelphia_Vireo.Behavior: Often found high in trees with other vireos and warblers during migration.
Philadelphia_Vireo.Habitat: Breeds in young deciduous and mixed forests; migrates through eastern North America.
Philadelphia_Vireo.Similar Looking Birds: Warbling Vireo is paler with no yellow; Red-eyed Vireo is larger with gray cap.
Philadelphia_Vireo.Best Ways to Identify: Yellow wash on underparts and dark eye line — plainer than other vireos.

Pied-billed_Grebe.Description: Stocky grebe with chicken-like bill banded with black in breeding, brown plumage, and white rump.
Pied-billed_Grebe.Behavior: Can adjust buoyancy to sink slowly out of sight rather than diving. Rarely flies.
Pied-billed_Grebe.Habitat: Freshwater marshes and ponds across North America.
Pied-billed_Grebe.Similar Looking Birds: Other grebes have pointed bills; Pied-billed has thick chicken-like bill.
Pied-billed_Grebe.Best Ways to Identify: Stout chicken-like bill with black band in breeding — sinks slowly rather than diving.

Pied_Wheatear.Description: Small chat. Male black throat and back, white crown and rump, white below. Female brown. About 5.5 inches.
Pied_Wheatear.Behavior: Perches upright on rocks and boulders. Rare vagrant to western Alaska from Siberia and Central Asia.
Pied_Wheatear.Habitat: Open rocky and semi-arid country of Siberia and Central Asia. Very rare vagrant to western Alaska.
Pied_Wheatear.Similar Looking Birds: Northern Wheatear gray above without black back. No similar black-backed chat in Alaska range.
Pied_Wheatear.Best Ways to Identify: Male black throat and back with white crown and rump. Very rare Alaska vagrant from Siberia.

Pigeon_Guillemot.Description: Medium alcid. Breeding adult black with white wing patch bisected by black bar, red mouth and legs. Winter mostly white. About 13 inches.
Pigeon_Guillemot.Behavior: Dives for fish and invertebrates near shore. Less pelagic than other alcids. Found year-round along rocky Pacific coast.
Pigeon_Guillemot.Habitat: Rocky Pacific coastlines from Alaska to California. Nests in rock crevices and sea caves. Year-round resident along Pacific coast.
Pigeon_Guillemot.Similar Looking Birds: Black Guillemot on Atlantic coast is nearly identical. Pigeon Guillemot has wing patch bisected by bar.
Pigeon_Guillemot.Best Ways to Identify: White wing patch with black wedge through middle on otherwise black breeding bird. Red legs and mouth.

Pileated_Woodpecker.Description: Crow-sized woodpecker with brilliant red crest, black body, white wing patches, and white stripes on neck.
Pileated_Woodpecker.Behavior: Excavates large rectangular holes in dead trees for carpenter ants. Loud wuk-wuk-wuk call.
Pileated_Woodpecker.Habitat: Mature forests with large trees across North America.
Pileated_Woodpecker.Similar Looking Birds: No other woodpecker approaches its large size and brilliant red crest.
Pileated_Woodpecker.Best Ways to Identify: Largest North American woodpecker — crow-sized with spectacular red crest.

Pin-tailed_Snipe.Description: Medium snipe. Brown cryptically patterned plumage with narrow outer tail feathers (pin-like). Bill moderately long. About 10 inches.
Pin-tailed_Snipe.Behavior: Secretive; rises with slow wingbeats when flushed. Rare vagrant to western Alaska from Asian breeding grounds.
Pin-tailed_Snipe.Habitat: Breeds in Asian boreal and subarctic wetlands. Winters in South Asia. Rare vagrant to western Alaska.
Pin-tailed_Snipe.Similar Looking Birds: Common Snipe nearly identical. Pin-tailed Snipe has narrow pin-like outer tail feathers.
Pin-tailed_Snipe.Best Ways to Identify: Narrow outer tail feathers diagnostic but very hard to see in field. Slow wingbeats when flushed.

Pin-tailed_Whydah.Description: Small bird. Breeding male black-and-white with extraordinary long black pin-tail. Female streaked brown. About 5 inches (plus 8-inch tail).
Pin-tailed_Whydah.Behavior: Brood parasite of waxbills. Males display with pin-tail in flight. Established in California.
Pin-tailed_Whydah.Habitat: Open areas and gardens. Established feral population in California. Native to sub-Saharan Africa.
Pin-tailed_Whydah.Similar Looking Birds: No other bird has black-and-white pattern plus extremely long pin-tail.
Pin-tailed_Whydah.Best Ways to Identify: Male extraordinary long black tail, black-and-white body. Unmistakable. California feral population.

Pine_Bunting.Description: Medium bunting. Male has white head with brown streaking, chestnut breast, chestnut back. Female streaked brown. About 6.5 inches.
Pine_Bunting.Behavior: Forages on ground for seeds. Very rare vagrant to western Alaska from Siberia.
Pine_Bunting.Habitat: Open woodland, scrub, and farmland of Siberia and Central Asia. Very rare vagrant to western Alaska.
Pine_Bunting.Similar Looking Birds: Yellow-breasted Bunting has yellow below. Yellowhammer has yellow head. No similar white-headed bunting in range.
Pine_Bunting.Best Ways to Identify: Male white head and chestnut breast. Very rare Alaska vagrant from Siberia. Female streaked brown.

Pine_Flycatcher.Description: Small Empidonax flycatcher, olive-green above, pale below with two wing bars. Very similar to other Empidonax. About 5 inches.
Pine_Flycatcher.Behavior: Very rare vagrant from Mexico. Best identified by call which differs from similar species.
Pine_Flycatcher.Habitat: Pine forest of Mexico and Central America. Very rare vagrant to southern Arizona.
Pine_Flycatcher.Similar Looking Birds: Cordilleran and other Empidonax nearly identical. Best identified by voice.
Pine_Flycatcher.Best Ways to Identify: Nearly identical to other Empidonax flycatchers. Best identified by call. Very rare vagrant from Mexico.

Pine_Grosbeak.Description: Large finch with rosy-red plumage on male, two white wing bars, and large finch bill. Female is olive-gray.
Pine_Grosbeak.Behavior: Irruptive migrant that moves south when northern food crops fail. Very tame.
Pine_Grosbeak.Habitat: Boreal coniferous forests; irrupts to northern states in winter.
Pine_Grosbeak.Similar Looking Birds: White-winged Crossbill has crossed bill; Purple Finch is smaller; Pine Grosbeak is largest.
Pine_Grosbeak.Best Ways to Identify: Largest North American finch — rosy-red male with white wing bars and plump body.

Pine_Siskin.Description: Small streaked finch with yellow in wings and at base of tail, pointed bill, and heavily streaked body.
Pine_Siskin.Behavior: Irruptive nomad that follows conifer seed crops. Aggressive at feeders.
Pine_Siskin.Habitat: Coniferous forests and weedy fields across North America; highly irruptive.
Pine_Siskin.Similar Looking Birds: American Goldfinch is brighter yellow with less streaking; Pine Siskin is heavily streaked.
Pine_Siskin.Best Ways to Identify: Heavily streaked with yellow wing and tail flashes — often visits feeders in irruption years.

Pine_Warbler.Description: Yellow-olive warbler with unstreaked back, white wing bars, and yellow breast with faint streaking.
Pine_Warbler.Behavior: Year-round resident in pine forests. Probes pine bark and eats pine seeds in winter.
Pine_Warbler.Habitat: Pine forests of eastern North America.
Pine_Warbler.Similar Looking Birds: Prairie and Palm Warblers have distinctive marks; Pine Warbler is plain with unstreaked back.
Pine_Warbler.Best Ways to Identify: Plain olive-yellow with unstreaked back, white wing bars, and pine forest year-round residency.

Pink-footed_Goose.Description: A medium-sized goose with a short pink-and-black bill, distinctive pink legs and feet, and a rounded brown head with dark neck.
Pink-footed_Goose.Behavior: Grazes on crops, grass, and root vegetables. Highly gregarious, forming enormous flocks. Known for spectacular mass flights at dusk.
Pink-footed_Goose.Habitat: Breeds in Greenland, Iceland, and Svalbard in remote mountain valleys. Winters on agricultural land and estuaries in western Europe.
Pink-footed_Goose.Similar Looking Birds: Similar to Bean Goose but has pink (not orange) legs. Greylag Goose is larger with all-orange bill and paler plumage.
Pink-footed_Goose.Best Ways to Identify: Pink legs and feet are the primary field mark. Short pink-and-black bill, small rounded head, and dark chocolate-brown neck are key identifiers.

Pink-footed_Shearwater.Description: Large shearwater, grayish-brown above, white below with mottled sides, pink bill and feet. About 19 inches.
Pink-footed_Shearwater.Behavior: Breeds on Juan Fernandez Islands; common offshore Pacific coast. One of the most regular Pacific shearwaters off California.
Pink-footed_Shearwater.Habitat: Eastern North Pacific. Common offshore California and Pacific coast. Breeds on Chilean islands.
Pink-footed_Shearwater.Similar Looking Birds: Buller's Shearwater paler with bold M-pattern. Flesh-footed all-dark with pink bill and feet.
Pink-footed_Shearwater.Best Ways to Identify: Large grayish-brown shearwater with pink bill and feet. Mottled belly. Very common offshore California.

Pinyon_Jay.Description: Stocky blue jay with no crest, short tail, long bill. Dull blue throughout with pale streaks on throat. About 10 inches.
Pinyon_Jay.Behavior: Highly nomadic, travels in large flocks through pinyon-juniper woodlands. Caches pine seeds extensively. Loud, crowlike calls.
Pinyon_Jay.Habitat: Pinyon-juniper woodlands of western United States. Nomadic, moving in response to pine cone crop abundance.
Pinyon_Jay.Similar Looking Birds: Western Scrub-Jay and Steller's Jay both crested. Clark's Nutcracker grayish with white wing patches.
Pinyon_Jay.Best Ways to Identify: All-blue jay with no crest. Long sharp bill adapted for pine seeds. Travels in large noisy flocks.

Piping_Plover.Description: Pale sandy plover with orange legs, black chest band, orange bill base, and white forehead.
Piping_Plover.Behavior: Nests on open sand beaches. Runs rapidly and freezes, blending with sand perfectly.
Piping_Plover.Habitat: Sandy ocean beaches and Great Lakes shores during breeding.
Piping_Plover.Similar Looking Birds: Semipalmated Plover is darker brown; Piping Plover is pale sand-colored.
Piping_Plover.Best Ways to Identify: Pale as dry sand, orange legs, and partial black breast band — endangered beach nester.

Piratic_Flycatcher.Description: Small flycatcher, brown above streaked, whitish below with brown streaking, dark mask, yellow crown patch. About 6 inches.
Piratic_Flycatcher.Behavior: Pirates nest cavities from other species. Migratory; rare vagrant to North American Atlantic and Gulf coasts.
Piratic_Flycatcher.Habitat: Open woodland and forest edge of tropical Americas. Rare vagrant to Atlantic and Gulf coasts.
Piratic_Flycatcher.Similar Looking Birds: Variegated Flycatcher very similar. Piratic Flycatcher has different streaking pattern.
Piratic_Flycatcher.Best Ways to Identify: Streaked brown flycatcher with white supercilium, yellow crown. Rare vagrant to Atlantic and Gulf coasts.

Plain-capped_Starthroat.Description: Large hummingbird. Long straight bill. Gray-brown above and below, crimson throat, broad white facial stripes, white rump patch. About 5 inches.
Plain-capped_Starthroat.Behavior: Feeds on nectar from various flowers. Often perches prominently. Rare vagrant to Arizona from Mexico.
Plain-capped_Starthroat.Habitat: Dry thorn scrub, tropical forest edges, and arid areas of Mexico and Central America. Rare visitor to southeastern Arizona.
Plain-capped_Starthroat.Similar Looking Birds: Long bill distinguishes it from other hummingbirds. White facial stripes and rump patch distinctive.
Plain-capped_Starthroat.Best Ways to Identify: Long straight bill, red throat patch, bold white facial stripes, and white rump patch. Rare vagrant in southeastern Arizona.

Plain_Chachalaca.Description: Chicken-like bird with long tail and small head. Olive-brown overall with bare red throat skin. About 22 inches including long tail.
Plain_Chachalaca.Behavior: Groups call loudly at dawn with raucous chorus. Forages in trees and shrubs for fruit, berries, and leaves in dense South Texas brush.
Plain_Chachalaca.Habitat: Dense thorny scrub, riparian forests, and brushy areas of southern Texas and Central America. Common in Lower Rio Grande Valley.
Plain_Chachalaca.Similar Looking Birds: No similar bird in US range. Large dove or small pheasant in shape but behavior is distinctive.
Plain_Chachalaca.Best Ways to Identify: Long tail, small head, olive-brown coloring with bare red throat skin. Loud "cha-cha-lac" calls given in groups at dawn.

Plumbeous_Vireo.Description: Medium vireo with gray back, white underparts, white spectacles, and two white wing bars; no yellow tones.
Plumbeous_Vireo.Behavior: Sings persistently from treetops; gleans insects from foliage methodically; builds cup nest in fork of branch.
Plumbeous_Vireo.Habitat: Montane pine-oak forests and juniper woodlands of Rocky Mountains and southwestern US highlands.
Plumbeous_Vireo.Similar Looking Birds: Cassin's Vireo has greenish or yellowish tones; Blue-headed Vireo has blue-gray head contrasting with white throat.
Plumbeous_Vireo.Best Ways to Identify: All gray and white; bold white spectacles; strong white wing bars; no yellow or olive tones; mountain forests.

Pomarine_Jaeger.Description: Large jaeger with twisted spoon-shaped central tail feathers (breeding). Dark and light morphs. Broad wings, heavy chest. About 22 inches.
Pomarine_Jaeger.Behavior: Pursues other seabirds to steal food. Follows ships. Seen offshore on both coasts during migration. Most common large jaeger.
Pomarine_Jaeger.Habitat: Breeds on Arctic tundra. Pelagic outside breeding season. Regular offshore both coasts during migration.
Pomarine_Jaeger.Similar Looking Birds: Parasitic Jaeger smaller and slimmer. Spoon-shaped tail projection distinctive.
Pomarine_Jaeger.Best Ways to Identify: Twisted blunt-tipped central tail feathers in breeding. Heavy-chested compared to Parasitic Jaeger. Yellow neck on light morph.

Poo-uli.Description: Small Hawaiian honeycreeper, dark brown above with black mask, pale buff-white below. Short thick bill. About 5.5 inches.
Poo-uli.Behavior: Foraged for snails in dense native forest. Last individual died in captivity in 2004. Fastest extinction of a modern bird.
Poo-uli.Habitat: Dense wet native forest on the slopes of Haleakala, Maui. Extinct due to habitat loss and avian disease.
Poo-uli.Similar Looking Birds: No similar bird. Unique among Hawaiian honeycreepers with its snail-eating habits and black mask.
Poo-uli.Best Ways to Identify: Extinct species. Black mask, brown above, pale below. Short thick bill. Last seen in wild 2004 on Maui.

Prairie_Falcon.Description: Sandy-brown falcon with white cheeks, thin dark mustache, dark axillaries, and dark wing linings.
Prairie_Falcon.Behavior: Hunts ground squirrels and birds by flying low and fast over open terrain.
Prairie_Falcon.Habitat: Open prairies, grasslands, and desert of western North America.
Prairie_Falcon.Similar Looking Birds: Peregrine Falcon has slate-blue back and heavy mustache; Prairie is sandy with thin mustache.
Prairie_Falcon.Best Ways to Identify: Sandy-brown with narrow mustache and distinctive black axillaries visible in flight.

Prairie_Warbler.Description: Yellow warbler with chestnut streaks on back, black streaks on sides, and black-and-yellow face pattern.
Prairie_Warbler.Behavior: Bobs tail constantly. Sings ascending buzzy zee-zee-zee-zee-zee.
Prairie_Warbler.Habitat: Shrubby fields, young pines, and mangrove edges in eastern North America.
Prairie_Warbler.Similar Looking Birds: Palm Warbler has rufous cap; Prairie has face pattern and back streaks.
Prairie_Warbler.Best Ways to Identify: Tail-bobbing, face pattern with black streaks, and chestnut back streaks.

Prothonotary_Warbler.Description: Brilliant golden-yellow head and breast, blue-gray wings, and white underparts. Cavity nester.
Prothonotary_Warbler.Behavior: Only eastern warbler that nests in cavities over water. Loud sweet-sweet song.
Prothonotary_Warbler.Habitat: Wooded swamps and flooded bottomlands in the southeastern United States.
Prothonotary_Warbler.Similar Looking Birds: Yellow Warbler lacks blue-gray wings; Blue-winged has yellow with black eye line.
Prothonotary_Warbler.Best Ways to Identify: Golden-yellow head and breast with blue-gray wings in flooded swamp forests.

Providence_Petrel.Description: Large dark brown gadfly petrel with white primary patch on underwing. About 16 inches.
Providence_Petrel.Behavior: Breeds on Lord Howe and Norfolk Islands. Forages North Pacific in non-breeding season; occasional vagrant to Pacific coast.
Providence_Petrel.Habitat: North Pacific in non-breeding season; breeds on Australian subantarctic islands. Rare vagrant to Pacific coast.
Providence_Petrel.Similar Looking Birds: Murphy's Petrel similar but smaller and paler. Providence Petrel larger and darker overall.
Providence_Petrel.Best Ways to Identify: Large dark petrel with white primary bases visible from below. North Pacific in non-breeding season.

Puaiohi.Description: Small Hawaiian thrush, brown above, gray below, pink legs, white eye ring. About 6.5 inches.
Puaiohi.Behavior: Critically endangered. Forages for fruit and insects along steep stream banks. Captive breeding program underway.
Puaiohi.Habitat: Steep stream valleys in native wet forest of Kauai. Very few individuals remain in small area.
Puaiohi.Similar Looking Birds: Kamao larger, now extinct. Omao on Big Island. Pink legs distinctive among Hawaiian thrushes.
Puaiohi.Best Ways to Identify: Pink legs, white eye ring, small size. Kauai native wet forest stream valleys only. Critically endangered.

Purple_Finch.Description: Male is raspberry-red washed over head, back, and underparts. Female is heavily streaked brown.
Purple_Finch.Behavior: Males give rich warbling song. Irruptive migrant following seed crop abundance.
Purple_Finch.Habitat: Coniferous and mixed forests; irrupts to more southern states in winter.
Purple_Finch.Similar Looking Birds: House Finch male has red chest only; Purple Finch male is raspberry-washed overall.
Purple_Finch.Best Ways to Identify: Male is dipped in raspberry juice — uniformly wine-red rather than orange-red like House Finch.

Purple_Gallinule.Description: Stunning bird with purple-blue underparts, green back, red-and-yellow bill, and yellow-green legs.
Purple_Gallinule.Behavior: Walks on floating vegetation and lily pads. Climbs into shrubs to roost.
Purple_Gallinule.Habitat: Freshwater marshes with dense floating vegetation in southeastern United States.
Purple_Gallinule.Similar Looking Birds: Common Gallinule has red frontal shield and gray body; Purple Gallinule is blue-purple.
Purple_Gallinule.Best Ways to Identify: Purple-blue underparts, green back, and rainbow-colored bill and legs — unmistakable.

Purple_Martin.Description: Largest swallow. Male is all-dark glossy blue-black. Female has whitish belly and gray collar.
Purple_Martin.Behavior: Highly colonial, nesting almost exclusively in martin houses in eastern North America.
Purple_Martin.Habitat: Open areas near water; nests in multi-unit martin houses across eastern North America.
Purple_Martin.Similar Looking Birds: Tree Swallow is green-and-white; Purple Martin male is the only all-dark large swallow.
Purple_Martin.Best Ways to Identify: Largest swallow — male is entirely glossy blue-black.

Purple_Sandpiper.Description: Stocky sandpiper with slate-gray plumage, orange-yellow bill base and legs, and purple gloss in fresh plumage.
Purple_Sandpiper.Behavior: Forages on wave-washed rocky coasts and jetties in winter. Very tame.
Purple_Sandpiper.Habitat: Rocky seacoasts and jetties along the Atlantic coast in winter.
Purple_Sandpiper.Similar Looking Birds: Rock Sandpiper is the Pacific counterpart; Purple Sandpiper stays on Atlantic rocky shores.
Purple_Sandpiper.Best Ways to Identify: Dark gray with yellowish bill base, found only on rocky Atlantic shorelines in winter.

Pygmy_Nuthatch.Description: Tiny nuthatch with gray-brown cap, blue-gray back, pale underparts, and white spot on nape.
Pygmy_Nuthatch.Behavior: Highly social; roosts communally in cavities. Forages in flocks at treetops.
Pygmy_Nuthatch.Habitat: Ponderosa pine forests of western mountains.
Pygmy_Nuthatch.Similar Looking Birds: Red-breasted Nuthatch has rust-colored underparts; Pygmy is tiny with brown cap.
Pygmy_Nuthatch.Best Ways to Identify: Tiniest nuthatch — brown cap, communal roosting, and acrobatic foraging at pine treetops.

Pyrrhuloxia.Description: Desert cardinal; male gray with red tinges on crest, wings, and tail; stubby curved yellow parrot-like bill.
Pyrrhuloxia.Behavior: Forages for seeds and insects in desert scrub; sings rich whistled phrases; often in pairs or small flocks.
Pyrrhuloxia.Habitat: Thorny desert scrub, mesquite thickets, and brushy desert washes of southwestern US and northern Mexico.
Pyrrhuloxia.Similar Looking Birds: Northern Cardinal male is all red; female Cardinal has orange bill; both have less curved bills than Pyrrhuloxia.
Pyrrhuloxia.Best Ways to Identify: Curved yellow bill; gray body with red accents on crest and wings; male's red face mask; desert habitat.

Razorbill.Description: Medium alcid. Black above, white below, distinctive deep laterally compressed bill with white line. About 17 inches.
Razorbill.Behavior: Dives for fish. Swims underwater using wings. Breeds in North Atlantic; winters offshore. Regular winter visitor on Atlantic coast.
Razorbill.Habitat: Breeds on rocky Atlantic islands and cliffs. Winters offshore in North Atlantic. Regular winter visitor to Atlantic coast.
Razorbill.Similar Looking Birds: Common Murre similar size but has thinner bill. Razorbill's deep compressed bill distinctive.
Razorbill.Best Ways to Identify: Deep blade-like bill with white cross-stripe distinctive. Thicker bill compared to murres. Atlantic species.

Red-backed_Shrike.Description: Medium shrike. Male has gray head, chestnut back, black mask. Female brown with barred underparts. About 7 inches.
Red-backed_Shrike.Behavior: Hunts from exposed perches, diving on insects, lizards, and small birds. Impales prey on thorns. Rare vagrant.
Red-backed_Shrike.Habitat: Open country with scattered bushes and thorns in Europe and Asia. Very rare vagrant to northeastern North America.
Red-backed_Shrike.Similar Looking Birds: Brown Shrike lacks gray head in male. Loggerhead Shrike much larger, gray above with heavy hooked bill.
Red-backed_Shrike.Best Ways to Identify: Male: gray head plus chestnut back distinctive. Female: brown with scalloped pattern. Very rare vagrant from Eurasia.

Red-bellied_Woodpecker.Description: Medium woodpecker with red cap and nape on male, black-and-white barred back, and pale belly with faint red tinge.
Red-bellied_Woodpecker.Behavior: Loud churr-churr call. Caches food in bark crevices.
Red-bellied_Woodpecker.Habitat: Deciduous forests and suburbs of eastern North America.
Red-bellied_Woodpecker.Similar Looking Birds: Red-headed Woodpecker has all-red head; Red-bellied has red only on cap and nape.
Red-bellied_Woodpecker.Best Ways to Identify: Barred black-and-white back, red cap and nape on male, and faint reddish belly wash.

Red-billed_Leiothrix.Description: Small colorful bird, olive-green back, yellow-orange throat and breast, red bill, red and yellow in wing. About 5.5 inches.
Red-billed_Leiothrix.Behavior: Active and noisy in dense undergrowth. Beautiful melodious song. Introduced to Hawaii and present in forests.
Red-billed_Leiothrix.Habitat: Dense forest understory and scrub. Introduced to Hawaiian Islands, found on several islands in native forests.
Red-billed_Leiothrix.Similar Looking Birds: No similar bird in Hawaii. Colorful combination of yellow, orange, and red with olive-green back unique.
Red-billed_Leiothrix.Best Ways to Identify: Red bill, yellow-orange underparts, colorful wing pattern. Olive-green back. Melodious song. Hawaiian introduced species.

Red-billed_Pigeon.Description: Medium pigeon. Dark maroon-red head, neck and breast, darker brown back, pale gray belly. Bright red bill with yellow tip. About 14 inches.
Red-billed_Pigeon.Behavior: Feeds on berries, seeds, and fruit in tree canopy. Usually found in pairs or small flocks. Year-round resident in southern Texas Rio Grande Valley.
Red-billed_Pigeon.Habitat: Dense riparian forest and woodland edges along lower Rio Grande in Texas. Common in Mexico and Central America.
Red-billed_Pigeon.Similar Looking Birds: Band-tailed Pigeon larger with different bill. No other large red-billed pigeon in range.
Red-billed_Pigeon.Best Ways to Identify: All-dark maroon-red body with distinctly bright red bill. Slightly larger than Mourning Dove. Found in dense riverside forest in South Texas.

Red-billed_Tropicbird.Description: White seabird with brilliant red bill, black-barred back, very long white tail streamers, black eye stripe. About 40 inches with tail.
Red-billed_Tropicbird.Behavior: Plunge-dives for fish and squid. Nests in cliff crevices on tropical islands. Rare offshore in Atlantic and Pacific.
Red-billed_Tropicbird.Habitat: Tropical Atlantic and Pacific oceans. Breeds on Caribbean and eastern Pacific islands. Occasional offshore Atlantic coast.
Red-billed_Tropicbird.Similar Looking Birds: White-tailed Tropicbird similar but has yellow or orange bill. Red bill of this species diagnostic.
Red-billed_Tropicbird.Best Ways to Identify: Brilliant red bill most distinctive feature. White tail streamers, barred back. Rare but striking offshore seabird.

Red-breasted_Merganser.Description: Diving duck with shaggy double crest, red serrated bill, and white neck ring on male.
Red-breasted_Merganser.Behavior: Dives in coastal waters for fish. Fast flier in low lines over water.
Red-breasted_Merganser.Habitat: Coastal bays and large lakes; breeds near water in boreal regions.
Red-breasted_Merganser.Similar Looking Birds: Common Merganser male has smooth green head; Red-breasted has shaggy crest and streaked breast.
Red-breasted_Merganser.Best Ways to Identify: Shaggy double crest, red serrated bill, and rusty streaked breast on male.

Red-breasted_Nuthatch.Description: Small nuthatch with black cap, white supercilium, blue-gray back, and rusty-orange underparts.
Red-breasted_Nuthatch.Behavior: Irruptive migrant; moves south in large numbers when conifer cone crops fail.
Red-breasted_Nuthatch.Habitat: Coniferous forests; irruptive visitor to parks and feeders in irruption years.
Red-breasted_Nuthatch.Similar Looking Birds: White-breasted Nuthatch is larger with white underparts; Red-breasted has rusty belly.
Red-breasted_Nuthatch.Best Ways to Identify: Rusty-orange underparts and bold white eyebrow on blue-gray nuthatch.

Red-breasted_Sapsucker.Description: Woodpecker with entirely red head and breast, black and white back pattern. White wing patch in flight. About 8 inches.
Red-breasted_Sapsucker.Behavior: Drills rows of sap wells in trees. Common in Pacific coast forests from Alaska to Baja California.
Red-breasted_Sapsucker.Habitat: Conifer and mixed forest along Pacific coast. Breeds in mountains; moves to lower elevations in winter.
Red-breasted_Sapsucker.Similar Looking Birds: Yellow-bellied and Red-naped Sapsuckers have partial red. Red-breasted has entirely red head.
Red-breasted_Sapsucker.Best Ways to Identify: Entirely red head and breast. White wing patch. Pacific coast and western mountain forest sapsucker.

Red-cockaded_Woodpecker.Description: Small woodpecker with large white cheek patch, black cap and nape, barred back, and tiny red cockade on males.
Red-cockaded_Woodpecker.Behavior: Excavates nest cavities only in living longleaf pines. Lives in cooperative family groups.
Red-cockaded_Woodpecker.Habitat: Old-growth longleaf pine savannas of the southeastern United States.
Red-cockaded_Woodpecker.Similar Looking Birds: Hairy and Downy have unbarred black-and-white backs; Red-cockaded has barred back.
Red-cockaded_Woodpecker.Best Ways to Identify: Large white cheek patch on barred-back woodpecker in old longleaf pine forest.

Red-crested_Cardinal.Description: Medium bird, brilliant red crest and face, gray above, white below. Bold and distinctive. About 7.5 inches.
Red-crested_Cardinal.Behavior: Bold and conspicuous in open areas. Forages on ground for seeds. Introduced to Hawaii; very common.
Red-crested_Cardinal.Habitat: Open areas, gardens, and parks. Introduced to Hawaii; very common on several islands.
Red-crested_Cardinal.Similar Looking Birds: Northern Cardinal has all-red body on male. Yellow-billed Cardinal lacks gray back.
Red-crested_Cardinal.Best Ways to Identify: Brilliant red crest and face contrasting with gray back and white belly. Very common in Hawaii.

Red-crowned_Amazon.Description: Medium parrot, green with red crown and lores, blue behind eye, yellowish face. About 13 inches.
Red-crowned_Amazon.Behavior: Endangered in Mexico; established feral populations in California and southern Texas. Loud flocking calls.
Red-crowned_Amazon.Habitat: Feral in Los Angeles, San Diego, and Rio Grande Valley, Texas. Endangered in native Mexican range.
Red-crowned_Amazon.Similar Looking Birds: Lilac-crowned Amazon has lilac on crown. Red-crowned has brighter red crown patch.
Red-crowned_Amazon.Best Ways to Identify: Red crown patch, blue behind eye. Green parrot. Established feral populations in California and Texas.

Red-eyed_Vireo.Description: Medium vireo with red eye, gray cap, white supercilium, dark eye line, olive back, and white underparts.
Red-eyed_Vireo.Behavior: Sings persistently all summer long — one of the most tireless singers. Stays in tree canopy.
Red-eyed_Vireo.Habitat: Deciduous forests across eastern North America; one of the most common forest birds.
Red-eyed_Vireo.Similar Looking Birds: Blue-headed Vireo has bold white spectacles and wing bars; Red-eyed is plainer.
Red-eyed_Vireo.Best Ways to Identify: Red eye, gray cap, and white supercilium with dark eye line — sings endlessly from treetops.

Red-faced_Cormorant.Description: Medium cormorant, dark glossy green-black plumage with bright red-orange facial skin. About 28 inches.
Red-faced_Cormorant.Behavior: Dives for fish. Breeds on Aleutian Islands and Alaskan rocky coasts. Common in Alaskan waters.
Red-faced_Cormorant.Habitat: Alaskan waters; breeds on rocky Aleutian Islands. Western Alaska, not found in lower 48 states.
Red-faced_Cormorant.Similar Looking Birds: Pelagic Cormorant in same range. Red-faced has much broader red facial skin.
Red-faced_Cormorant.Best Ways to Identify: Broad red-orange facial skin around eye and base of bill. Dark glossy plumage. Western Alaska species.

Red-faced_Warbler.Description: Gray warbler with brilliant red-and-black head pattern and white nape patch.
Red-faced_Warbler.Behavior: Forages actively in pine-oak forest, often hanging from branch tips.
Red-faced_Warbler.Habitat: Mountain pine-oak forests of southeastern Arizona and New Mexico.
Red-faced_Warbler.Similar Looking Birds: Painted Redstart has red breast; Red-faced Warbler has red face with black borders.
Red-faced_Warbler.Best Ways to Identify: Red face bordered by black with white nape patch — brilliant in its mountain forest.

Red-flanked_Bluetail.Description: Small chat. Male blue above with orange-red flanks, white belly. Female brown with blue tail. About 5.5 inches.
Red-flanked_Bluetail.Behavior: Skulks in dense vegetation but perches openly. Flicks tail. Increasingly regular vagrant to western Alaska.
Red-flanked_Bluetail.Habitat: Coniferous forest of Siberia and East Asia. Regular vagrant to western Alaska and Aleutian Islands.
Red-flanked_Bluetail.Similar Looking Birds: Bluethroat has blue throat, breeds in Alaska. No other bird with orange flanks and blue tail in Alaska.
Red-flanked_Bluetail.Best Ways to Identify: Orange-red flanks contrasting with blue tail. Male blue above. Increasingly regular Alaska fall vagrant.

Red-footed_Booby.Description: Small booby with bright red feet. Polymorphic: white morph white with black wings; brown morph all brown. About 28 inches.
Red-footed_Booby.Behavior: Only tree-nesting booby; breeds in shrubs. Plunge-dives for fish and squid. Breeds on Hawaiian islands; forages offshore.
Red-footed_Booby.Habitat: Tropical Pacific and Atlantic. Breeds on Hawaiian Northwestern Islands; forages in tropical Pacific.
Red-footed_Booby.Similar Looking Birds: Brown Booby has yellow feet. Red-footed Booby's bright red feet diagnostic.
Red-footed_Booby.Best Ways to Identify: Bright red feet and legs distinctive. White morph most common; brown morph also occurs. Only booby that nests in trees.

Red-footed_Falcon.Description: Small falcon. Male dark gray with red feet and vent; female rufous with gray back and barred underparts. About 11 inches.
Red-footed_Falcon.Behavior: Highly migratory; feeds on insects. Very rare vagrant from Europe/Asia to Atlantic coast of North America.
Red-footed_Falcon.Habitat: Open farmland and steppe of Europe and Central Asia. Very rare vagrant to Atlantic coast.
Red-footed_Falcon.Similar Looking Birds: Merlin similar size. Red-footed Falcon male's all-gray body with red feet distinctive.
Red-footed_Falcon.Best Ways to Identify: Male: dark gray with red feet. Female: rufous with barred underparts. Very rare Atlantic vagrant from Europe.

Red-headed_Woodpecker.Description: Striking woodpecker with entirely crimson-red head, pure white body, and large white wing patches.
Red-headed_Woodpecker.Behavior: Catches insects in flight like a flycatcher. Stores food under bark.
Red-headed_Woodpecker.Habitat: Open woodlands with large trees, orchards, and snags in eastern North America.
Red-headed_Woodpecker.Similar Looking Birds: Red-bellied has red only on cap; Red-headed has entire head red with white body.
Red-headed_Woodpecker.Best Ways to Identify: Entire head is brilliant red — only North American woodpecker with this pattern.

Red-legged_Honeycreeper.Description: Small bird. Male brilliant blue with black back and wings, red legs, yellow underwing. Female greenish. About 4.5 inches.
Red-legged_Honeycreeper.Behavior: Probes flowers for nectar with curved bill. Forages in fruiting trees. Rare vagrant to Texas from Mexico.
Red-legged_Honeycreeper.Habitat: Tropical forest and woodland from Mexico to South America. Rare vagrant to southern Texas.
Red-legged_Honeycreeper.Similar Looking Birds: Indigo Bunting has different bill. Shining Honeycreeper similar. Red legs distinctive.
Red-legged_Honeycreeper.Best Ways to Identify: Male brilliant blue with black wings and red legs. Yellow underwing in flight. Rare Texas vagrant.

Red-legged_Kittiwake.Description: Medium gull. White with gray back, black wingtips, red legs (not yellow). Short yellow bill. About 15 inches.
Red-legged_Kittiwake.Behavior: Pelagic; breeds on steep Alaskan cliff islands. Forages over Bering Sea. Less common than Black-legged Kittiwake.
Red-legged_Kittiwake.Habitat: Breeds on Pribilof and Aleutian Islands in Bering Sea. Winters offshore in North Pacific.
Red-legged_Kittiwake.Similar Looking Birds: Black-legged Kittiwake nearly identical but has yellow legs and is far more common.
Red-legged_Kittiwake.Best Ways to Identify: Red legs diagnostic; Black-legged Kittiwake has yellow legs. Shorter bill. Breeds mainly on Pribilof Islands.

Red-legged_Thrush.Description: Medium thrush, blue-gray above, white throat with black streaks, orange-red bill and legs. About 10.5 inches.
Red-legged_Thrush.Behavior: Forages on ground for fruit and invertebrates. Bold in parks and gardens. Rare vagrant to Florida from Bahamas.
Red-legged_Thrush.Habitat: Forest, gardens, and parks of the Bahamas and Caribbean. Rare vagrant to southern Florida.
Red-legged_Thrush.Similar Looking Birds: American Robin has red breast. Blue-gray plumage distinctive. Red legs unique among thrushes in range.
Red-legged_Thrush.Best Ways to Identify: Red-orange legs distinctive. Blue-gray overall with white throat. Florida vagrant from the Bahamas.

Red-lored_Amazon.Description: Large parrot, green with red forehead and lores, yellow cheeks, blue crown. About 13 inches.
Red-lored_Amazon.Behavior: Highly gregarious, noisy in flocks. Forages for fruit and seeds. Feral populations in California and Florida.
Red-lored_Amazon.Habitat: Tropical forest and urban areas. Feral populations in southern California and Florida.
Red-lored_Amazon.Similar Looking Birds: Yellow-headed Amazon has yellow head. Red-crowned Amazon has red crown only. Red lores distinctive.
Red-lored_Amazon.Best Ways to Identify: Red forehead and lores with yellow cheeks. Green parrot. Feral in California and Florida suburbs.

Red-masked_Parakeet.Description: Large green parakeet with extensive red on head extending behind eye. Long tail. About 13 inches.
Red-masked_Parakeet.Behavior: Established feral populations in San Francisco and San Diego. Often mixes with other feral parakeets.
Red-masked_Parakeet.Habitat: Feral in San Francisco Bay Area and San Diego in suburban habitats. Also feral in Florida.
Red-masked_Parakeet.Similar Looking Birds: Mitred Parakeet similar but less red on head. Red-masked has extensive red face mask.
Red-masked_Parakeet.Best Ways to Identify: Extensive red mask on face and head. Green body. Feral in San Francisco Bay Area and San Diego.

Red-naped_Sapsucker.Description: Black-and-white woodpecker with red crown, nape, and chin on male; red crown and nape on female.
Red-naped_Sapsucker.Behavior: Drills rows of sap wells in trees and returns to feed on sap and trapped insects.
Red-naped_Sapsucker.Habitat: Aspen and riparian forests of the Rocky Mountains.
Red-naped_Sapsucker.Similar Looking Birds: Yellow-bellied Sapsucker has white nasal tufts and no red nape; Red-naped has red nape.
Red-naped_Sapsucker.Best Ways to Identify: Red crown and nape, sap well rows in aspen trees of the Rocky Mountain region.

Red-necked_Grebe.Description: Medium grebe with rich rusty-red neck, black cap, white cheeks, and yellow-and-black bill.
Red-necked_Grebe.Behavior: Dives for fish and invertebrates. Often seen in large flocks on open water in winter.
Red-necked_Grebe.Habitat: Large lakes and coastal bays; breeds on boreal lakes.
Red-necked_Grebe.Similar Looking Birds: Horned Grebe is smaller with golden ear tufts; Red-necked is larger with rusty neck.
Red-necked_Grebe.Best Ways to Identify: Rusty-red neck, white cheek, and yellow-based bill — larger than other grebes.

Red-necked_Phalarope.Description: Small shorebird. Breeding female has rusty neck patches and gray back. Spins on water surface.
Red-necked_Phalarope.Behavior: Females are more colorful; males incubate eggs and raise young. Spins to stir up plankton.
Red-necked_Phalarope.Habitat: Breeds on Arctic tundra; winters on ocean. Migrates through inland lakes.
Red-necked_Phalarope.Similar Looking Birds: Red Phalarope is larger with brick-red neck; Red-necked has thinner neck patches.
Red-necked_Phalarope.Best Ways to Identify: Spins on water surface, rusty neck patches, and reversed sex roles in breeding.

Red-necked_Stint.Description: Very small sandpiper. Breeding adult has reddish-orange face and upper breast. Non-breeding gray above, white below. About 6 inches.
Red-necked_Stint.Behavior: Forages on mudflats picking small invertebrates. Regular migrant through western Alaska; rare on Pacific coast.
Red-necked_Stint.Habitat: Breeds on Arctic Siberian tundra. Migrates through western Alaska. Winters on Southeast Asian and Australian coasts.
Red-necked_Stint.Similar Looking Birds: Semipalmated Sandpiper similar in non-breeding. Red- necked has rufous face and breast in summer.
Red-necked_Stint.Best Ways to Identify: Rufous-orange face and breast in breeding plumage. Non-breeding very similar to Semipalmated. Rare on Pacific coast.

Red-shouldered_Hawk.Description: Medium hawk with rusty-orange barred underparts, reddish shoulders, and checkered black-and-white wings.
Red-shouldered_Hawk.Behavior: Calls loudly kee-ahh in forest. Often seen near wetlands and streams.
Red-shouldered_Hawk.Habitat: Forests near streams and wet areas in eastern North America and California.
Red-shouldered_Hawk.Similar Looking Birds: Red-tailed Hawk has solid belly band; Red-shouldered has barred rusty underparts.
Red-shouldered_Hawk.Best Ways to Identify: Rusty barred underparts, checkered wings, and loud kee-ahh call in forested wetlands.

Red-tailed_Hawk.Description: Most common and widespread hawk. Adults have a distinctive brick-red tail, dark back, and belly band.
Red-tailed_Hawk.Behavior: Soars over open country. Perches on utility poles and fence posts.
Red-tailed_Hawk.Habitat: Almost every habitat from forests to deserts across North America.
Red-tailed_Hawk.Similar Looking Birds: Red-shouldered has barred underparts; Ferruginous has all-white belly; Red-tailed has belly band.
Red-tailed_Hawk.Best Ways to Identify: Brick-red tail on adults visible from below — the most common soaring hawk in North America.

Red-tailed_Tropicbird.Description: White seabird with red tail streamers, red bill, very clean white plumage with limited black markings. About 37 inches.
Red-tailed_Tropicbird.Behavior: Plunge-dives for fish. Breeds on Hawaiian and Pacific islands. Nests in burrows or cliff crevices.
Red-tailed_Tropicbird.Habitat: Tropical Pacific Ocean. Breeds on Hawaiian Northwest Islands and other Pacific tropical islands. Offshore Pacific waters.
Red-tailed_Tropicbird.Similar Looking Birds: White-tailed Tropicbird has white tail and more black. Red-tailed has clean white body and red streamers.
Red-tailed_Tropicbird.Best Ways to Identify: Red tail streamers on very white body. Minimal black markings. Pacific species. Cleanest-looking of the tropicbirds.

Red-throated_Loon.Description: Smallest loon with thin upturned bill and rusty-red throat patch in breeding. Gray head with striped nape.
Red-throated_Loon.Behavior: Can take flight from land without a running start, unlike other loons.
Red-throated_Loon.Habitat: Arctic tundra lakes in summer; winters along coasts.
Red-throated_Loon.Similar Looking Birds: Pacific and Common Loons have heavier bills; Red-throated has slim upturned bill.
Red-throated_Loon.Best Ways to Identify: Slim upturned bill, smallest loon, and rusty throat patch in breeding plumage.

Red-throated_Pipit.Description: Small pipit, heavily streaked above, pinkish-red throat and breast in breeding. About 6 inches.
Red-throated_Pipit.Behavior: Forages on open ground and tundra. Breeds in arctic tundra of Alaska. Migrates to Asia in fall.
Red-throated_Pipit.Habitat: Open tundra, wet meadows, and arctic grassland in Alaska. Winters in Southeast Asia.
Red-throated_Pipit.Similar Looking Birds: Olive-backed Pipit lacks reddish throat. American Pipit more uniform below in fall. Red throat distinctive in spring.
Red-throated_Pipit.Best Ways to Identify: Reddish throat and breast in breeding. Heavily streaked in fall. Alaska tundra breeder. Long-distance migrant to Asia.

Red-vented_Bulbul.Description: Medium songbird, brown-black with scaly pattern, white rump, red undertail coverts. Pointed crest. About 9 inches.
Red-vented_Bulbul.Behavior: Noisy and bold, often near human habitation. Invasive species in Hawaii, eating fruit and damaging crops.
Red-vented_Bulbul.Habitat: Introduced to Oahu and Maui, Hawaii. Scrub, forest edges, and urban areas. Invasive, spreading from original native range in South Asia.
Red-vented_Bulbul.Similar Looking Birds: Red-whiskered Bulbul has red cheek patch and longer crest. Common in same Hawaii habitats.
Red-vented_Bulbul.Best Ways to Identify: Red undertail coverts, white rump, scaly brown-black pattern, pointed crest. Invasive in Hawaii. Very noisy.

Red-whiskered_Bulbul.Description: Medium songbird with tall pointed black crest, white face with red cheek spot, red undertail coverts. About 8 inches.
Red-whiskered_Bulbul.Behavior: Noisy and conspicuous in suburbs. Eats fruit and insects. Invasive in Florida and Hawaii.
Red-whiskered_Bulbul.Habitat: Suburban gardens, parks, and forest edges. Introduced populations in southern Florida and Hawaii.
Red-whiskered_Bulbul.Similar Looking Birds: Red-vented Bulbul lacks red cheek patch and has more uniform brown-black plumage.
Red-whiskered_Bulbul.Best Ways to Identify: Red cheek spot and tall black crest unique. Red undertail coverts. Invasive in south Florida and Hawaii.

Red-winged_Blackbird.Description: Male is all black with brilliant red-and-yellow shoulder patches. Female is brown and streaked.
Red-winged_Blackbird.Behavior: Males display shoulder patches prominently. One of the most abundant birds in North America.
Red-winged_Blackbird.Habitat: Marshes, wet fields, and roadsides across North America.
Red-winged_Blackbird.Similar Looking Birds: No other blackbird has red-and-yellow shoulder patches on all-black body.
Red-winged_Blackbird.Best Ways to Identify: All-black with red-and-yellow shoulder patches on male — among the most common birds.

Red_Avadavat.Description: Tiny finch. Male brilliant red with white spots throughout, red bill. Female brown with red bill and rump. About 4 inches.
Red_Avadavat.Behavior: Highly gregarious in flocks. Forages for grass seeds. Introduced to Hawaii and Puerto Rico.
Red_Avadavat.Habitat: Grasslands and open areas. Introduced to Hawaii and Puerto Rico. Native to India and Southeast Asia.
Red_Avadavat.Similar Looking Birds: No other tiny red bird with white spots in Hawaii. Unique pattern.
Red_Avadavat.Best Ways to Identify: Brilliant red with white spots and red bill. Tiny size. Gregarious. Introduced to Hawaii.

Red_Crossbill.Description: Medium finch. Male brick-red with dark wings. Female olive-green. Bill tips visibly crossed. About 6 inches.
Red_Crossbill.Behavior: Uses crossed bill to pry open conifer cones. Nomadic, following cone crops across North America.
Red_Crossbill.Habitat: Coniferous forests across North America and Eurasia. Nomadic following cone crop availability.
Red_Crossbill.Similar Looking Birds: White-winged Crossbill has white wing bars. Cassia Crossbill similar but restricted to Cassia County, Idaho.
Red_Crossbill.Best Ways to Identify: Crossed bill tips visible in field. Male brick-red. Female olive-green. Nomadic in conifer forests.

Red_Junglefowl.Description: Ancestor of domestic chicken. Male has brilliant red and orange plumage, red comb and wattles, arched iridescent green-black tail. Female brown. About 17 inches.
Red_Junglefowl.Behavior: Forages on forest floor for seeds, insects, and fruit. Male crows loudly. Feral populations established in Hawaii from escaped domestic birds.
Red_Junglefowl.Habitat: South and Southeast Asian forests. In US found in Hawaii as feral birds, particularly on Kauai where they roam freely.
Red_Junglefowl.Similar Looking Birds: Domestic chickens are direct descendants; identical to wild type males.
Red_Junglefowl.Best Ways to Identify: Male's red comb, orange-red hackles, dark iridescent tail. Female similar to domestic hen. Wild birds slimmer than domestic chickens.

Red_Knot.Description: Medium chunky sandpiper. Breeding adult has rusty-red underparts and mottled reddish-gray back.
Red_Knot.Behavior: Makes one of the longest migrations — from Arctic to Tierra del Fuego and back.
Red_Knot.Habitat: Coastal beaches and mudflats during migration; Arctic tundra for breeding.
Red_Knot.Similar Looking Birds: Dunlin has drooping bill tip; Dowitcher is larger; Red Knot is stocky with straight bill.
Red_Knot.Best Ways to Identify: Stocky medium sandpiper with rusty-red underparts in breeding — one of longest migrations.

Red_Phalarope.Description: Medium phalarope. Breeding female has brick-red body, white face, yellow bill. Non-breeding gray above, white below. About 8.5 inches.
Red_Phalarope.Behavior: Swims in offshore waters spinning to stir up plankton. Roles reversed; female more colorful. Common offshore in fall migration.
Red_Phalarope.Habitat: Breeds on High Arctic tundra. Pelagic in non-breeding season. Seen offshore during migration; rarely near shore.
Red_Phalarope.Similar Looking Birds: Red-necked Phalarope thinner-billed. Breeding Red Phalarope is red below.
Red_Phalarope.Best Ways to Identify: Breeding female unmistakable red below with white face. Non-breeding gray above with thick yellow-based bill.

Reddish_Egret.Description: Medium egret. Dark morph: slate gray with rufous head and neck. White morph: all white. Both have pink-based dark bill. About 30 inches.
Reddish_Egret.Behavior: Active and agile forager; rushes and dances while hunting fish. Coastal specialist. Gulf Coast and Caribbean.
Reddish_Egret.Habitat: Coastal lagoons, mangroves, and tidal flats of Gulf Coast and Florida. Also Caribbean.
Reddish_Egret.Similar Looking Birds: Dark morph: distinctive. White morph: similar to other white egrets but has pink-based dark bill.
Reddish_Egret.Best Ways to Identify: Pink-based dark bill diagnostic. Dark morph uniquely slate-gray with rufous neck. Active dancing feeding behavior.

Redhead.Description: Diving duck. Male has chestnut-red head, gray body, and blue-gray bill. Female is brown with blue-gray bill.
Redhead.Behavior: Often parasitizes other duck nests by laying eggs for others to raise.
Redhead.Habitat: Freshwater lakes and coastal bays across North America.
Redhead.Similar Looking Birds: Canvasback has rusty-red head but also has sloping forehead and black bill.
Redhead.Best Ways to Identify: Round red head and blue-gray bill on male — contrasts with Canvasback's sloping profile.

Redpoll.Description: Small finch, streaked brown with red forehead patch, pinkish-red breast in male, small yellow bill. About 5 inches.
Redpoll.Behavior: Irruptive species, invades southern areas when birch seed crop fails. Forages in birch and alder trees.
Redpoll.Habitat: Boreal forest and arctic scrub across North America and Eurasia. Irruptive winter visitor to northern states.
Redpoll.Similar Looking Birds: Common and Hoary Redpolls nearly identical. Pine Siskin has yellow wing stripe. Red forehead spot helpful.
Redpoll.Best Ways to Identify: Red forehead, pink breast on male. Streaked brown. Irruptive visitor to birch trees in winter.

Redwing.Description: Medium thrush, brown above with bold creamy supercilium, heavily streaked breast, red-orange underwing and flank patch. About 8.5 inches.
Redwing.Behavior: Travels in flocks, foraging for berries in winter. Rare but annual vagrant to northeastern North America from Europe.
Redwing.Habitat: Open woodland, parks, and berry-bearing scrub in Europe. Rare vagrant to Atlantic coast of North America.
Redwing.Similar Looking Birds: Song Thrush has spots not streaks below, lacks red flank patch. Fieldfare has gray head.
Redwing.Best Ways to Identify: Red-orange flank patch and underwing distinctive. Bold creamy supercilium. Streaked breast. Rare European vagrant.

Reed_Bunting.Description: Medium bunting. Male has black head and throat with white collar. Female streaked brown. About 6 inches.
Reed_Bunting.Behavior: Inhabits wetlands and reed beds. Sings from reeds. Rare vagrant to western Alaska from Asia.
Reed_Bunting.Habitat: Wetlands, reed beds, and marshes across Europe and Asia. Rare vagrant to western Alaska.
Reed_Bunting.Similar Looking Birds: Pallas's Bunting smaller. Lapland Longspur has chestnut nape. Male pattern distinctive.
Reed_Bunting.Best Ways to Identify: Male black head and throat with white collar. Wetland habitat. Rare Alaska vagrant from Siberia.

Rhinoceros_Auklet.Description: Large alcid. Dark gray-brown above, lighter below. Breeding adult has two white facial plumes and horn-like bill projection. About 15 inches.
Rhinoceros_Auklet.Behavior: Nests in burrows. Brings fish to colony at night. Pelagic outside breeding; found along Pacific coast.
Rhinoceros_Auklet.Habitat: Nests on Pacific coast islands from Alaska to California. Winters offshore along Pacific coast.
Rhinoceros_Auklet.Similar Looking Birds: Tufted Puffin similar size but has orange bill. Rhinoceros Auklet brownish with white plumes.
