Spotted_Dove.Description: Medium dove with pinkish-brown body, long tail, and distinctive black hindneck collar with white spots like a necklace. About 12 inches.
Spotted_Dove.Behavior: Forages on ground for seeds and grain. Found in pairs or small flocks. Introduced from Asia; established in southern California and Hawaii.
Spotted_Dove.Habitat: Urban parks, gardens, agricultural areas, and open woodland. Introduced populations in Los Angeles area and Hawaiian Islands.
Spotted_Dove.Similar Looking Birds: Eurasian Collared-Dove similar size but lacks spotted neck collar. Mourning Dove slimmer.
Spotted_Dove.Best Ways to Identify: Black and white spotted collar on hindneck unique among North American doves. Brown-pink plumage and long rounded tail.

Spotted_Flycatcher.Description: Small flycatcher, gray-brown above with streaked crown, white below with streaked breast. About 5.5 inches.
Spotted_Flycatcher.Behavior: Sallies from upright perch returning to same spot. Rare vagrant to North America from Europe.
Spotted_Flycatcher.Habitat: Open woodland and gardens in Europe and Asia. Very rare vagrant to North America.
Spotted_Flycatcher.Similar Looking Birds: Gray-streaked Flycatcher has gray-brown breast streaking without crown streaking. European vagrant context helpful.
Spotted_Flycatcher.Best Ways to Identify: Streaked crown distinguishes from other Muscicapa flycatchers. Streaked breast. Very rare European vagrant to East Coast.

Spotted_Owl.Description: Medium owl with dark brown plumage and white spots covering breast and belly; dark eyes; no ear tufts; round head.
Spotted_Owl.Behavior: Nocturnal hunter of flying squirrels and woodrats; hooting calls; threatened by Barred Owl competition.
Spotted_Owl.Habitat: Old-growth and mature forests of Pacific Coast and Rocky Mountains; needs large trees and dense canopy.
Spotted_Owl.Similar Looking Birds: Barred Owl has streaked belly and barred breast; Barn Owl is paler with heart-shaped face; larger owls have ear tufts.
Spotted_Owl.Best Ways to Identify: Dark brown with white spots on belly; dark brown eyes; old-growth forest; no ear tufts; round facial disc.

Spotted_Rail.Description: Medium rail. Dark brown with bold white spots on breast and flanks, long red bill with green base, red legs. About 10 inches.
Spotted_Rail.Behavior: Secretive; skulks in dense marsh vegetation. Rarely seen. Rare vagrant to US from Caribbean and South America.
Spotted_Rail.Habitat: Freshwater marshes and wet grasslands in Caribbean, South America, and occasionally Mexico. Rare vagrant to Gulf Coast states.
Spotted_Rail.Similar Looking Birds: Sora and other small rails. Spotted Rail's bold white spots and red bill distinctive.
Spotted_Rail.Best Ways to Identify: Bold white spots on dark brown plumage with bright red bill. Found in dense marsh vegetation. Very secretive.

Spotted_Redshank.Description: Large sandpiper. Breeding adult entirely sooty black with white spots; non-breeding pale gray above, white below. Long red legs. About 12 inches.
Spotted_Redshank.Behavior: Forages by wading and swimming. Rare vagrant to both coasts of North America from Eurasia.
Spotted_Redshank.Habitat: Breeds on Eurasian subarctic tundra. Winters on African and Asian coasts. Rare vagrant to North America.
Spotted_Redshank.Similar Looking Birds: Common Redshank has white wing patches. Breeding Spotted Redshank all-black unmistakable.
Spotted_Redshank.Best Ways to Identify: Breeding adult all-black with white spots unmistakable. Non-breeding pale gray. Long red legs and bill.

Spotted_Sandpiper.Description: Small sandpiper; breeding plumage has bold black spots on white underparts; orange bill; constantly teeters body.
Spotted_Sandpiper.Behavior: Teeters rear end up and down constantly while walking; low stiff-winged flight; polyandrous breeding system.
Spotted_Sandpiper.Habitat: Shorelines of streams, lakes, and rivers throughout North America; very widespread migratory species.
Spotted_Sandpiper.Similar Looking Birds: Solitary Sandpiper bobs but has spotted back and different tail pattern; Common Sandpiper is very similar Eurasian.
Spotted_Sandpiper.Best Ways to Identify: Constant teetering bobbing motion; spotted breast in summer; orange bill with dark tip; stiff shallow wingbeats in flight.

Spotted_Towhee.Description: Large sparrow; male has black hood, white-spotted black back, rufous sides, and white belly; red eye; white corners in tail.
Spotted_Towhee.Behavior: Scratches vigorously in leaf litter with both feet; sings loud 'drink your tea'; dense shrub thicket dweller.
Spotted_Towhee.Habitat: Dense brushy undergrowth, chaparral, and shrubby forest edges of western North America.
Spotted_Towhee.Similar Looking Birds: Eastern Towhee is similar but lacks white spots on back; Rufous-sided Towhee was former combined name.
Spotted_Towhee.Best Ways to Identify: White spots on black back and wings; rufous sides; black hood; red eye; white outer tail corners; ground scratching.

Spragues_Pipit.Description: Buffy streaked pipit with pale face, buffy streaked breast, pale pinkish legs, and white outer tail feathers.
Spragues_Pipit.Behavior: Flies up in spiraling song flight for extended periods; very secretive on ground; walks rather than hops.
Spragues_Pipit.Habitat: Native short and mixed-grass prairies of northern Great Plains; declining due to grassland conversion.
Spragues_Pipit.Similar Looking Birds: American Pipit has gray back and bobs tail; Horned Lark has black face marks; Savannah Sparrow has notched tail.
Spragues_Pipit.Best Ways to Identify: Buffy streaked appearance; pale pinkish legs; white outer tail feathers; extended spiraling song flight over grasslands.

Spruce_Grouse.Description: Chicken-sized grouse with dark plumage. Male has black throat and breast, red eye combs. Female cryptically barred brown. About 16 inches.
Spruce_Grouse.Behavior: Highly confiding; often called "fool hen." Feeds primarily on spruce and fir needles in winter. Year-round resident of boreal forests.
Spruce_Grouse.Habitat: Dense boreal spruce and fir forests of Canada and northern US. Found in wet coniferous forests with dense understory.
Spruce_Grouse.Similar Looking Birds: Sooty and Dusky Grouse in similar western habitats. Male's black and red pattern distinctive.
Spruce_Grouse.Best Ways to Identify: Male's black throat and breast with red eye combs. Female barred brown in spruce forest. Very tame and approachable.

Stejnegers_Petrel.Description: Small gadfly petrel very similar to Cook's Petrel. Darker cap, slightly darker gray above. About 11 inches.
Stejnegers_Petrel.Behavior: Breeds on Juan Fernandez Islands, Chile. Migrates into North Pacific; rare vagrant off California.
Stejnegers_Petrel.Habitat: North Pacific in non-breeding season. Rare vagrant off Pacific coast; breeds on Chilean islands.
Stejnegers_Petrel.Similar Looking Birds: Cook's Petrel almost identical. Stejneger's has darker gray cap contrasting with back.
Stejnegers_Petrel.Best Ways to Identify: Very similar to Cook's Petrel; darker cap contrasting more with back. Rare Pacific coast vagrant requiring careful scrutiny.

Stejnegers_Scoter.Description: Large sea duck. Male is all black with white wing patch and distinctly knobbed bill with orange-yellow sides. Female dark brown. About 22 inches.
Stejnegers_Scoter.Behavior: Dives for mollusks in coastal marine waters. Breeds in Siberian taiga lakes. Rare vagrant to western Alaska; Asian counterpart of White-winged Scoter.
Stejnegers_Scoter.Habitat: Breeds on large Siberian lakes and rivers. Winters along East Asian coast. Rare in western Aleutian Islands.
Stejnegers_Scoter.Similar Looking Birds: White-winged Scoter nearly identical. Best distinguished by bill pattern and range.
Stejnegers_Scoter.Best Ways to Identify: Male's distinctly knobbed bill with orange coloring and white wing patches in flight. Nearly impossible to separate from White-winged Scoter in field.

Stellers_Eider.Description: Smallest eider duck. Male has white head with green face patch, black eye ring, white body with rusty underparts. Female mottled brown. About 18 inches.
Stellers_Eider.Behavior: Dives for mollusks, crustaceans, and marine invertebrates. Forms large flocks on Alaskan coast in winter. Threatened species.
Stellers_Eider.Habitat: Breeds on Arctic tundra in Alaska and Siberia. Winters along Alaska Peninsula and Aleutian Islands in shallow coastal waters.
Stellers_Eider.Similar Looking Birds: Other eider species are larger. Male's distinctive color pattern unlike other eiders.
Stellers_Eider.Best Ways to Identify: Small size compared to other eiders. Male's white and rust coloring with green face patch unmistakable. Female's blue speculum.

Stellers_Jay.Description: Large crested jay with sooty black head and upper body and vivid blue wings, tail, and lower body; white streaks on forehead.
Stellers_Jay.Behavior: Bold and loud; mimics hawks and other birds; caches acorns; dominates feeders; noisy flocking in winter.
Stellers_Jay.Habitat: Coniferous and mixed forests of western North America from Alaska to Central America; common in mountains.
Stellers_Jay.Similar Looking Birds: Blue Jay has white in wings; Scrub-jays lack crest; Pinyon Jay is all blue without crest and different body shape.
Stellers_Jay.Best Ways to Identify: Black head with prominent crest; brilliant blue body; white forehead streaks; western mountain conifer forests.

Stellers_Sea-Eagle.Description: Largest eagle in the world. Dark black-brown with white shoulders, thighs, and tail. Massive orange-yellow bill. About 42 inches.
Stellers_Sea-Eagle.Behavior: Hunts salmon and other fish; powerful predator. Rare vagrant from Siberia to western Alaska.
Stellers_Sea-Eagle.Habitat: Coasts and rivers of eastern Russia. Rare vagrant to western Alaska and Pacific coast.
Stellers_Sea-Eagle.Similar Looking Birds: Bald Eagle lacks white shoulder patches and huge bill. Steller's Sea-Eagle unmistakably large.
Stellers_Sea-Eagle.Best Ways to Identify: Enormous size with white shoulder patches. Massive orange bill. Very rare vagrant from Russia to Alaska.

Stilt_Sandpiper.Description: Medium sandpiper with long greenish-yellow legs, drooped bill tip, and in breeding plumage rufous ear patch with barred underparts.
Stilt_Sandpiper.Behavior: Wades deeply and sews bill through mud like dowitcher; often with dowitchers in shallow mudflats.
Stilt_Sandpiper.Habitat: Breeds on Arctic tundra; migrates through interior wetlands, mudflats, and shallow ponds; winters in South America.
Stilt_Sandpiper.Similar Looking Birds: Dowitchers have longer straight bills; Dunlin is smaller; Lesser Yellowlegs has bright yellow legs and straight bill.
Stilt_Sandpiper.Best Ways to Identify: Long greenish legs; slightly drooped bill; sewing sewing motion feeding; rufous ear patch in breeding plumage.

Streak-backed_Oriole.Description: Medium oriole, orange-red with black-streaked back, black throat, white wing bars. About 8.5 inches.
Streak-backed_Oriole.Behavior: Forages in trees for insects and nectar. Rare vagrant to California, Arizona, and New Mexico from Mexico.
Streak-backed_Oriole.Habitat: Thorn forest and woodland of Mexico. Rare vagrant to southwestern United States.
Streak-backed_Oriole.Similar Looking Birds: Hooded Oriole all-orange back. Bullock's Oriole has bold white wing patch. Streaked back distinctive.
Streak-backed_Oriole.Best Ways to Identify: Streaked black-and-orange back unique. Orange-red body. Rare fall and winter vagrant from Mexico.

Streaked_Shearwater.Description: Large shearwater, brown above, white below with brown- streaked white head. Pink bill. Large Calonectris shearwater. About 19 inches.
Streaked_Shearwater.Behavior: Asian Pacific shearwater. Rare vagrant to Pacific coast of North America. Follows fishing boats.
Streaked_Shearwater.Habitat: Northwestern Pacific Ocean. Rare vagrant to Pacific coast of North America, particularly in late summer and fall.
Streaked_Shearwater.Similar Looking Birds: Cory's Shearwater similar but has plain yellow bill without streaked head.
Streaked_Shearwater.Best Ways to Identify: Streaked white head with brown markings unique among shearwaters. Pink bill, white below. Asian Pacific vagrant.

Striped_Sparrow.Description: Medium sparrow, streaked above, white below, bold white supercilium, rufous cap with white central stripe. About 6.5 inches.
Striped_Sparrow.Behavior: Secretive in tall grass. Rare vagrant to Arizona and New Mexico from Mexico.
Striped_Sparrow.Habitat: High-elevation grasslands of Mexico. Rare vagrant to Arizona and New Mexico.
Striped_Sparrow.Similar Looking Birds: Baird's Sparrow has orange head. No other sparrow has bold white supercilium plus rufous cap with central stripe.
Striped_Sparrow.Best Ways to Identify: Bold white supercilium and rufous-striped cap. White below. Rare high-elevation vagrant from Mexico.

Stygian_Owl.Description: Medium-large dark owl with long ear tufts. Dark brown to blackish plumage, orange-red eyes, white forehead patch. About 17 inches.
Stygian_Owl.Behavior: Nocturnal forest hunter. Rare vagrant to southern Texas and Florida from Caribbean and Mexico.
Stygian_Owl.Habitat: Forest of Caribbean islands and Mexico. Rare vagrant to southern Florida and Texas.
Stygian_Owl.Similar Looking Birds: Long-eared Owl paler with more pronounced facial disk. Stygian Owl much darker overall.
Stygian_Owl.Best Ways to Identify: Very dark owl with long ear tufts, orange-red eyes, white forehead. Rare vagrant from Caribbean and Mexico.

Sulphur-bellied_Flycatcher.Description: Large flycatcher with heavily streaked body, rufous tail, yellow belly, and bold white supercilium over black mask.
Sulphur-bellied_Flycatcher.Behavior: Gives loud squeaky rubber duck calls; catches insects by sallying; nests in sycamore tree cavities in canyons.
Sulphur-bellied_Flycatcher.Habitat: Riparian sycamore canyons of southeastern Arizona; migrant through Mexico; winters in South America.
Sulphur-bellied_Flycatcher.Similar Looking Birds: Streaked Flycatcher is very similar but found in tropics; other large flycatchers lack bold streaked pattern.
Sulphur-bellied_Flycatcher.Best Ways to Identify: Heavily streaked breast; bright yellow belly; rufous tail; loud squeaky call; sycamore canyon habitat in Arizona.

Summer_Tanager.Description: Male entirely rose-red with large pale bill; female olive-yellow; both larger and heavier-billed than other tanagers.
Summer_Tanager.Behavior: Catches bees and wasps in flight; rubs stingers off before eating; sings robin-like phrases; canopy species.
Summer_Tanager.Habitat: Open oak and pine-oak woodlands and riparian forests across southern US; winters in Central and South America.
Summer_Tanager.Similar Looking Birds: Scarlet Tanager male has black wings; Northern Cardinal has crest; male House Finch has streaked back and sides.
Summer_Tanager.Best Ways to Identify: Entirely red male with no wing contrast; large pale bill; female olive-yellow; bee-eating behavior; southern woods.

Sungrebe.Description: Slender waterbird. Brown and black striped head and neck with black and white facial stripes, brown body. Lobed toes. About 11 inches.
Sungrebe.Behavior: Swims and dives in tropical rivers. Female carries chicks in wing pouches during flight. Rare vagrant to Texas from Mexico and Central America.
Sungrebe.Habitat: Tropical rivers and streams with dense overhanging vegetation in Mexico and Central America. Very rare vagrant to Texas.
Sungrebe.Similar Looking Birds: Grebes have similar body shape. Sungrebe's striped head and neck unique.
Sungrebe.Best Ways to Identify: Bold black and white striped face and neck on brown body. Lobed toes. Swims low in tropical rivers.

Surf_Scoter.Description: Large sea duck; male black with white patches on forehead and nape; gaudy orange-red bill with white and black pattern.
Surf_Scoter.Behavior: Dives through surf to eat mussels and clams; large rafts on coastal waters; nests on northern lakes.
Surf_Scoter.Habitat: Breeds on boreal lakes; winters in coastal bays, estuaries, and surf zones along both North American coasts.
Surf_Scoter.Similar Looking Birds: Black Scoter male is all black with yellow bill; White-winged Scoter has white wing patch; female scoters all brown.
Surf_Scoter.Best Ways to Identify: Male's white head patches; multicolored orange bill; black body; white in wing absent; coastal ocean winter habitat.

Surfbird.Description: Stocky shorebird with short yellow legs, short bill, white tail base with black band, and gray overall plumage.
Surfbird.Behavior: Forages on wave-washed rocks feeding on barnacles and mussels; tame; migrates along Pacific Coast.
Surfbird.Habitat: Rocky coastlines of Pacific Coast in winter; breeds on alpine tundra of Alaska; associated with wave-washed rocks.
Surfbird.Similar Looking Birds: Rock Sandpiper is similar on same rocky habitat; Wandering Tattler has longer bill and barred breeding plumage.
Surfbird.Best Ways to Identify: White rump with black terminal band on tail; yellow legs; stocky build; wave-washed rocky intertidal habitat.

Swainsons_Hawk.Description: Large hawk; typical light morph has white belly with dark chest band and brown back; two-tone wings from below.
Swainsons_Hawk.Behavior: Long-distance migrant to Argentina; follows army ants; soars in large kettles called whirlpools during migration.
Swainsons_Hawk.Habitat: Open grasslands, agricultural fields, and prairies of western North America; breeds in isolated trees on plains.
Swainsons_Hawk.Similar Looking Birds: Red-tailed Hawk has dark belly band not chest band; Ferruginous Hawk has leg feathering and different pattern.
Swainsons_Hawk.Best Ways to Identify: Dark bib contrasting with white belly; dark flight feathers contrasting with white wing linings from below; long pointed wings.

Swainsons_Thrush.Description: Medium olive-brown thrush with buffy eye-ring and buffy wash on spotted breast; uniform olive-brown upperparts.
Swainsons_Thrush.Behavior: Gives high peep call at night during migration; sings upward spiraling fluty phrases; forages on ground.
Swainsons_Thrush.Habitat: Moist coniferous and mixed forests of boreal zone and mountains; migrates through eastern and western US.
Swainsons_Thrush.Similar Looking Birds: Hermit Thrush has rufous tail contrasting with brown back; Veery is richer brown with fainter spots.
Swainsons_Thrush.Best Ways to Identify: Buffy eye-ring and face; buffy spotted breast; olive-brown back without rufous tail; upward spiraling flute song.

Swainsons_Warbler.Description: Medium warbler, plain olive-brown above, plain pale below, rusty-brown crown, bold supercilium. About 5.5 inches.
Swainsons_Warbler.Behavior: Forages secretively on ground in dense vegetation. Loud clear song belies its secretive nature.
Swainsons_Warbler.Habitat: Dense lowland swamps and rhododendron thickets in mountains of southeastern United States.
Swainsons_Warbler.Similar Looking Birds: Worm-eating Warbler has striped head. Ovenbird has orange crown. Plain brown above distinctive.
Swainsons_Warbler.Best Ways to Identify: Plain olive-brown above, pale below, rusty crown. Very secretive. Loud clear song from dense swamp vegetation.

Swallow-tailed_Gull.Description: Medium gull with distinctive deeply forked tail. Gray back, white head with red eye ring, dark hood in breeding. About 22 inches.
Swallow-tailed_Gull.Behavior: Only fully nocturnal gull; feeds at night on squid. Breeds on Galapagos. Rare vagrant to Pacific coast from South America.
Swallow-tailed_Gull.Habitat: Breeds on Galapagos Islands. Pelagic in Pacific Ocean. Rare vagrant to Pacific coast of North America.
Swallow-tailed_Gull.Similar Looking Birds: No other gull has deeply forked tail. Unmistakable.
Swallow-tailed_Gull.Best Ways to Identify: Deeply forked tail unique among gulls. Red eye ring. Gray back with dark hood. Rare vagrant on Pacific coast.

Swallow-tailed_Kite.Description: Unmistakable black-and-white kite with very long deeply forked tail. White head and body, black wings. About 23 inches.
Swallow-tailed_Kite.Behavior: Aerial acrobat; catches insects and lizards in flight. Breeds in southeastern US; winters in South America.
Swallow-tailed_Kite.Habitat: Bottomland hardwood forest and cypress swamps of southeastern US. Rare but regular in Florida and along Gulf Coast.
Swallow-tailed_Kite.Similar Looking Birds: No other North American raptor has long forked tail with black and white pattern.
Swallow-tailed_Kite.Best Ways to Identify: Long deeply forked tail on black-and-white bird. Unmistakable. Southeastern US breeding species, winter migrant to South America.

Swamp_Sparrow.Description: Stocky sparrow with rufous crown, gray face, white throat, and reddish-brown streaked back; dull breast with no spots.
Swamp_Sparrow.Behavior: Secretive in marsh vegetation; chips sharply; sings slow sweet musical trills; forages on mud for invertebrates.
Swamp_Sparrow.Habitat: Freshwater marshes, bogs, and shrubby wetland edges throughout eastern North America.
Swamp_Sparrow.Similar Looking Birds: Song Sparrow has streaked breast and central spot; Lincoln's Sparrow has buffy wash and fine streaking on breast.
Swamp_Sparrow.Best Ways to Identify: Rufous crown; gray face; white throat; plain gray-brown breast without streaking; freshwater marsh habitat.

Swinhoes_Storm-Petrel.Description: Small all-dark storm-petrel without white rump. Dark brown plumage, pale upperwing bar. About 8 inches.
Swinhoes_Storm-Petrel.Behavior: Asian Pacific storm-petrel. Rare vagrant to North American Atlantic coast; occasional in North Pacific offshore waters.
Swinhoes_Storm-Petrel.Habitat: Northwestern Pacific Ocean. Rare vagrant to North American Atlantic coast; very rare elsewhere in North America.
Swinhoes_Storm-Petrel.Similar Looking Birds: Ashy Storm-Petrel similar but smaller and grayer. Swinhoe's lacks white rump.
Swinhoes_Storm-Petrel.Best Ways to Identify: All-dark storm-petrel without white rump. Pale upperwing bar. Asian Pacific species, rare North American vagrant.

Swinhoes_White-eye.Description: Tiny bird, olive-green above, yellow throat, white eye ring, whitish below. About 4 inches.
Swinhoes_White-eye.Behavior: Highly gregarious in flocks. Forages for insects and nectar. Introduced to California.
Swinhoes_White-eye.Habitat: Gardens, woodland edges, and parks. Introduced to Los Angeles area California. Native to China and Japan.
Swinhoes_White-eye.Similar Looking Birds: Warbling White-eye (Japanese White-eye) nearly identical; same group. No other bird has white eye ring in range.
Swinhoes_White-eye.Best Ways to Identify: White eye ring on olive-green bird. Tiny size. California introduced population. Gregarious in flocks.

Tahiti_Petrel.Description: Large dark petrel with contrasting white belly and undertail. Dark brown-black above and on throat. Heavy dark bill. About 15 inches.
Tahiti_Petrel.Behavior: Breeds on South Pacific islands. Rare visitor to tropical Pacific waters; occasional vagrant to Hawaii and Pacific coast.
Tahiti_Petrel.Habitat: Tropical South Pacific. Rare vagrant to Hawaiian waters and North American Pacific coast.
Tahiti_Petrel.Similar Looking Birds: Large Bulweria petrels similar but all dark. Tahiti has contrasting white belly.
Tahiti_Petrel.Best Ways to Identify: Dark above and on breast, contrasting white belly and undertail. Heavy dark bill. Large tropical Pacific petrel.

Taiga_Bean-Goose.Description: A medium-large brown goose with an orange and black bill pattern and orange legs. Has a long neck and relatively small head.
Taiga_Bean-Goose.Behavior: Grazes on grass, crops, and berries. Migrates in family groups. Tends to be shy and wary compared to other geese.
Taiga_Bean-Goose.Habitat: Breeds in taiga forests and bogs of Scandinavia and Russia. Winters in agricultural fields and wetlands in western Europe.
Taiga_Bean-Goose.Similar Looking Birds: Very similar to Tundra Bean-Goose and Pink-footed Goose. Greater White-fronted Goose is similar but has white forehead patch.
Taiga_Bean-Goose.Best Ways to Identify: Look for the orange-banded black bill, longer neck, and larger size compared to Tundra Bean-Goose. Orange (not pink) legs are key.

Taiga_Flycatcher.Description: Small flycatcher, gray-brown above, white below with orange-red throat on male. Black tail with white base. About 4.5 inches.
Taiga_Flycatcher.Behavior: Perches upright on exposed branches. Fans tail showing white patches. Rare vagrant to western Alaska from Asia.
Taiga_Flycatcher.Habitat: Taiga forests of Siberia and East Asia. Rare vagrant to western Alaska and Aleutian Islands.
Taiga_Flycatcher.Similar Looking Birds: Red-flanked Bluetail has blue tail. Bluethroat has blue throat. Siberian Rubythroat has red throat.
Taiga_Flycatcher.Best Ways to Identify: Small brown flycatcher with orange-red throat on male. White tail base. Rare Alaska vagrant from Siberia.

Tamaulipas_Crow.Description: Small glossy crow, entirely black with blue-green gloss. Short bill, small size compared to other crows. About 14 inches.
Tamaulipas_Crow.Behavior: Formerly regular in small numbers at Brownsville, Texas landfill. Social in flocks. Now very rare north of Mexico.
Tamaulipas_Crow.Habitat: Arid scrub and agricultural areas of northeastern Mexico. Rarely wanders into extreme southern Texas.
Tamaulipas_Crow.Similar Looking Birds: American Crow much larger. Chihuahuan Raven larger with different range. Fish Crow similar but different range.
Tamaulipas_Crow.Best Ways to Identify: Very small glossy crow in far southern Texas. Strong blue-green gloss. Short bill. Rare vagrant.

Tanimbar_Corella.Description: Medium white cockatoo with salmon-pink face and lores, small erectile crest. About 12 inches.
Tanimbar_Corella.Behavior: Highly intelligent, uses tools. Gregarious in flocks. Small feral populations in California and Florida.
Tanimbar_Corella.Habitat: Open woodland and agricultural areas. Feral populations in parts of California and Florida. Native to Indonesia.
Tanimbar_Corella.Similar Looking Birds: Sulphur-crested Cockatoo larger with yellow crest. Other white cockatoos different crest color.
Tanimbar_Corella.Best Ways to Identify: White cockatoo with salmon-pink face. Small size among cockatoos. Feral in California and Florida.

Tawny-shouldered_Blackbird.Description: Medium blackbird. Male black with tawny-buff shoulder patch. Female dusky brown. About 8.5 inches.
Tawny-shouldered_Blackbird.Behavior: Forages in flocks in open agricultural areas. Rare vagrant to Florida from Cuba and Hispaniola.
Tawny-shouldered_Blackbird.Habitat: Open agricultural land of Cuba and Haiti. Rare vagrant to southern Florida.
Tawny-shouldered_Blackbird.Similar Looking Birds: Red-winged Blackbird has red-and-yellow epaulet. Tawny-buff shoulder patch distinctive.
Tawny-shouldered_Blackbird.Best Ways to Identify: Tawny-buff shoulder on black body. Very rare Florida vagrant from Cuba. Similar shape to Red-winged Blackbird.

Temmincks_Stint.Description: Very small sandpiper. Uniform gray-brown above, white below with gray-brown breast band. Short legs, creeping behavior. About 6 inches.
Temmincks_Stint.Behavior: Creeps mouse-like through vegetation. Prefers freshwater to coastal habitats. Rare vagrant to North America from Eurasia.
Temmincks_Stint.Habitat: Breeds on subarctic tundra and mountain slopes. Winters on African and Asian wetlands. Rare vagrant to North America.
Temmincks_Stint.Similar Looking Birds: Little Stint similar. Temminck's has white outer tail feathers and uniform gray-brown back.
Temmincks_Stint.Best Ways to Identify: White outer tail feathers visible in flight. Uniform gray-brown above without white supercilium. Mouse-like creeping behavior.

Tennessee_Warbler.Description: Small warbler; breeding male gray-green with white eyebrow, green back, and white underparts; female greener and yellower.
Tennessee_Warbler.Behavior: Sings staccato three-part accelerating song; forages high in trees; pierces flower bases for nectar in tropics.
Tennessee_Warbler.Habitat: Boreal forests for breeding; migrates through eastern and central US; winters in Central American shade coffee.
Tennessee_Warbler.Similar Looking Birds: Orange-crowned Warbler is yellowish; Nashville Warbler has yellow underparts; Philadelphia Vireo is larger.
Tennessee_Warbler.Best Ways to Identify: White eyebrow; clean white underparts; green back; gray head in male; flat forehead; thin pointed bill.

Terek_Sandpiper.Description: Medium sandpiper with distinctive long upturned bill. Gray-brown above, white below, orange-yellow legs. About 9 inches.
Terek_Sandpiper.Behavior: Runs rapidly along mudflats with body tilted forward. Rare vagrant to both coasts from Eurasia.
Terek_Sandpiper.Habitat: Breeds along Eurasian rivers. Winters on African and Asian coasts. Rare vagrant to Pacific and Atlantic coasts of North America.
Terek_Sandpiper.Similar Looking Birds: No other sandpiper has upturned bill. Dunlin similar size but bill curves down.
Terek_Sandpiper.Best Ways to Identify: Distinctive long upturned bill unique among sandpipers. Gray-brown with orange-yellow legs. Rapidly running feeding behavior.

Thick-billed_Kingbird.Description: Large kingbird with noticeably thick heavy bill. Brown- gray above, white throat, pale yellow belly. About 9 inches.
Thick-billed_Kingbird.Behavior: Perches conspicuously and makes long aerial sallies for insects. Regular summer resident in southeastern Arizona.
Thick-billed_Kingbird.Habitat: Riparian cottonwood-sycamore forest in southeastern Arizona. Summer resident; winters in Mexico.
Thick-billed_Kingbird.Similar Looking Birds: Tropical Kingbird similar but has thinner bill. Thick- billed has noticeably heavier bill.
Thick-billed_Kingbird.Best Ways to Identify: Noticeably heavy thick bill. Brown-gray back, pale yellow belly. Summer resident in Arizona riparian forest.

Thick-billed_Murre.Description: Large alcid with black head and upperparts, white underparts, and short thick bill with pale gape stripe at base.
Thick-billed_Murre.Behavior: Dives to great depths for fish; dense cliff colonies; single egg laid on bare rock ledge; excellent swimmer.
Thick-billed_Murre.Habitat: Arctic and subarctic ocean cliffs for nesting; winters offshore on northern Atlantic and Pacific oceans.
Thick-billed_Murre.Similar Looking Birds: Common Murre has thinner longer bill without gape stripe; Razorbill has deep laterally compressed bill.
Thick-billed_Murre.Best Ways to Identify: White stripe at bill base called gape stripe; stockier shorter bill than Common Murre; black and white seabird.

Thick-billed_Parrot.Description: Medium parrot, mostly green with red forehead and shoulders, thick black bill, red leg bend. About 15 inches.
Thick-billed_Parrot.Behavior: Endangered; flocks in pine forest. Extirpated from Arizona; recent small irruptions to Chiricahua Mountains.
Thick-billed_Parrot.Habitat: Pine forest in Sierra Madre Occidental of Mexico. Occasional irruptive visitor to southeastern Arizona mountains.
Thick-billed_Parrot.Similar Looking Birds: No other parrot in range has thick black bill with red forehead and shoulders.
Thick-billed_Parrot.Best Ways to Identify: Red forehead and shoulders, thick black bill. Green parrot in pine forest. Occasional irruptive visitor to Arizona mountains.

Thick-billed_Vireo.Description: Small vireo, olive-gray above with two wing bars and broken eye ring. Yellow-white below. Thick bill. About 5 inches.
Thick-billed_Vireo.Behavior: Caribbean vireo. Rare vagrant to southern Florida from Bahamas; possibly breeds on Florida Keys.
Thick-billed_Vireo.Habitat: Forest and thicket of Bahamas and Caribbean. Rare vagrant to southern Florida; possible rare breeder in Keys.
Thick-billed_Vireo.Similar Looking Birds: White-eyed Vireo similar. Thick-billed Vireo has thicker bill and different eye ring.
Thick-billed_Vireo.Best Ways to Identify: Thick bill, broken eye ring. Olive-gray with wing bars. Caribbean species rare in southern Florida.

Thick-billed_Warbler.Description: Large plain warbler, brown above with rufous tones, buff below. Heavy bill, rounded tail. About 7 inches.
Thick-billed_Warbler.Behavior: Skulking in dense vegetation. Loud rich song. Very rare vagrant to western Alaska from Asia.
Thick-billed_Warbler.Habitat: Dense reed beds, scrub, and tall grass in Asia. Very rare vagrant to western Alaska.
Thick-billed_Warbler.Similar Looking Birds: Common Reed Warbler similar but smaller. Blyth's Reed Warbler thinner billed. Generally distinctive in Alaska.
Thick-billed_Warbler.Best Ways to Identify: Large size, heavy bill, rufous-brown tones. Very rare Alaska vagrant. Skulks in dense vegetation.

Townsends_Solitaire.Description: Medium thrush-like bird with gray body, white eye-ring, buffy wing patches, and white outer tail feathers; slender build.
Townsends_Solitaire.Behavior: Sings beautiful complex warbling song year-round; guards juniper berry patches in winter; aerial flycatching.
Townsends_Solitaire.Habitat: Montane coniferous forests for breeding; winters in juniper woodlands and lower elevation shrubby areas.
Townsends_Solitaire.Similar Looking Birds: Northern Mockingbird has white wing patches but is larger; Townsend's Solitaire is slimmer than thrushes.
Townsends_Solitaire.Best Ways to Identify: Bold buffy wing patches in flight; white outer tail; white eye-ring; slim gray body; upright posture on perch.

Townsends_Storm-Petrel.Description: Small dark storm-petrel with white rump. Very similar to Leach's Storm-Petrel. About 7 inches.
Townsends_Storm-Petrel.Behavior: Breeds on Guadalupe Island, Mexico. Smaller and shorter- tailed than Leach's. Forages in Pacific off Mexico and California.
Townsends_Storm-Petrel.Habitat: Eastern Pacific Ocean off Baja California and Mexico. Breeds on Guadalupe Island.
Townsends_Storm-Petrel.Similar Looking Birds: Leach's Storm-Petrel nearly identical but larger. Townsend's best identified by smaller size.
Townsends_Storm-Petrel.Best Ways to Identify: Very similar to Leach's Storm-Petrel but smaller. Best distinguished at sea by size. Eastern Pacific off Mexico.

Townsends_Warbler.Description: Bright warbler; male has black and yellow face pattern with black throat; yellow breast; greenish back with streaking.
Townsends_Warbler.Behavior: Forages in conifer foliage gleaning insects; sings buzzy rising and falling phrases; high elevation breeder.
Townsends_Warbler.Habitat: Coniferous forests of Pacific Northwest and mountains; winters along California coast and in Mexico.
Townsends_Warbler.Similar Looking Birds: Hermit Warbler male has yellow face without black cheeks; Black-throated Green Warbler has yellow face and green back.
Townsends_Warbler.Best Ways to Identify: Black and yellow face with black cheek patch; black throat; yellow breast with black streaking; conifer forest.

Tree_Pipit.Description: Small pipit, streaked brown above, buff breast with dark streaks, pale base to bill. About 6 inches.
Tree_Pipit.Behavior: Song flight from tree top. Perches in trees unlike most pipits. Very rare vagrant to western Alaska from Europe.
Tree_Pipit.Habitat: Open woodland and scrub in Europe and Asia. Very rare vagrant to western Alaska.
Tree_Pipit.Similar Looking Birds: Olive-backed Pipit has olive tones. Red-throated Pipit brighter in breeding. Very similar to other pipits.
Tree_Pipit.Best Ways to Identify: Pale base to lower mandible (pinkish). Buff breast streaking. Perches in trees. Very rare Alaska vagrant.

Tree_Swallow.Description: Glossy iridescent blue-green upperparts contrasting with clean white underparts; slightly notched tail; compact build.
Tree_Swallow.Behavior: Eats flying insects caught aerially; readily uses nest boxes; flocks in large numbers in migration near water.
Tree_Swallow.Habitat: Open areas near water with dead trees for nesting; fields, marshes, and lakeshores throughout North America.
Tree_Swallow.Similar Looking Birds: Violet-green Swallow has white patches on sides of rump; Bank Swallow has brown chest band; Barn Swallow has long tail.
Tree_Swallow.Best Ways to Identify: Iridescent blue-green above; clean white below extending to below eye; no brown chest band; slight tail notch.

Tricolored_Blackbird.Description: Medium blackbird. Male black with red and white shoulder patch. Female dark brown with streaking. About 8.5 inches.
Tricolored_Blackbird.Behavior: Nests in huge colonies, sometimes hundreds of thousands. Highly colonial and nomadic. Rapidly declining.
Tricolored_Blackbird.Habitat: Freshwater marshes, agricultural fields, and open land in California. Critically endangered.
Tricolored_Blackbird.Similar Looking Birds: Red-winged Blackbird has red and yellow shoulder without white bar. White bar on shoulder distinctive.
Tricolored_Blackbird.Best Ways to Identify: White bar on red shoulder patch distinctive. All-black male. California endemic. Massive colony nester.

Tricolored_Heron.Description: Slender heron with dark slate-blue neck and upperparts, white belly, and white stripe down foreneck; slim proportions.
Tricolored_Heron.Behavior: Actively chases fish with quick dashing movements; spreads wings to shade water while foraging; colonial nester.
Tricolored_Heron.Habitat: Saltwater and brackish marshes, mangroves, and coastal wetlands of southeastern US and Gulf Coast.
Tricolored_Heron.Similar Looking Birds: Little Blue Heron lacks white belly; Reddish Egret is stockier and rusty; Great Blue Heron is much larger.
Tricolored_Heron.Best Ways to Identify: Distinctive white belly contrasting with dark blue neck; white foreneck stripe; slender build; rusty neck plumes.

Tricolored_Munia.Description: Small finch, chestnut-brown head and back, black breast and belly, white sides. About 4.5 inches.
Tricolored_Munia.Behavior: Gregarious, forages in flocks for grass seeds. Introduced to Hawaii; present on several islands.
Tricolored_Munia.Habitat: Grasslands, rice fields, and open areas. Introduced to Hawaii.
Tricolored_Munia.Similar Looking Birds: Chestnut Munia has chestnut belly not black. Scaly-breasted Munia has spotted breast. Black belly distinctive.
Tricolored_Munia.Best Ways to Identify: Black belly contrasting with white sides. Chestnut-brown head. Gregarious in Hawaiian grasslands.

Trindade_Petrel.Description: Polymorphic gadfly petrel; light, intermediate, and dark morphs. Breeds on Trindade Island, Brazil. About 15 inches.
Trindade_Petrel.Behavior: Breeds on Trindade Island; disperses into Atlantic and occasionally to North American Atlantic coast.
Trindade_Petrel.Habitat: South Atlantic Ocean. Rare vagrant to North American Atlantic coast, particularly offshore mid-Atlantic states.
Trindade_Petrel.Similar Looking Birds: Herald Petrel similar in Pacific. Trindade in Atlantic is dark with white primary flash.
Trindade_Petrel.Best Ways to Identify: Dark morph most common vagrant: dark brown with white primary flash. Rare Atlantic vagrant. Polymorphic species.

Tristrams_Storm-Petrel.Description: Large dark storm-petrel with pale upperwing bar. Larger than most Pacific storm-petrels. About 10 inches.
Tristrams_Storm-Petrel.Behavior: Breeds on Hawaiian Northwestern Islands; forages in Hawaiian and central Pacific waters. Nocturnal at breeding colonies.
Tristrams_Storm-Petrel.Habitat: Central North Pacific Ocean. Breeds on Hawaiian Northwestern Islands; rare in Hawaiian offshore waters.
Tristrams_Storm-Petrel.Similar Looking Birds: Black Storm-Petrel similar but found in eastern Pacific. Tristram's larger than most Hawaiian storm-petrels.
Tristrams_Storm-Petrel.Best Ways to Identify: Large dark storm-petrel in Hawaiian waters. Pale upperwing bar. Largest storm-petrel in central North Pacific.

Tropical_Kingbird.Description: Large flycatcher with gray head, yellow belly, olive-green back, notched brown tail, and concealed orange crown patch.
Tropical_Kingbird.Behavior: Sings twittering trilled calls; aggressive defense of territory; sallies for insects; expanding into Arizona.
Tropical_Kingbird.Habitat: Open woodland edges, riparian areas, and urban parks of Mexico and Central America; regular in southeast Arizona.
Tropical_Kingbird.Similar Looking Birds: Western Kingbird has white outer tail edges; Couch's Kingbird is nearly identical but different call and range.
Tropical_Kingbird.Best Ways to Identify: Notched brown tail without white edges; large size; bright yellow belly; gray head; twittering call in Arizona.

Tropical_Mockingbird.Description: Medium mockingbird, gray above, white below, white wing patches, white outer tail feathers. About 10 inches.
Tropical_Mockingbird.Behavior: Mimics other species and sings persistently. Bold in open areas. Rare vagrant to southern Florida and Texas.
Tropical_Mockingbird.Habitat: Open areas, urban environments, and forest edges from Mexico to South America. Rare vagrant to Florida and Texas.
Tropical_Mockingbird.Similar Looking Birds: Northern Mockingbird nearly identical. Tropical slightly more gray above with different tail pattern.
Tropical_Mockingbird.Best Ways to Identify: Nearly identical to Northern Mockingbird. Smaller tail pattern and subtle gray tones. Rare tropical vagrant to Florida.

Tropical_Parula.Description: Small warbler, blue-gray above, bright yellow throat and breast, no white eye ring. About 4.5 inches.
Tropical_Parula.Behavior: Active forager in tree canopy. Breeds rarely in extreme south Texas and more commonly in Mexico.
Tropical_Parula.Habitat: Riparian woodland, Spanish moss, and forest in south Texas and Mexico.
Tropical_Parula.Similar Looking Birds: Northern Parula has white eye ring and dark breast band. Tropical lacks eye ring.
Tropical_Parula.Best Ways to Identify: Blue-gray above with yellow below but no eye ring. Lacks breast band of Northern Parula. South Texas.

Trumpeter_Swan.Description: Largest North American waterfowl; entirely white with black bill and lores; no yellow on bill base; very long neck.
Trumpeter_Swan.Behavior: Gives loud trumpeting call; grazes aquatic vegetation; recovering from near extinction; family bonds strong.
Trumpeter_Swan.Habitat: Large lakes, rivers, and wetlands; reintroduced across much of northern US and Canada; wintering flocks in Pacific Northwest.
Trumpeter_Swan.Similar Looking Birds: Tundra Swan is smaller with yellow spot on bill base; Whooping Crane is taller with red crown and different profile.
Trumpeter_Swan.Best Ways to Identify: All black bill with no yellow; very large size; all white plumage; straight neck; loud trumpeting vocalizations.

Tufted_Duck.Description: Male black and white with distinctive drooping head tuft; yellow eye; blue-gray bill; female brown with smaller tuft.
Tufted_Duck.Behavior: Dives for mollusks and aquatic invertebrates; Eurasian species appearing regularly in North America in winter.
Tufted_Duck.Habitat: Lakes, reservoirs, and coastal bays; rare visitor to North America often associating with scaup flocks.
Tufted_Duck.Similar Looking Birds: Ring-necked Duck lacks head tuft; Greater Scaup lacks tuft and has different head shape; Lesser Scaup similar.
Tufted_Duck.Best Ways to Identify: Drooping black head tuft; black and white male; yellow eye; blue-gray bill; Eurasian vagrant to North America.

Tufted_Flycatcher.Description: Small flycatcher with prominent pointed crest. Brown- olive above, orange-buff below with two wing bars. About 5 inches.
Tufted_Flycatcher.Behavior: Sallies for insects from exposed perch. Mexican species; rare vagrant to southern Arizona and Texas.
Tufted_Flycatcher.Habitat: Pine-oak forest of Mexico and Central America. Rare vagrant to southeastern Arizona and southern Texas.
Tufted_Flycatcher.Similar Looking Birds: Pewees lack the pointed crest. Tufted Flycatcher's crest distinguishes it.
Tufted_Flycatcher.Best Ways to Identify: Prominent pointed crest. Buff-orange below. Small. Rare vagrant from Mexico to Arizona and Texas.

Tufted_Puffin.Description: Large stocky alcid; black body with white face patch and drooping yellowish tufts in breeding; huge orange-red bill.
Tufted_Puffin.Behavior: Dives for fish; nests in burrows on grassy clifftops; large colorful bill used in courtship; colonial nester.
Tufted_Puffin.Habitat: Rocky offshore islands and sea cliffs of North Pacific; winters far offshore on open ocean.
Tufted_Puffin.Similar Looking Birds: Atlantic Puffin has different facial pattern without tufts; Horned Puffin lacks tufts and has different bill pattern.
Tufted_Puffin.Best Ways to Identify: Long yellow tufts behind eye in summer; white face; massive orange bill; black body; North Pacific ocean habitat.

Tufted_Titmouse.Description: Small bird with prominent gray crest, gray above, white below with rusty-orange flanks. Black forehead. About 6 inches.
Tufted_Titmouse.Behavior: Bold and inquisitive at feeders. Caches food for winter. Loud and persistent peter-peter-peter song.
Tufted_Titmouse.Habitat: Deciduous and mixed forests of eastern United States. Common in suburbs and at backyard feeders year-round.
Tufted_Titmouse.Similar Looking Birds: Black-crested Titmouse has black crest. Carolina Chickadee smaller with black bib and cap.
Tufted_Titmouse.Best Ways to Identify: Gray pointed crest, black forehead, rusty flanks. Bold behavior at feeders. Loud repetitive peter-peter song.

Tundra_Bean-Goose.Description: A compact, dark brown goose with a shorter neck than Taiga Bean-Goose, orange-and-black bill, and orange legs. Rounder head profile.
Tundra_Bean-Goose.Behavior: Feeds on tundra vegetation, grasses, and agricultural crops in winter. Forms large flocks on wintering grounds in Asia and Europe.
Tundra_Bean-Goose.Habitat: Breeds on open Arctic tundra in Russia and eastern Siberia. Winters in coastal wetlands, rice fields, and grasslands in East Asia.
Tundra_Bean-Goose.Similar Looking Birds: Very similar to Taiga Bean-Goose but stockier. Also resembles Greater White-fronted Goose without the white face patch.
Tundra_Bean-Goose.Best Ways to Identify: Shorter, stubbier bill and neck than Taiga Bean-Goose. Rounder head, darker brown overall plumage, and compact body shape are key.

Tundra_Swan.Description: Large white swan with black bill and small yellow spot at base of bill near eye; more rounded head than Trumpeter.
Tundra_Swan.Behavior: Gives musical whooping calls; migrates in family groups; winters in coastal estuaries and agricultural fields.
Tundra_Swan.Habitat: Arctic tundra for nesting; winters on Chesapeake Bay, Central Valley California, and interior marshes.
Tundra_Swan.Similar Looking Birds: Trumpeter Swan is larger with all-black bill and no yellow; Whooping Crane is taller not a swan.
Tundra_Swan.Best Ways to Identify: Small yellow spot at bill base near eye; black bill otherwise; smaller than Trumpeter Swan; musical whooping calls.

Turkey_Vulture.Description: Large black soaring bird with bare red head, two-toned underwings, and small head; distinctive V-shaped soaring posture.
Turkey_Vulture.Behavior: Locates carrion by smell, unique among raptors; rocks in flight due to small wingloading; rarely flaps wings.
Turkey_Vulture.Habitat: Open country, roadsides, and forests throughout the Americas; roosts communally; very widespread species.
Turkey_Vulture.Similar Looking Birds: Black Vulture has white wing patches and flat soaring posture; eagles and hawks have feathered heads.
Turkey_Vulture.Best Ways to Identify: Red bare head; two-toned black and silver underwing; V-shaped dihedral soaring; rocking side-to-side in thermals.

Ula-ai-hawane.Description: Tiny Hawaiian honeycreeper, male brilliant red with gray wings and tail. Female brown. About 4 inches.
Ula-ai-hawane.Behavior: Fed on hawane palm fruits in native Hawaiian forest. Extinct since approximately 1892.
Ula-ai-hawane.Habitat: Native forests with loulu palm on Big Island. Extinct due to deforestation and introduced species.
Ula-ai-hawane.Similar Looking Birds: Iiwi larger with curved bill. Apapane similar red color. No similar tiny red bird survives.
Ula-ai-hawane.Best Ways to Identify: Extinct tiny red honeycreeper from Big Island. Associated with loulu palms. No longer exists.

Upland_Sandpiper.Description: Medium brown sandpiper with small pigeon-like head, long neck, long tail, and short bill; grassland species.
Upland_Sandpiper.Behavior: Perches on fence posts; gives ascending wolf-whistle call; feeds on grasshoppers; long-distance migrant.
Upland_Sandpiper.Habitat: Native grasslands and prairies of Great Plains and Great Lakes region; declining with grassland loss.
Upland_Sandpiper.Similar Looking Birds: Buff-breasted Sandpiper is similar but stockier without small head appearance; Whimbrel has curved bill and different size.
Upland_Sandpiper.Best Ways to Identify: Small round head on long neck; pigeon-like proportions; long primary projection; perches on fence posts; grasslands.

Variable_Hawk.Description: Medium to large hawk, highly variable plumage from gray and white to dark rufous-brown. Broad rounded wings. About 22 inches.
Variable_Hawk.Behavior: Soars over open country and hillsides. Extremely rare vagrant to North America from South America.
Variable_Hawk.Habitat: Open country, hillsides, and mountains of South America. Extremely rare vagrant to North America.
Variable_Hawk.Similar Looking Birds: Red-tailed Hawk has dark belly band. Highly variable plumage makes comparison difficult.
Variable_Hawk.Best Ways to Identify: Extremely rare South American vagrant. Variable plumage from gray to rufous. Broad rounded wings and open country.

Varied_Bunting.Description: Small bunting. Male complex purple-blue with red nape patch and red-purple rump. Female plain brown. About 5 inches.
Varied_Bunting.Behavior: Forages in dense thorny scrub. Male often appears blackish in poor light. Skulks.
Varied_Bunting.Habitat: Dense thorn scrub along streams and brushy areas in southeastern Arizona and southwest Texas.
Varied_Bunting.Similar Looking Birds: Indigo Bunting lighter blue. Painted Bunting has green back and red belly. Complex purple-blue in good light.
Varied_Bunting.Best Ways to Identify: Male complex purple-blue with red nape, appears dark in poor light. Dense thorn scrub in Arizona and Texas.

Varied_Thrush.Description: Robin-like thrush; male has orange and dark gray pattern with orange supercilium and dark breast band; orange wing bars.
Varied_Thrush.Behavior: Solitary and shy; gives long haunting whistled note; winters irruptively at feeders; forages under dense conifers.
Varied_Thrush.Habitat: Moist old-growth and mature coniferous forests of Pacific Northwest; winters in California and southwest.
Varied_Thrush.Similar Looking Birds: American Robin has plain red breast without band; female Varied Thrush is brownish where male is gray.
Varied_Thrush.Best Ways to Identify: Orange supercilium and wing bars; dark breast band; gray and orange male; haunting single-note whistle call.

Variegated_Flycatcher.Description: Medium flycatcher, brown and white streaked above, white below with brown streaks, rufous on wing and tail. About 7 inches.
Variegated_Flycatcher.Behavior: South American migrant; rare vagrant to eastern North America. Perches conspicuously.
Variegated_Flycatcher.Habitat: Open woodland and forest edge of South America. Rare vagrant to Atlantic coast of North America.
Variegated_Flycatcher.Similar Looking Birds: Piratic Flycatcher similar but lacks rufous on wings and tail.
Variegated_Flycatcher.Best Ways to Identify: Streaked flycatcher with rufous wing edging and tail. Rare South American vagrant to Atlantic coast.

Vauxs_Swift.Description: Very small swift. Dark sooty gray-brown overall, slightly paler throat and rump. Tiny with stubby tail and cigar-shaped body. About 4.5 inches.
Vauxs_Swift.Behavior: Aerial insect feeder; never perches on ground. Roosts and nests in hollow trees. Migrates along Pacific coast; gregarious in large flocks.
Vauxs_Swift.Habitat: Forests of Pacific coast from Alaska to Central America. Uses hollow conifers for nesting. Migrates through Pacific states.
Vauxs_Swift.Similar Looking Birds: Chimney Swift nearly identical but found in East. Both are tiny dark swifts.
Vauxs_Swift.Best Ways to Identify: Tiny size, sooty gray plumage, and cigar-shaped body in twinkling flight. Paler rump. Mainly on Pacific Coast.

Veery.Description: Medium thrush with rich tawny-cinnamon upperparts and lightly spotted breast; spotted breast much less distinct than congeners.
Veery.Behavior: Sings descending ethereal spiraling veer-y veer-y song at dusk; forages on ground; long-distance migrant.
Veery.Habitat: Moist deciduous forests and streamside thickets; breeds across northeastern and north-central US and Canada.
Veery.Similar Looking Birds: Swainson's Thrush has buffy eye-ring; Hermit Thrush has rufous tail only; Wood Thrush has bolder spots.
Veery.Best Ways to Identify: Warm tawny-cinnamon color; faint spots on upper breast; no bold eye-ring; descending spiraling ethereal song.

Vega_Gull.Description: Large gull, pale gray back, pink legs, yellow bill with red spot. Similar to Herring Gull. About 24 inches.
Vega_Gull.Behavior: Breeds in Siberia; winters in eastern Asia and occasionally reaches western Alaska and Pacific coast of North America.
Vega_Gull.Habitat: Siberian coastlines and tundra. Rare winter visitor to Alaska and occasionally Pacific coast of North America.
Vega_Gull.Similar Looking Birds: American Herring Gull very similar. Vega Gull slightly darker gray with pinkish orbital ring.
Vega_Gull.Best Ways to Identify: Siberian counterpart to Herring Gull. Slightly darker gray back. Rare visitor to western Alaska and Pacific coast.

Verdin.Description: Tiny gray bird with yellow head and chestnut shoulder patches; small and active in desert thorny shrubs.
Verdin.Behavior: Builds spherical stick nests for roosting year-round in addition to breeding; gleans insects from thorny desert plants.
Verdin.Habitat: Thorny desert scrub, mesquite, and arid brushland of southwestern US and northern Mexico.
Verdin.Similar Looking Birds: No similar tiny gray-bodied yellow-headed bird in range; Lucy's Warbler has white not chestnut shoulder.
Verdin.Best Ways to Identify: Yellow head and face; chestnut shoulder patch; tiny gray body; desert thorny shrub habitat; round stick nests.

Vermilion_Flycatcher.Description: Unmistakable small flycatcher. Male brilliant red crown and underparts, brown-black back. Female brown with streaked belly. About 6 inches.
Vermilion_Flycatcher.Behavior: Sallies for insects. Males display dramatically in flight. Common in desert riparian areas of Southwest.
Vermilion_Flycatcher.Habitat: Desert and semi-arid areas near water. Common from Texas to California; also along Gulf Coast in winter.
Vermilion_Flycatcher.Similar Looking Birds: No other small flycatcher has the brilliant red plumage of male Vermilion Flycatcher.
Vermilion_Flycatcher.Best Ways to Identify: Male: brilliant red with brown-black back. Unmistakable. Female: streaked below. Desert Southwest riparian areas.

Vesper_Sparrow.Description: Medium sparrow, streaked brown above and below, white outer tail feathers, chestnut shoulder patch. About 6.5 inches.
Vesper_Sparrow.Behavior: Sings beautiful song at dusk, giving it the name Vesper. Walks on ground in open grasslands.
Vesper_Sparrow.Habitat: Open grasslands, fields, and sagebrush across North America. Declining in many areas.
Vesper_Sparrow.Similar Looking Birds: Savannah Sparrow lacks chestnut shoulder. Song Sparrow more heavily streaked. White outer tail in flight helpful.
Vesper_Sparrow.Best Ways to Identify: White outer tail feathers in flight. Chestnut shoulder patch. Streaked grassland sparrow. Beautiful dusk song.

Violet-crowned_Hummingbird.Description: Medium hummingbird. Brilliant violet-blue crown, plain white underparts, green back, red-orange bill. Clean white underparts distinctive. About 4.5 inches.
Violet-crowned_Hummingbird.Behavior: Feeds on nectar and insects. Rare summer visitor to Arizona and New Mexico riparian canyons from Mexico. Visits flowers and feeders.
Violet-crowned_Hummingbird.Habitat: Riparian woodland and canyon scrub in southeastern Arizona, southwestern New Mexico, and adjacent Mexico.
Violet-crowned_Hummingbird.Similar Looking Birds: Berylline Hummingbird in similar range. Violet-crowned's plain white underparts unique.
Violet-crowned_Hummingbird.Best Ways to Identify: Brilliant violet-blue crown and entirely clean white underparts unmistakable. Red-orange bill. Riparian canyons in southeastern Arizona.

Violet-green_Swallow.Description: Iridescent green and purple upperparts with white patches wrapping onto sides of rump; white extends above eye.
Violet-green_Swallow.Behavior: Forages aerially for insects; nests in tree cavities and nest boxes; colonial and often mixes with other swallows.
Violet-green_Swallow.Habitat: Open woodlands, mountain forests, and cliffs of western North America; common in suburban areas.
Violet-green_Swallow.Similar Looking Birds: Tree Swallow lacks white rump patches and white above eye; White-throated Swift is black and white with longer wings.
Violet-green_Swallow.Best Ways to Identify: White patches on sides of rump; white wraps above eye level on face; green and purple iridescent back; western US.

Virginia_Rail.Description: Small rail with long slightly downcurved reddish bill, rufous breast, barred flanks, and gray cheeks; brown streaked back.
Virginia_Rail.Behavior: Secretive in dense marsh vegetation; gives distinctive kid-ik descending calls and oinking grunts at night.
Virginia_Rail.Habitat: Dense freshwater and brackish marshes with cattails and sedges throughout North America.
Virginia_Rail.Similar Looking Birds: Sora has short yellow bill; King Rail is much larger with rufous cheeks; Clapper Rail is gray-brown.
Virginia_Rail.Best Ways to Identify: Long reddish-orange bill; gray cheeks; rufous breast; barred flanks; small size; freshwater cattail marshes.

Virginia_Warbler.Description: Small gray warbler with white eye-ring, yellow rump, yellow patch on breast, and chestnut crown patch; slim build.
Virginia_Warbler.Behavior: Bobs tail constantly like Nashville Warbler; sings from dense mountain shrubs; ground nester on steep slopes.
Virginia_Warbler.Habitat: Dense mountain brush and scrub oak on dry slopes of southern Rocky Mountains and Great Basin ranges.
Virginia_Warbler.Similar Looking Birds: Nashville Warbler has yellow throat; Colima Warbler is larger and browner; Lucy's Warbler has white underparts.
Virginia_Warbler.Best Ways to Identify: Gray body with yellow chest patch; yellow rump; white eye-ring; tail bobbing behavior; mountain shrubby slopes.

Virginias_Warbler.Description: Small warbler, gray above, white below, yellow breast patch and undertail coverts, rusty crown. About 4.5 inches.
Virginias_Warbler.Behavior: Forages low in shrubs. Bobs tail frequently. Mountain scrub specialist in southwestern United States.
Virginias_Warbler.Habitat: Dry mountain scrub and pinyon-juniper woodland in the southern Rocky Mountains and Great Basin.
Virginias_Warbler.Similar Looking Birds: Colima Warbler in Chisos Mountains. Nashville Warbler more yellow below. Gray body with yellow patches.
Virginias_Warbler.Best Ways to Identify: Gray body with yellow breast patch and undertail. Rusty crown. Tail bobbing behavior. Mountain scrub in southwest.

Wandering_Albatross.Description: Largest albatross; greatest wingspan of any living bird. White body, black wingtips, pink bill. About 11-foot wingspan.
Wandering_Albatross.Behavior: Circumnavigates Southern Ocean on wind currents. Breeds every other year on South Atlantic and Indian Ocean islands.
Wandering_Albatross.Habitat: Southern Ocean; rare vagrant to North Pacific and North Atlantic. Among the most impressive seabirds.
Wandering_Albatross.Similar Looking Birds: Royal Albatross similar. Wandering Albatross distinguishable by white back developing with age.
Wandering_Albatross.Best Ways to Identify: Enormous wingspan; all-white body develops with age. Pink bill. Very rare North American vagrant from Southern Ocean.

Wandering_Tattler.Description: Medium sandpiper. Uniform gray above, white below with barred underparts in breeding. Yellow legs. About 11 inches.
Wandering_Tattler.Behavior: Bobs tail while walking on rocky shores. Loud "weet" calls. Found on rocky Pacific coasts. Long nasal groove separates from Gray-tailed Tattler.
Wandering_Tattler.Habitat: Breeds along mountain streams in Alaska and Yukon. Winters on rocky Pacific shores and islands.
Wandering_Tattler.Similar Looking Birds: Gray-tailed Tattler nearly identical. Wandering has longer nasal groove on bill.
Wandering_Tattler.Best Ways to Identify: Uniform gray plumage on rocky Pacific shores. Longer nasal groove on bill. Loud piped calls. Bobs tail constantly.

Warbling_Vireo.Description: Plain gray-green vireo with pale eyebrow, whitish underparts, and no wing bars; one of dullest but sweetest-singing vireos.
Warbling_Vireo.Behavior: Sings long warbling phrases from canopy; deliberately gleans caterpillars and insects; forages high in trees.
Warbling_Vireo.Habitat: Riparian woodlands, deciduous forests, and shade trees throughout temperate North America.
Warbling_Vireo.Similar Looking Birds: Philadelphia Vireo has yellow underparts; Tennessee Warbler has shorter bill; Red-eyed Vireo has bold head stripes.
Warbling_Vireo.Best Ways to Identify: Plain unmarked face with pale eyebrow; no wing bars; plain greenish-gray; prolonged warbling song from treetops.

Warbling_White-eye.Description: Tiny bright green bird with distinctive white eye ring, yellow throat and breast, gray flanks. About 4 inches.
Warbling_White-eye.Behavior: Highly active in flocks foraging for insects, nectar, and fruit. Invasive in Hawaii, competing with native species.
Warbling_White-eye.Habitat: Forests, gardens, and suburban areas. Introduced to Hawaii; now one of commonest birds throughout the islands.
Warbling_White-eye.Similar Looking Birds: No other bird in Hawaii has the white eye ring. Amakihi greener without eye ring.
Warbling_White-eye.Best Ways to Identify: Bold white eye ring on green body. Yellow throat. Tiny size. Common in Hawaii. Chattering calls in flocks.

Waved_Albatross.Description: Large albatross with fine wavy brown and white body pattern, yellow bill, white head with yellow-buff wash. About 35 inches.
Waved_Albatross.Behavior: Breeds almost exclusively on Espanola Island, Galapagos. Forages off South American coast; rare vagrant to North America.
Waved_Albatross.Habitat: Eastern Pacific off South America. Breeds Galapagos; very rare vagrant to Pacific coast of North America.
Waved_Albatross.Similar Looking Birds: Other large albatrosses lack the wavy brown-white body pattern of Waved Albatross.
Waved_Albatross.Best Ways to Identify: Wavy brown-and-white body pattern distinctive. Yellow bill, white head. Galapagos breeder, rare North American vagrant.

Wedge-rumped_Storm-Petrel.Description: Dark storm-petrel with enormous white rump patch extending nearly to tail tip. About 7 inches.
Wedge-rumped_Storm-Petrel.Behavior: Breeds on Galapagos; post-breeding birds move up Pacific coast. Rare visitor to eastern Pacific off California.
Wedge-rumped_Storm-Petrel.Habitat: Eastern tropical Pacific. Post-breeding dispersal brings rare visitors to California offshore waters.
Wedge-rumped_Storm-Petrel.Similar Looking Birds: Other storm-petrels have smaller white rump patches. Wedge-rumped's enormous white rump diagnostic.
Wedge-rumped_Storm-Petrel.Best Ways to Identify: Enormous white rump patch extending almost to tail. Much larger white rump than other dark storm-petrels.

Wedge-tailed_Shearwater.Description: Medium shearwater with long wedge-shaped tail. Polymorphic: dark morph all brown, light morph white below. About 17 inches.
Wedge-tailed_Shearwater.Behavior: Breeds on Hawaiian and Pacific islands. Common in Hawaiian offshore waters and tropical Pacific.
Wedge-tailed_Shearwater.Habitat: Tropical Pacific Ocean. Breeds on Hawaiian Islands and other Pacific tropical islands. Common in Hawaiian offshore waters.
Wedge-tailed_Shearwater.Similar Looking Birds: Other dark shearwaters lack wedge-shaped tail. Light morph similar to Buller's but has longer wedge tail.
Wedge-tailed_Shearwater.Best Ways to Identify: Long wedge-shaped tail distinctive. Polymorphic; dark morph all-brown, light morph has white underparts.

West_Indian_Whistling-Duck.Description: Large duck, dark brown above, pale below with dark spots, long neck, upright posture. About 20 inches.
West_Indian_Whistling-Duck.Behavior: Nocturnal, roosts in trees. Whistling calls. Rare visitor to southern Florida from Caribbean.
West_Indian_Whistling-Duck.Habitat: Mangroves, swamps, and woodland near water in the Caribbean. Rare visitor to Florida.
West_Indian_Whistling-Duck.Similar Looking Birds: Black-bellied Whistling-Duck has red bill and black belly. Fulvous Whistling-Duck has buff body.
West_Indian_Whistling-Duck.Best Ways to Identify: Dark brown with spotted flanks, upright posture, long neck. Rare Florida visitor from Caribbean.

Western_Bluebird.Description: Male deep blue head and wings with rusty-orange breast; some show orange on back; female grayish with blue tones.
Western_Bluebird.Behavior: Drops to ground from perch to catch insects; uses nest boxes and tree cavities; flocks in winter on berries.
Western_Bluebird.Habitat: Open woodlands, pine-oak forests, and forest edges of western North America; partial migrant.
Western_Bluebird.Similar Looking Birds: Eastern Bluebird has orange on throat; Mountain Bluebird male is all blue without orange breast.
Western_Bluebird.Best Ways to Identify: Blue throat and head contrasting with orange breast; no orange on throat unlike Eastern Bluebird; open western forests.

Western_Cattle-Egret.Description: Small white egret with orange-buff patches on head, breast, and back in breeding. Short yellow bill. About 20 inches.
Western_Cattle-Egret.Behavior: Follows cattle and large animals to catch disturbed insects. Highly successful colonizer; spread from Africa to Americas.
Western_Cattle-Egret.Habitat: Pastures, agricultural fields, and open areas. Common throughout southeastern US; spreading northward and westward.
Western_Cattle-Egret.Similar Looking Birds: Snowy Egret all white with black bill. Cattle Egret has yellow bill and stocky build.
Western_Cattle-Egret.Best Ways to Identify: Short yellow bill, stocky build, follows cattle and farm machinery. Orange-buff patches in breeding. Common in pastures.

Western_Flycatcher.Description: Small Empidonax flycatcher, olive-green above, yellow wash on belly, teardrop eye ring. About 5 inches.
Western_Flycatcher.Behavior: Breeds in moist conifer and mixed forest of Pacific states. Gives sharp upward-slurred whistle call.
Western_Flycatcher.Habitat: Moist forest near streams along Pacific coast from Alaska to Baja. Common but secretive.
Western_Flycatcher.Similar Looking Birds: Cordilleran Flycatcher nearly identical. Western and Cordilleran best separated by range.
Western_Flycatcher.Best Ways to Identify: Teardrop eye ring, yellow wash on throat and belly. Pacific coast moist forests. Sharp whistle call.

Western_Grebe.Description: Large grebe with black and white plumage, long slender neck, long yellow-green pointed bill, and red eyes.
Western_Grebe.Behavior: Performs spectacular rushing courtship display across water; dives for fish; builds floating nest in reeds.
Western_Grebe.Habitat: Large lakes and reservoirs for breeding; winters on coastal bays and larger inland lakes of western North America.
Western_Grebe.Similar Looking Birds: Clark's Grebe is nearly identical but has white around eye and brighter orange-yellow bill; both do rush display.
Western_Grebe.Best Ways to Identify: Long slender neck; black cap extends below eye level; yellow-green bill; large size; lakes of western North America.

Western_Gull.Description: Large gull, dark gray back, pink legs, yellow bill with red spot. White head and underparts. About 25 inches.
Western_Gull.Behavior: Common along Pacific coast. Bold scavenger at beaches, harbors, and fishing docks. Nests on offshore rocky islands.
Western_Gull.Habitat: Pacific coast from Washington to Baja California. Rocky islands for nesting; coastlines, harbors, and beaches year-round.
Western_Gull.Similar Looking Birds: Glaucous-winged Gull similar in range. Western Gull has darker gray back and pink legs.
Western_Gull.Best Ways to Identify: Dark gray back combined with pink legs distinctive on Pacific coast. Large size, yellow bill with red spot.

Western_Kingbird.Description: Gray-headed kingbird with yellow belly, olive back, and black tail with white outer edges; orange crown patch concealed.
Western_Kingbird.Behavior: Aggressive toward larger birds; sallies for insects from exposed perch; chatters constantly; common roadside bird.
Western_Kingbird.Habitat: Open country with scattered trees, roadsides, farms, and rangelands throughout western North America.
Western_Kingbird.Similar Looking Birds: Cassin's Kingbird has darker gray chest with white chin; Tropical Kingbird has notched brownish tail without white edges.
Western_Kingbird.Best Ways to Identify: White outer tail edges on black tail; yellow belly; gray head; no chest band; common open country western bird.

Western_Marsh_Harrier.Description: Large harrier. Male brown with gray wings and tail; female dark brown with cream crown and throat. About 22 inches.
Western_Marsh_Harrier.Behavior: Hunts over reedbeds and marshes. Common in Europe. Rare vagrant to Atlantic coast of North America.
Western_Marsh_Harrier.Habitat: Reedbeds, marshes, and wetlands of Europe and western Asia. Rare vagrant to Atlantic coast.
Western_Marsh_Harrier.Similar Looking Birds: Northern Harrier lacks brown body coloration and cream head of Western Marsh Harrier.
Western_Marsh_Harrier.Best Ways to Identify: Large brown harrier, cream crown and throat. Male has gray wing patches. Rare Atlantic vagrant.

Western_Meadowlark.Description: Brown streaked bird with brilliant yellow underparts, V-shaped black breast band, and white outer tail feathers.
Western_Meadowlark.Behavior: Sings beautiful flute-like bubbling song; walks through grass foraging for insects; flushes showing white outer tail.
Western_Meadowlark.Habitat: Native grasslands, prairies, and open fields throughout western North America; state bird of several states.
Western_Meadowlark.Similar Looking Birds: Eastern Meadowlark is nearly identical visually but has different song; both have same field marks.
Western_Meadowlark.Best Ways to Identify: Yellow breast with black V; flute-like bubbling song; white outer tail feathers; brown streaked back; grasslands.

Western_Reef-Heron.Description: Medium heron with two morphs: dark gray or white. Yellow bill with dark culmen, yellow-green legs. About 23 inches.
Western_Reef-Heron.Behavior: Forages on rocky coasts and reefs. African and Asian coastal species; very rare vagrant to North American Atlantic coast.
Western_Reef-Heron.Habitat: Rocky coasts and estuaries of Africa and Asia. Very rare vagrant to northeastern North America.
Western_Reef-Heron.Similar Looking Birds: Dark morph similar to Little Blue Heron. White morph similar to Little or Snowy Egret.
Western_Reef-Heron.Best Ways to Identify: Yellow bill with dark culmen on dark or white heron. Coastal reef habitat. Very rare Atlantic vagrant.

Western_Sandpiper.Description: Small sandpiper with slightly drooped bill tip; rufous back and cap in breeding; gray in winter; black legs.
Western_Sandpiper.Behavior: Migrates in enormous flocks; probes mud in shallow water; common peep in western and central US on migration.
Western_Sandpiper.Habitat: Breeds on Arctic tundra of Alaska; migrates along all coasts and interior; winters on southern coasts.
Western_Sandpiper.Similar Looking Birds: Semipalmated Sandpiper has straighter shorter bill; Dunlin has more drooped bill and larger size; Least Sandpiper has yellow legs.
Western_Sandpiper.Best Ways to Identify: Slightly drooped bill longer than Semipalmated; rufous back and cap in breeding; black legs; small peep shorebird.

Western_Screech-Owl.Description: Small owl with ear tufts, yellow eyes, and gray or brownish cryptic bark-patterned plumage; compact body.
Western_Screech-Owl.Behavior: Gives descending whinny and double trill calls; nocturnal; roosts in tree cavities by day; hunts insects and small vertebrates.
Western_Screech-Owl.Habitat: Various woodlands, riparian areas, and deserts of western North America; uses nest boxes.
Western_Screech-Owl.Similar Looking Birds: Eastern Screech-Owl is very similar but limited overlap in range; Whiskered Screech-Owl has finer streaking.
Western_Screech-Owl.Best Ways to Identify: Small ear-tufted owl; gray bark-like cryptic patterning; yellow eyes; western range; descending whinny call.

Western_Spindalis.Description: Medium bird. Male striking with black head, white stripes, orange-red breast. Female olive-green. About 6.5 inches.
Western_Spindalis.Behavior: Forages in fruiting trees. Rare but regular visitor to Florida Keys from Bahamas and Cuba.
Western_Spindalis.Habitat: Forest and woodland of the Bahamas and Cuba. Rare but regular visitor to southern Florida.
Western_Spindalis.Similar Looking Birds: No similar bird in Florida range. Male with black-white-orange pattern unique.
Western_Spindalis.Best Ways to Identify: Male unmistakable: black head, white stripes, orange breast. Rare Florida visitor from Caribbean islands.

Western_Tanager.Description: Male has red head, yellow body, and black wings with yellow and white wing bars; female yellow-green with wing bars.
Western_Tanager.Behavior: Forages in conifer canopy for insects; eats berries in migration; distinctive two-note burry song.
Western_Tanager.Habitat: Coniferous and mixed forests of western North America; breeds in mountains; widespread in migration.
Western_Tanager.Similar Looking Birds: Summer Tanager male is all red; Scarlet Tanager male has scarlet body; no other tanager has red head with yellow body.
Western_Tanager.Best Ways to Identify: Red head; yellow body; black wings with two white or yellow wing bars; male unmistakable; mountain conifer forests.

Western_Warbling-Vireo.Description: Small plain vireo, gray-green above, whitish below with faint yellowish wash on flanks. No wing bars. About 5 inches.
Western_Warbling-Vireo.Behavior: Sings persistently from dense foliage, a rambling warbling song. Forages slowly for insects in tree canopy.
Western_Warbling-Vireo.Habitat: Deciduous and mixed forests, riparian woodlands, and mountain slopes of western North America.
Western_Warbling-Vireo.Similar Looking Birds: Eastern Warbling-Vireo nearly identical. Cassin's Vireo has white spectacles and wing bars.
Western_Warbling-Vireo.Best Ways to Identify: Plain vireo with no wing bars or eye ring. Distinctive warbling song. Western range helpful for separation.

Western_Wood-Pewee.Description: Medium flycatcher with dark gray-olive plumage, two white wing bars, and slightly peaked head; no eye-ring.
Western_Wood-Pewee.Behavior: Sings harsh descending burry peeer call; sallies for insects from exposed dead branch; long-distance migrant.
Western_Wood-Pewee.Habitat: Open woodlands, forest edges, and riparian areas throughout western North America; winters in South America.
Western_Wood-Pewee.Similar Looking Birds: Eastern Wood-Pewee is very similar but different call; Empidonax flycatchers have eye-rings; pewees have longer wings.
Western_Wood-Pewee.Best Ways to Identify: Dark gray-olive; two wing bars; no eye-ring; flat-headed look; harsh burry call; open woodland sallying behavior.

Whimbrel.Description: Large brownish shorebird with long downcurved bill, striped crown, and dark eyeline; mottled brown overall plumage.
Whimbrel.Behavior: Migrates along both coasts; eats fiddler crabs and invertebrates; gives rapid repetitive tititi whistles.
Whimbrel.Habitat: Tundra for breeding; coastal mudflats, wetlands, and beaches during migration; winters on tropical coasts.
Whimbrel.Similar Looking Birds: Long-billed Curlew is larger with very long bill and cinnamon underparts; Bristle-thighed Curlew similar but rare.
Whimbrel.Best Ways to Identify: Long downcurved bill; striped crown with pale central stripe; brown mottled plumage; rapid whistled call on coasts.

Whip-poor-will.Description: Cryptically patterned brown and gray nightjar with large dark eyes, wide mouth, and rictal bristles; white throat patch.
Whip-poor-will.Behavior: Nocturnal insect hunter; sings loud repetitive whip-poor-will at dusk and dawn; sits motionless on ground by day.
Whip-poor-will.Habitat: Deciduous and mixed forests of eastern North America; sits on leaf litter; rare and declining species.
Whip-poor-will.Similar Looking Birds: Chuck-will's-widow is larger with buff throat; Common Nighthawk has white wing bar and pointed wings.
Whip-poor-will.Best Ways to Identify: Cryptic leaf-litter camouflage; repetitive whip-poor-will song at night; white tail corners in male; wide gaping mouth.

Whiskered_Auklet.Description: Small dark auklet with elaborate white facial plumes (whiskers). Dark gray with small red bill with white basal plate. About 7.5 inches.
Whiskered_Auklet.Behavior: Feeds on zooplankton in tidal rips. Found mainly in central Aleutian Islands. Dives and forages in strong currents.
Whiskered_Auklet.Habitat: Central Aleutian Islands and adjacent Pacific; strongly tied to tidal rips with strong currents. Rarely seen far from Aleutians.
Whiskered_Auklet.Similar Looking Birds: Crested Auklet has forward crest. Whiskered Auklet's multiple white facial plumes distinctive.
Whiskered_Auklet.Best Ways to Identify: Multiple white facial whisker plumes. Small size. Found in Aleutian Island tidal rips. Rarely far from the Aleutians.

Whiskered_Screech-Owl.Description: Small owl with ear tufts. Gray-brown streaked plumage, yellow eyes. Bold facial disk whisker marks. About 7 inches.
Whiskered_Screech-Owl.Behavior: Nocturnal insect hunter. Regular resident in oak-pine forest of southeastern Arizona and southwestern New Mexico mountains.
Whiskered_Screech-Owl.Habitat: Oak-pine woodland in mountain canyons of southeastern Arizona and southwestern New Mexico. Year-round resident.
Whiskered_Screech-Owl.Similar Looking Birds: Western Screech-Owl similar but larger with different call. Whiskered has bolder whisker marks.
Whiskered_Screech-Owl.Best Ways to Identify: Bold whisker marks on facial disk. Small ear-tufted owl. Southeastern Arizona mountain oak woodland resident.

Whiskered_Tern.Description: Small marsh tern. Breeding adult has gray body, black cap, white cheeks, red bill. Non-breeding gray and white. About 10 inches.
Whiskered_Tern.Behavior: Forages over freshwater marshes for insects and small fish. Rare vagrant to Atlantic coast from Eurasia.
Whiskered_Tern.Habitat: Breeds on freshwater marshes in Eurasia and Africa. Rare vagrant to eastern North America.
Whiskered_Tern.Similar Looking Birds: Black Tern in non-breeding. Breeding Whiskered has gray belly, not black.
Whiskered_Tern.Best Ways to Identify: Gray belly (not black like Black Tern) with white cheeks in breeding. Non-breeding pale gray overall.

White-breasted_Nuthatch.Description: Black crown contrasting white face and underparts; blue-gray back; rusty vent area; compact neckless body.
White-breasted_Nuthatch.Behavior: Creeps headfirst down tree trunks; caches seeds; nasal yank-yank calls; pairs defend territory year-round.
White-breasted_Nuthatch.Habitat: Deciduous and mixed forests, oak woodlands, and wooded suburbs throughout North America.
White-breasted_Nuthatch.Similar Looking Birds: Red-breasted Nuthatch has rusty underparts and white eyebrow; Pygmy Nuthatch is tiny and brown-capped.
White-breasted_Nuthatch.Best Ways to Identify: Black cap; white face; creeping headfirst down trees; nasal calls; blue-gray back; compact stocky body.
