White-capped_Albatross.Description: Medium mollymawk albatross. White head and body, dark gray-black back and wings, yellow bill. About 36 inches wingspan.
White-capped_Albatross.Behavior: Pelagic wanderer from New Zealand subantarctic islands. Very rare vagrant to North American Pacific coast.
White-capped_Albatross.Habitat: Southern Ocean, particularly waters off New Zealand. Very rare vagrant to North American Pacific coast.
White-capped_Albatross.Similar Looking Birds: Salvin's Albatross has grayish head. White-capped has cleaner white head.
White-capped_Albatross.Best Ways to Identify: Very white head and forehead contrasting with dark back. Rare vagrant albatross. Southern Ocean species rare in North America.

White-cheeked_Pintail.Description: Slender dabbling duck with brown streaked body, white cheek and throat, red-based gray bill. Long pointed tail. About 17 inches.
White-cheeked_Pintail.Behavior: Dabbles in shallow saltwater and brackish lagoons. Less wary than other ducks. Found in Caribbean and South America; vagrant to Florida.
White-cheeked_Pintail.Habitat: Caribbean wetlands, mangroves, coastal lagoons, and brackish ponds. Florida records mostly in South Florida lagoons and ponds.
White-cheeked_Pintail.Similar Looking Birds: Northern Pintail similar shape but has white neck stripe and different overall coloring.
White-cheeked_Pintail.Best Ways to Identify: Bright white cheek patch and throat contrasting with brown body unmistakable. Red bill base visible at close range.

White-chinned_Petrel.Description: Large all-dark petrel with pale ivory bill, white chin patch (variable, sometimes absent). About 22 inches.
White-chinned_Petrel.Behavior: Large and aggressive. Follows ships. Breeds on South Atlantic and Indian Ocean islands. Very rare vagrant to North Atlantic.
White-chinned_Petrel.Habitat: Southern Ocean. Very rare vagrant to North American Atlantic and Pacific coasts.
White-chinned_Petrel.Similar Looking Birds: Parkinson's Petrel similar but all black with pale bill. White chin patch of White-chinned variable.
White-chinned_Petrel.Best Ways to Identify: Large dark petrel with pale bill. White chin patch variable. Follows ships. Very rare southern vagrant.

White-collared_Swift.Description: Very large swift. Entirely black with distinctive white collar around neck. Large size and collar unmistakable. About 8 inches with 18-inch wingspan.
White-collared_Swift.Behavior: Feeds on flying insects in fast, powerful flight. Forms huge flocks. Rare vagrant to southern US from Mexico and Central America.
White-collared_Swift.Habitat: Tropical and subtropical mountain forests from Mexico to South America. Rare vagrant to Texas and Florida.
White-collared_Swift.Similar Looking Birds: Chimney and Vaux's Swifts much smaller. White collar unique among swifts.
White-collared_Swift.Best Ways to Identify: Very large size for a swift with conspicuous white collar. All-black plumage. Rare vagrant in southern US.

White-crested_Elaenia.Description: Small flycatcher, olive above, pale below. White crown crest visible when raised, two wing bars. About 6 inches.
White-crested_Elaenia.Behavior: Migratory South American species. Very rare vagrant to North American Atlantic coast.
White-crested_Elaenia.Habitat: Woodland and scrub of South America. Very rare vagrant to Atlantic coast.
White-crested_Elaenia.Similar Looking Birds: Other elaenias very similar. White crown crest when raised.
White-crested_Elaenia.Best Ways to Identify: Olive flycatcher with white crown crest visible when raised. Two wing bars. Very rare South American vagrant.

White-crowned_Pigeon.Description: Large dark gray pigeon with brilliant white crown. Iridescent neck feathers with scaly pattern. Red eye ring. About 14 inches.
White-crowned_Pigeon.Behavior: Feeds on fruit, especially poisonwood and other tropical trees. Nests in mangroves. Found in Florida Keys and Everglades.
White-crowned_Pigeon.Habitat: Coastal mangrove forests and tropical hardwood hammocks in Florida Keys and Everglades. Common in Caribbean.
White-crowned_Pigeon.Similar Looking Birds: Scaly-naped Pigeon darker and lacks the brilliant white crown cap.
White-crowned_Pigeon.Best Ways to Identify: Brilliant white crown cap contrasting with dark gray body unmistakable. Large pigeon found in Florida Keys and Caribbean.

White-crowned_Sparrow.Description: Bold black and white striped crown with gray face and breast; pinkish or orangish bill; streaked brown back.
White-crowned_Sparrow.Behavior: Scratches in leaf litter; sings whistled songs varying by subspecies; common migrant and winter feeder bird.
White-crowned_Sparrow.Habitat: Brushy areas, thickets, roadsides, and gardens; breeds in tundra and mountain meadow edges across North America.
White-crowned_Sparrow.Similar Looking Birds: White-throated Sparrow has white throat patch and yellow lore; Golden-crowned Sparrow has yellow crown center.
White-crowned_Sparrow.Best Ways to Identify: Bold black and white crown stripes; gray face; pinkish bill; streaked brown back; very common at feeders in winter.

White-eared_Hummingbird.Description: Medium hummingbird. Male has iridescent green body, purple crown, red bill with black tip, bold white stripe behind eye. About 3.75 inches.
White-eared_Hummingbird.Behavior: Feeds on nectar; visits mountain flowers. Rare summer visitor to Arizona mountain canyons from Mexico. Males sing from exposed perches.
White-eared_Hummingbird.Habitat: Pine-oak mountain forests of Mexico and Central America. Rare visitor to Chiricahua Mountains and other Arizona sky islands.
White-eared_Hummingbird.Similar Looking Birds: Broad-billed Hummingbird similar green. White-eared's bold white eye stripe unique.
White-eared_Hummingbird.Best Ways to Identify: Bold white stripe behind eye diagnostic. Red bill with black tip. Male's purple crown and green body. Rare in Arizona mountains.

White-eyed_Parakeet.Description: Large parakeet, green with red scattered on face and wings, white eye ring, long tail. About 13 inches.
White-eyed_Parakeet.Behavior: Gregarious and noisy. Feral population in Florida. Forages in fruiting trees.
White-eyed_Parakeet.Habitat: Forest and woodland. Feral populations in Florida. Native to South America.
White-eyed_Parakeet.Similar Looking Birds: Mitred Parakeet more red on face. Blue-crowned Parakeet has blue crown. White eye ring distinctive.
White-eyed_Parakeet.Best Ways to Identify: White eye ring on green parakeet. Scattered red on face and wings. Long tail. Florida feral.

White-eyed_Vireo.Description: Small vireo with white eye, yellow spectacles, two white wing bars, yellow flanks, and olive-green upperparts.
White-eyed_Vireo.Behavior: Sings loud explosive quick-with-the-beer-quick song in dense thickets; secretive but vocal; mimics other birds.
White-eyed_Vireo.Habitat: Dense brushy thickets, shrubby forest edges, and overgrown fields of eastern and southeastern US.
White-eyed_Vireo.Similar Looking Birds: Bell's Vireo has faint spectacles and darker eye; other vireos lack white eye and yellow spectacles combination.
White-eyed_Vireo.Best Ways to Identify: White iris; yellow spectacles around white eye; yellow flanks; two wing bars; explosive song from dense thickets.

White-faced_Ibis.Description: Dark glossy maroon-bronze ibis with long downcurved bill; breeding adult has white feathering bordering bare red face.
White-faced_Ibis.Behavior: Probes mud with curved bill for invertebrates; flocks fly in lines and V formations; colonial nester.
White-faced_Ibis.Habitat: Freshwater and alkaline marshes, flooded fields, and wetlands of western US and Gulf Coast.
White-faced_Ibis.Similar Looking Birds: Glossy Ibis lacks white face border and has blue facial skin; both very similar in non-breeding plumage.
White-faced_Ibis.Best Ways to Identify: White facial border in breeding; glossy maroon plumage; red facial skin; long downcurved bill; western US marshes.

White-faced_Storm-Petrel.Description: Unique storm-petrel, pale gray and brown above with white face and underparts, dark eye stripe. Bouncing sea-skimmer. About 8 inches.
White-faced_Storm-Petrel.Behavior: Unique feeding posture: skips along water surface with feet pushing off. Rare vagrant to North American Atlantic coast.
White-faced_Storm-Petrel.Habitat: Atlantic and Indian Oceans; breeds on islands. Rare vagrant to offshore North American Atlantic coast.
White-faced_Storm-Petrel.Similar Looking Birds: No other storm-petrel has white face and underparts with this bold patterning.
White-faced_Storm-Petrel.Best Ways to Identify: White face and underparts with dark eye stripe. Unique bouncing walking on water surface feeding method.

White-fronted_Amazon.Description: Medium parrot, green with white forehead, red lores, blue crown on male. About 10 inches. Smallest Amazona.
White-fronted_Amazon.Behavior: Active and vocal in flocks. Forages in trees for fruit. Small feral populations in Florida.
White-fronted_Amazon.Habitat: Tropical forest and dry woodland. Small feral populations in Florida. Native to Mexico and Central America.
White-fronted_Amazon.Similar Looking Birds: Red-lored Amazon larger. Lilac-crowned Amazon has lilac crown. Small size distinctive among Amazon parrots.
White-fronted_Amazon.Best Ways to Identify: White forehead with red lores on green parrot. Smallest Amazon parrot. Florida feral populations.

White-headed_Woodpecker.Description: Striking black woodpecker with entirely white head and large white wing patch visible in flight; male has red nape.
White-headed_Woodpecker.Behavior: Pries bark scales from ponderosa pine to extract seeds; quiet for a woodpecker; local and declining species.
White-headed_Woodpecker.Habitat: Ponderosa pine forests of the mountains of California, Oregon, Washington, and Idaho.
White-headed_Woodpecker.Similar Looking Birds: No other North American woodpecker has all-white head with black body; distinctive and unmistakable.
White-headed_Woodpecker.Best Ways to Identify: All-white head on black body; large white wing patch; ponderosa pine forest; male's small red nape patch.

White-necked_Petrel.Description: Large gadfly petrel, pale gray above with dark M-pattern, white underparts, white collar around nape. About 17 inches.
White-necked_Petrel.Behavior: Breeds on Kermadec Islands north of New Zealand. Migrates into North Pacific; very rare vagrant off Pacific coast.
White-necked_Petrel.Habitat: North Pacific in non-breeding season. Very rare vagrant to North American Pacific coast.
White-necked_Petrel.Similar Looking Birds: Juan Fernandez Petrel similar but lacks white collar. White-necked has distinctive white nape collar.
White-necked_Petrel.Best Ways to Identify: Distinctive white collar around nape. Large pale gadfly petrel. Very rare visitor to North Pacific coast.

White-rumped_Sandpiper.Description: Small sandpiper with long wings extending beyond tail. Brown streaked plumage, white rump, streaked breast. About 7.5 inches.
White-rumped_Sandpiper.Behavior: Long-distance migrant; winters in southern South America. Forages on mudflats. Common in eastern North America during migration.
White-rumped_Sandpiper.Habitat: Breeds on Arctic tundra. Migrates through Great Plains and Atlantic coast. Winters in South America.
White-rumped_Sandpiper.Similar Looking Birds: Baird's Sandpiper similar wings-past-tail shape. White rump distinguishes White-rumped.
White-rumped_Sandpiper.Best Ways to Identify: White rump patch visible in flight. Wings extend past tail at rest. Rusty scapulars in breeding plumage.

White-rumped_Shama.Description: Medium bird, male glossy black with chestnut belly, white rump, long graduated tail. About 9 inches.
White-rumped_Shama.Behavior: Superb singer with rich, varied song. Bold and curious. Introduced to Hawaii; competes with native species.
White-rumped_Shama.Habitat: Dense forest undergrowth. Introduced to Hawaii, found on Oahu, Kauai, and other islands.
White-rumped_Shama.Similar Looking Birds: No similar black-and-chestnut bird in Hawaii. Long tail and white rump distinctive.
White-rumped_Shama.Best Ways to Identify: Glossy black with chestnut belly and white rump. Long tail. Superb loud song. Hawaiian introduced species.

White-tailed_Eagle.Description: Huge eagle with very short white wedge-shaped tail, massive yellow bill. Brown body, pale head. About 37 inches.
White-tailed_Eagle.Behavior: Soars over coasts and large water bodies. Hunts fish, waterbirds, and mammals. Rare vagrant to Alaska and Atlantic coast.
White-tailed_Eagle.Habitat: Coastlines and large lakes of Europe and Asia. Rare vagrant to Alaska; rare on Atlantic coast.
White-tailed_Eagle.Similar Looking Birds: Bald Eagle similar but has longer tail and black body. White-tailed Eagle very short broad tail.
White-tailed_Eagle.Best Ways to Identify: Short white wedge-shaped tail, massive yellow bill, very broad wings. Old World counterpart to Bald Eagle.

White-tailed_Hawk.Description: Large hawk, gray above, white below with rufous shoulder patches, short white tail with dark subterminal band. About 23 inches.
White-tailed_Hawk.Behavior: Soars over coastal prairies in Texas. Attracted to grass fires to catch fleeing prey. Resident of South Texas.
White-tailed_Hawk.Habitat: Open coastal prairies and grasslands of southern Texas. Regular resident in sparse populations in southernmost Texas.
White-tailed_Hawk.Similar Looking Birds: Swainson's Hawk lacks white tail and rufous shoulders. White-tailed distinctive pattern.
White-tailed_Hawk.Best Ways to Identify: White tail with dark terminal band, rufous shoulder patches. Coastal prairie specialist of southern Texas.

White-tailed_Kite.Description: Elegant white and gray raptor with black shoulder patches, red eyes, and long white tail; falcon-like proportions.
White-tailed_Kite.Behavior: Hovers kestrel-like over grasslands hunting voles; roosts communally in winter; gives high whistled calls.
White-tailed_Kite.Habitat: Open grasslands, marshes, and agricultural fields of California, Texas, and Pacific Coast lowlands.
White-tailed_Kite.Similar Looking Birds: Mississippi Kite is gray throughout; Swallow-tailed Kite is black and white with forked tail; harriers have different shape.
White-tailed_Kite.Best Ways to Identify: White body; black shoulder patches; hovers persistently over grasslands; long white tail; red eye; gray wings.

White-tailed_Ptarmigan.Description: Small grouse; white in winter with black bill and eye; mottled brown and white in summer; white tail always visible.
White-tailed_Ptarmigan.Behavior: Lives above treeline year-round; roosts in snow; feeds on alpine willow buds and leaves; very tame bird.
White-tailed_Ptarmigan.Habitat: Alpine tundra above treeline in Rocky Mountains and Cascades; year-round resident in harsh mountain environments.
White-tailed_Ptarmigan.Similar Looking Birds: Willow and Rock Ptarmigan have black outer tail feathers; both are larger; White-tailed always shows white tail.
White-tailed_Ptarmigan.Best Ways to Identify: All-white tail in all seasons; very small size among ptarmigan; rocky alpine habitat; entirely white in winter.

White-tailed_Tropicbird.Description: Elegant white seabird with very long white central tail streamers, black eye stripe, yellow or orange bill. About 30 inches including tail.
White-tailed_Tropicbird.Behavior: Plunge-dives for fish. Floats with tail elevated. Breeds on tropical islands; found offshore in Atlantic and Pacific.
White-tailed_Tropicbird.Habitat: Tropical oceans worldwide. Breeds on Bermuda and Caribbean islands. Offshore in Gulf of Mexico and Atlantic.
White-tailed_Tropicbird.Similar Looking Birds: Red-billed and Red-tailed Tropicbirds differ in bill color and tail streamer color.
White-tailed_Tropicbird.Best Ways to Identify: Very long white tail streamers, white plumage, black eye stripe. Yellow or orange bill. Graceful aerial seabird.

White-throated_Needletail.Description: Very large swift. Dark brown with white throat, white undertail coverts, and white on back forming horseshoe shape. About 8 inches.
White-throated_Needletail.Behavior: Extremely fast flier; said to be one of the fastest birds in level flight. Rare vagrant to western Alaska and Pacific islands from Asia.
White-throated_Needletail.Habitat: Breeds in East Asian and Siberian forests. Migrates to Australia and Southeast Asia. Rare vagrant to western North America.
White-throated_Needletail.Similar Looking Birds: White-collared Swift has white collar. Needletail larger than other swifts with distinctive shape.
White-throated_Needletail.Best Ways to Identify: Very large size among swifts. White throat and horseshoe-shaped white back pattern. Needle- like tail visible at close range.

White-throated_Sparrow.Description: Brown-streaked sparrow with bold white throat patch, yellow lore spot, and black and white or brown and tan crown stripes.
White-throated_Sparrow.Behavior: Scratches loudly in leaf litter; sings clear Oh sweet Canada Canada whistled song; common feeder bird in winter.
White-throated_Sparrow.Habitat: Boreal forests for breeding; brushy thickets, forest edges, and gardens throughout eastern US in winter.
White-throated_Sparrow.Similar Looking Birds: White-crowned Sparrow lacks white throat patch and yellow lore; Golden-crowned Sparrow lacks distinct throat.
White-throated_Sparrow.Best Ways to Identify: White throat patch; yellow lore spot; black and white crown stripes; song translates as Oh sweet Canada Canada.

White-throated_Swift.Description: Fast-flying swift with black and white plumage; white throat and center of belly; black sides; white flanks patch.
White-throated_Swift.Behavior: Extremely fast flight; forages aerially for insects; nests in cliff crevices; chatters loudly in fast flocks.
White-throated_Swift.Habitat: Rocky cliffs, canyons, and mountain faces throughout western North America; forages widely over open country.
White-throated_Swift.Similar Looking Birds: Vaux's Swift is all dark brown; Black Swift is all black; no other western swift has bold black and white pattern.
White-throated_Swift.Best Ways to Identify: Black and white contrasting pattern; white throat and belly center; black sides; very fast flight near cliffs.

White-throated_Thrush.Description: Medium thrush, gray-brown above, white throat with brown streaks, orange-yellow bill. About 9.5 inches.
White-throated_Thrush.Behavior: Forages in forest understory for fruit. Rare vagrant to extreme southern Texas from Mexico.
White-throated_Thrush.Habitat: Humid forest of Mexico and Central America. Rare vagrant to southern Texas.
White-throated_Thrush.Similar Looking Birds: Clay-colored Thrush lacks white throat. Rufous-backed Robin has rufous back. American Robin has red breast.
White-throated_Thrush.Best Ways to Identify: White throat with dark streaking contrasts with brown upperparts. Orange bill. Rare Texas vagrant from Mexico.

White-tipped_Dove.Description: Medium-sized dove. Brown above, pale pinkish-buff below, iridescent neck patch, white tail tips visible in flight, red eye ring. About 11 inches.
White-tipped_Dove.Behavior: Walks on ground foraging for seeds and fruit. Relatively tame. Resident in southern Texas; common in Central and South America.
White-tipped_Dove.Habitat: Dense scrub, forests, and woodland edges in southern Texas (Lower Rio Grande Valley). Common in Mexico and Central America.
White-tipped_Dove.Similar Looking Birds: White-winged Dove larger with prominent wing patches. White-tipped has distinctive pale underparts.
White-tipped_Dove.Best Ways to Identify: Plain brown bird with white tail corners visible in flight, bare red orbital ring, and pale pinkish underparts.

White-winged_Crossbill.Description: Small finch with crossed mandibles; male pink-red with black wings and two bold white wing bars; female greenish.
White-winged_Crossbill.Behavior: Pries open spruce cones with crossed bill; nomadic following cone crops; chatters in fast flocks through spruces.
White-winged_Crossbill.Habitat: Boreal spruce forests of Canada and northern mountains; irrupts south when cone crops fail.
White-winged_Crossbill.Similar Looking Birds: Red Crossbill lacks white wing bars; Pine Grosbeak is much larger; Common Redpoll is streaked without crossed bill.
White-winged_Crossbill.Best Ways to Identify: Crossed bill tips; two bold white wing bars; pink-red male; nomadic boreal forest; spruce cone specialist.

White-winged_Dove.Description: Grayish-brown dove with bold white wing stripe, blue orbital ring around orange-red eye, and rounded tail with white tips.
White-winged_Dove.Behavior: Gives who cooks for you song; expanding northward from desert Southwest; common at feeders and urban areas.
White-winged_Dove.Habitat: Desert scrub, riparian woodlands, and urban areas; expanding range northward and eastward from core range.
White-winged_Dove.Similar Looking Birds: Mourning Dove has pointed tail without white tips; Inca Dove is much smaller and scaly; Eurasian Collared-Dove has collar.
White-winged_Dove.Best Ways to Identify: Bold white wing stripe on folded wing; blue eye-ring; orange eye; rounded tail with white corners; deserts and cities.

White-winged_Parakeet.Description: Small green parakeet with distinctive white and yellow wing patches. Short pointed tail, yellow bill. About 9 inches.
White-winged_Parakeet.Behavior: Established feral population in Miami and Los Angeles areas. Forms flocks in suburban areas.
White-winged_Parakeet.Habitat: Feral in suburban South Florida and Los Angeles. Original range is South America.
White-winged_Parakeet.Similar Looking Birds: Yellow-chevroned Parakeet very similar but has yellow-only wing chevron.
White-winged_Parakeet.Best Ways to Identify: White wing patch with yellow. Small green parakeet. Feral in Miami and Los Angeles suburban areas.

White-winged_Scoter.Description: Large sea duck; male black with teardrop white eye patch and white wing speculum; orange bill with black knob.
White-winged_Scoter.Behavior: Dives for mussels and clams; large winter flocks on Great Lakes and coastal waters; breeds on boreal lakes.
White-winged_Scoter.Habitat: Boreal lakes and rivers for nesting; winters on both coasts and Great Lakes of North America.
White-winged_Scoter.Similar Looking Birds: Surf Scoter lacks white wing patch; Black Scoter is all black with yellow bill knob; all scoters dark-bodied.
White-winged_Scoter.Best Ways to Identify: White speculum visible in flight and at rest; white teardrop eye mark; black body; orange bill with black knob.

White-winged_Tern.Description: Small marsh tern. Breeding adult has black body, white wings, red bill. Non-breeding gray and white. About 9.5 inches.
White-winged_Tern.Behavior: Forages over marshes picking insects and small fish from surface. Rare vagrant to North America from Eurasia.
White-winged_Tern.Habitat: Breeds on Eurasian freshwater marshes. Winters in Africa and Asia. Rare vagrant to both coasts of North America.
White-winged_Tern.Similar Looking Birds: Black Tern similar. Breeding White-winged has white wing coverts contrasting with black body.
White-winged_Tern.Best Ways to Identify: Breeding bird's white wings contrasting with black body unmistakable. Non-breeding similar to Black Tern but paler.

White_Ibis.Description: Medium wading bird, all white plumage, bright red downturned bill and face, red legs. About 25 inches.
White_Ibis.Behavior: Forages in shallow water and mudflats. Highly gregarious; flocks rest and nest in trees. Common in southeastern US.
White_Ibis.Habitat: Coastal marshes, mangroves, and freshwater wetlands of southeastern US. Common from Carolina to Texas.
White_Ibis.Similar Looking Birds: Scarlet Ibis bright red; hybrids can be intermediate. Wood Stork larger and black-winged.
White_Ibis.Best Ways to Identify: All-white plumage with red downturned bill and red face. Common wading bird in southeastern US coastal marshes.

White_Wagtail.Description: Medium wagtail, black and white pattern, gray back, white face with black throat and cap. About 7 inches.
White_Wagtail.Behavior: Walks rapidly on ground wagging long tail constantly. Breeds in western Alaska. Bold and conspicuous.
White_Wagtail.Habitat: Open areas near water, towns, and open ground. Breeds in western Alaska near human habitation.
White_Wagtail.Similar Looking Birds: Black-backed Wagtail very similar subspecies. Eastern Yellow Wagtail yellow below.
White_Wagtail.Best Ways to Identify: Black-and-white pattern with long wagging tail. White face, black throat. Western Alaska breeder and vagrant.

Whooper_Swan.Description: A large white swan with a long, straight neck and distinctive yellow-and-black bill pattern. Adults weigh 7-12 kg with a 2-meter wingspan.
Whooper_Swan.Behavior: Grazes on aquatic vegetation, grasses, and crops. Highly vocal with a trumpeting call. Migrates in family groups over long distances.
Whooper_Swan.Habitat: Breeds near lakes and rivers in northern Eurasia. Winters on coastal bays, flooded fields, and large lakes in temperate regions.
Whooper_Swan.Similar Looking Birds: Very similar to Trumpeter Swan in North America. Bewick's Swan is smaller with less yellow on bill. Mute Swan has orange bill.
Whooper_Swan.Best Ways to Identify: Large yellow patch on bill extending to a point (not rounded), straight neck posture, loud bugling call, and lack of knob on bill distinguish it.

Whooping_Crane.Description: Very large white crane with red and black head, black wingtips visible in flight; tallest North American bird.
Whooping_Crane.Behavior: Endangered; loud whooping calls carry miles; dances in courtship; migrates between Texas and Canada.
Whooping_Crane.Habitat: Aransas National Wildlife Refuge in Texas for wintering; Wood Buffalo National Park in Canada for breeding.
Whooping_Crane.Similar Looking Birds: Sandhill Crane is gray; Snow Goose is smaller; Trumpeter Swan lacks red crown and black face mask.
Whooping_Crane.Best Ways to Identify: Tall all-white bird with red crown and black mask; black wingtips; very rare and endangered; loud whooping call.

Wild_Turkey.Description: Very large ground bird; male iridescent bronze and black with bare blue and red head, spurs, and fanned tail display.
Wild_Turkey.Behavior: Males gobble and strut in spring; forages for acorns and insects; roosts in trees; large flocks in winter.
Wild_Turkey.Habitat: Deciduous and mixed forests, open woodlands, and brushy edges throughout North America.
Wild_Turkey.Similar Looking Birds: Domestic turkey is very similar but tends to be fatter; no other bird could be confused with a Wild Turkey.
Wild_Turkey.Best Ways to Identify: Very large size; bronze iridescent body; bare red-blue head; fan tail display in male; gobbling call.

Willet.Description: Large gray-brown shorebird appearing plain at rest but revealing bold black and white wing pattern in flight.
Willet.Behavior: Calls pill-will-willet loudly; aggressive near nest; probes mud for invertebrates; common coastal shorebird.
Willet.Habitat: Coastal beaches, marshes, and mudflats; interior birds breed on prairie wetlands; two distinct subspecies.
Willet.Similar Looking Birds: Greater Yellowlegs has yellow legs and spotted back; Godwits have upturned or straight longer bills.
Willet.Best Ways to Identify: Bold black and white wing stripe; plain gray-brown at rest; thick straight bill; loud pill-will-willet call.

Williamsons_Sapsucker.Description: Male black with white wing patches, red throat, and yellow belly; female looks completely different with brown barring.
Williamsons_Sapsucker.Behavior: Drills sap wells in conifers; licks sap and catches insects attracted to it; quiet compared to other sapsuckers.
Williamsons_Sapsucker.Habitat: Mature coniferous forests of Rocky Mountains and Sierra Nevada mountains of western North America.
Williamsons_Sapsucker.Similar Looking Birds: Male unlike any other woodpecker; female resembles Northern Flicker; Yellow-bellied Sapsucker different pattern.
Williamsons_Sapsucker.Best Ways to Identify: Male's black body with white wing patches and red throat; yellow belly; extreme sexual dimorphism in this species.

Willow_Flycatcher.Description: Plain olive-brown Empidonax with faint eye-ring, two white wing bars, and olive-gray breast; no distinctive markings.
Willow_Flycatcher.Behavior: Sings fitz-bew! or sneeze-like song; identified almost exclusively by voice; nests in willows near water.
Willow_Flycatcher.Habitat: Willow and alder thickets near streams, wet meadows, and marsh edges throughout North America.
Willow_Flycatcher.Similar Looking Birds: Alder Flycatcher is essentially identical but sings fee-bee-o; other Empidonax flycatchers require voice for ID.
Willow_Flycatcher.Best Ways to Identify: Fitz-bew call essential for identification; faint eye-ring; willow habitat; olive-brown plumage; two wing bars.

Willow_Ptarmigan.Description: Largest ptarmigan; male brick-red head and white body in spring; all white in winter; black outer tail feathers.
Willow_Ptarmigan.Behavior: Males cackle and display in spring; forms large winter flocks; forages for willow buds; walks on snow via feathered feet.
Willow_Ptarmigan.Habitat: Arctic and subarctic tundra; associated with willow shrub thickets; widespread across northern North America.
Willow_Ptarmigan.Similar Looking Birds: Rock Ptarmigan is grayer with black lore line in male; White-tailed Ptarmigan has white outer tail feathers.
Willow_Ptarmigan.Best Ways to Identify: Black outer tail feathers; red combs over eyes in male; brick-red head in spring breeding plumage; willow tundra.

Willow_Warbler.Description: Small leaf warbler, olive-green above, pale yellowish below with pale supercilium. About 4.5 inches. Flesh-colored legs.
Willow_Warbler.Behavior: Active insect forager in tree canopy. Beautiful descending song. Rare vagrant to western and eastern Alaska.
Willow_Warbler.Habitat: Deciduous woodland, scrub, and forest edges across Europe and Asia. Rare vagrant to Alaska.
Willow_Warbler.Similar Looking Birds: Chiffchaff nearly identical but has dark legs. Arctic Warbler has wing bar. Yellow-browed Warbler has two wing bars.
Willow_Warbler.Best Ways to Identify: Flesh-colored legs (vs black in Chiffchaff). Plain wings no bars. Pale yellowish below. Very rare Alaska vagrant.

Wilsons_Phalarope.Description: Medium shorebird; breeding female has black and chestnut neck stripe on gray back; white underparts; needle-like bill.
Wilsons_Phalarope.Behavior: Female is brightly colored; polyandrous; spins in circles on water to stir up invertebrates; swims while feeding.
Wilsons_Phalarope.Habitat: Prairie potholes and marshes for breeding; large saline lakes during migration; winters in South America.
Wilsons_Phalarope.Similar Looking Birds: Red-necked Phalarope is smaller with shorter bill; Red Phalarope is stockier with broader bill; both more oceanic.
Wilsons_Phalarope.Best Ways to Identify: Needle-like thin bill; female's bold black and chestnut neck stripe; spinning feeding behavior on water surface.

Wilsons_Plover.Description: Medium plover with single broad breast band, disproportionately thick black bill, and pinkish legs; stocky build.
Wilsons_Plover.Behavior: Forages for fiddler crabs and ghost crabs on beaches; calls soft wit notes; nests in open beach scrapes.
Wilsons_Plover.Habitat: Sandy beaches, tidal flats, and barrier islands along Atlantic and Gulf coasts of southeastern US.
Wilsons_Plover.Similar Looking Birds: Semipalmated Plover has orange bill base and smaller bill; Piping Plover is paler with orange bill.
Wilsons_Plover.Best Ways to Identify: Very thick black bill; wide black breast band; pinkish legs; single breast band; sandy coastal beach habitat.

Wilsons_Snipe.Description: Plump brown shorebird with extremely long straight bill, bold buffy crown stripes, and streaked brown camouflage.
Wilsons_Snipe.Behavior: Probes deep in mud for earthworms; flushes explosively with scaipe call; male makes winnowing display flight.
Wilsons_Snipe.Habitat: Freshwater marshes, wet meadows, and boggy fields throughout North America; secretive among dense vegetation.
Wilsons_Snipe.Similar Looking Birds: American Woodcock is plumper with eyes set far back; dowitchers are longer necked and flock-flying birds.
Wilsons_Snipe.Best Ways to Identify: Extremely long bill; bold buffy head stripes; explosive flushing; camouflaged brown plumage; wet field habitat.

Wilsons_Storm-Petrel.Description: Small dark storm-petrel with white rump, square-cut tail, long legs with yellow-webbed feet visible in flight. About 7 inches.
Wilsons_Storm-Petrel.Behavior: Very abundant seabird worldwide. Patters on water surface feeding. Breeds in Antarctic; migrates north in summer.
Wilsons_Storm-Petrel.Habitat: Atlantic and Pacific Oceans. Common Atlantic coast in summer when Southern Hemisphere breeders migrate north.
Wilsons_Storm-Petrel.Similar Looking Birds: Leach's Storm-Petrel larger with forked tail. Wilson's has square tail and longer legs.
Wilsons_Storm-Petrel.Best Ways to Identify: Square tail, yellow-webbed feet dangling in flight. White rump. Small dark seabird very common in Atlantic summer.

Wilsons_Warbler.Description: Small yellow warbler; male has black cap on bright yellow face and underparts; female may have faint dark cap.
Wilsons_Warbler.Behavior: Very active and energetic; flicks wings; catches insects aerially; sings rapid staccato chi-chi-chi song.
Wilsons_Warbler.Habitat: Streamside willows, alder thickets, and moist mountain shrubs; migrates throughout North America.
Wilsons_Warbler.Similar Looking Birds: Yellow Warbler lacks black cap; Hooded Warbler male has black hood not just cap; Common Yellowthroat has mask.
Wilsons_Warbler.Best Ways to Identify: Bright yellow face and underparts; round black cap in male; energetic flicking wing behavior; willow thickets.

Winter_Wren.Description: Tiny dark brown wren with very short upright tail, barred plumage, and pale eyebrow; round compact body shape.
Winter_Wren.Behavior: Creeps mouse-like through dense undergrowth; sings extraordinarily long complex song for its tiny size.
Winter_Wren.Habitat: Dense coniferous forest undergrowth, windfall tangles, and forested ravines of eastern North America.
Winter_Wren.Similar Looking Birds: Pacific Wren is nearly identical western counterpart; Marsh Wren and Sedge Wren prefer open wetlands.
Winter_Wren.Best Ways to Identify: Tiny size; very short upright stubby tail; dark brown barred plumage; dense forest floor habitat; loud complex song.

Wood_Duck.Description: Male has iridescent green and purple crested head with white facial stripes; female gray-brown with white eye-ring.
Wood_Duck.Behavior: Nests in tree cavities; ducklings jump from nest on first day; male's rising squeaky call; perches in trees.
Wood_Duck.Habitat: Wooded swamps, beaver ponds, and flooded forests throughout eastern and Pacific Coast North America.
Wood_Duck.Similar Looking Birds: Mandarin Duck male similar but different head pattern; female resembles other female ducks but has white eye-ring.
Wood_Duck.Best Ways to Identify: Ornate iridescent male; crested head with white facial lines; female's white teardrop eye-ring; wooded wetland.

Wood_Sandpiper.Description: Medium sandpiper. Brown spotted upperparts, white supercilium, white underparts with streaked breast, yellow legs. About 8 inches.
Wood_Sandpiper.Behavior: Bobs tail. Forages in freshwater wetlands. Rare but regular vagrant to western Alaska; rare elsewhere in North America.
Wood_Sandpiper.Habitat: Breeds in Eurasian boreal forests and bogs. Winters in Africa and Asia. Rare vagrant to western Alaska.
Wood_Sandpiper.Similar Looking Birds: Solitary Sandpiper very similar. Wood Sandpiper has white rump and different leg color.
Wood_Sandpiper.Best Ways to Identify: White spotted brown back, white rump in flight, yellow legs. Regular vagrant in western Alaska.

Wood_Stork.Description: Large white wading bird with bare dark gray head and neck, black flight feathers, and thick down-curved bill.
Wood_Stork.Behavior: Uses tactile feeding method swinging bill through water; colonial nester in cypress trees; soars on thermals.
Wood_Stork.Habitat: Freshwater and coastal wetlands, cypress swamps of southeastern US; expanding nesting northward.
Wood_Stork.Similar Looking Birds: Great Egret is all white including flight feathers; Whooping Crane is taller with different profile in flight.
Wood_Stork.Best Ways to Identify: Bald dark head; black flight feathers on white body; thick decurved bill; soars with neck extended; southeastern US.

Wood_Thrush.Description: Reddish-brown head and back with white underparts boldly spotted with large black spots; orange-red eye-ring.
Wood_Thrush.Behavior: Sings beautiful flute-like ee-oh-lay phrases; forages on leaf litter; declining due to forest fragmentation.
Wood_Thrush.Habitat: Moist deciduous forests of eastern North America; requires large intact forest tracts for breeding success.
Wood_Thrush.Similar Looking Birds: Hermit Thrush is smaller with rufous tail; Veery has less distinct spotting; Swainson's has buffy eye-ring.
Wood_Thrush.Best Ways to Identify: Reddish-brown head contrasting with spotted white breast; large dark spots; orange eye-ring; forest interior.

Wood_Warbler.Description: Medium leaf warbler with bright yellow supercilium and throat, white belly, green back. About 5 inches.
Wood_Warbler.Behavior: Forages high in deciduous canopy. Distinctive song with spinning trill. Very rare vagrant to northeastern North America.
Wood_Warbler.Habitat: Mature deciduous forest in Europe. Very rare vagrant to northeastern North America.
Wood_Warbler.Similar Looking Birds: Yellow-browed Warbler smaller with wing bars. Willow Warbler lacks bright yellow supercilium.
Wood_Warbler.Best Ways to Identify: Bright yellow supercilium and throat contrast with white belly. Green back. Very rare European vagrant.

Woodhouses_Scrub-Jay.Description: Medium scrub-jay, blue above, gray-brown back, whitish below with incomplete blue breast band. About 11 inches.
Woodhouses_Scrub-Jay.Behavior: Forages on ground and in shrubs for acorns, insects, and berries. Caches food. Often found in pinyon-juniper habitat.
Woodhouses_Scrub-Jay.Habitat: Arid scrub, pinyon-juniper woodland, and chaparral of interior western United States from Oregon south to Mexico.
Woodhouses_Scrub-Jay.Similar Looking Birds: California Scrub-Jay coastal and brighter blue. Florida Scrub-Jay has whitish forehead and different range.
Woodhouses_Scrub-Jay.Best Ways to Identify: Interior western range. Dull blue with grayish back. Incomplete blue breast band. Pinyon-juniper habitat preference.

Worm-eating_Warbler.Description: Medium warbler, olive-green above, buff below, bold black crown stripes on buff head. About 5 inches.
Worm-eating_Warbler.Behavior: Forages on ground and in dead leaf clusters searching for caterpillars. Walks more than it hops.
Worm-eating_Warbler.Habitat: Mature deciduous forest on hillsides in eastern United States. Winters in Caribbean and Central America.
Worm-eating_Warbler.Similar Looking Birds: Swainson's Warbler has plain crown. Ovenbird has orange crown stripe. Bold head striping distinctive.
Worm-eating_Warbler.Best Ways to Identify: Bold black-and-buff striped head. Olive above, buff below. Dead leaf cluster forager. Hillside forest specialist.

Worthens_Sparrow.Description: Small sparrow, rusty cap, gray face, plain pale below with white wing bars. Similar to Field Sparrow. About 5.5 inches.
Worthens_Sparrow.Behavior: Forages in open grassland and scrub. Very rare vagrant to New Mexico from Mexico. Globally endangered.
Worthens_Sparrow.Habitat: Grasslands and shrubby areas of northeastern Mexico. Very rare vagrant to New Mexico.
Worthens_Sparrow.Similar Looking Birds: Field Sparrow has pink bill and eye ring. Clay-colored Sparrow has brown cheek patch. Nearly identical to Field Sparrow.
Worthens_Sparrow.Best Ways to Identify: Nearly identical to Field Sparrow. Very rare Mexico vagrant to New Mexico. Dark loral area helpful.

Wrentit.Description: Small brown bird with long rounded tail, short bill, white eye, and lightly streaked breast; tit-like and wren-like.
Wrentit.Behavior: Very secretive; rarely seen despite loud bouncing-ball song; pairs stay together year-round in dense chaparral.
Wrentit.Habitat: Coastal chaparral and dense scrub of California and southern Oregon; highly resident in small territories.
Wrentit.Similar Looking Birds: Wrens are more boldly barred; titmice have different body shape; Bewick's Wren has more prominent supercilium.
Wrentit.Best Ways to Identify: White eye in brown face; long round tail; staccato bouncing-ball song accelerating into trill; coastal chaparral.

Xantuss_Hummingbird.Description: Medium hummingbird. Male has green body, cinnamon- rufous belly, white stripe behind eye, red bill. Female similar but duller. About 3.5 inches.
Xantuss_Hummingbird.Behavior: Feeds on nectar and small insects. Endemic to Baja California; extremely rare vagrant to California. Active and territorial at feeders.
Xantuss_Hummingbird.Habitat: Endemic to Baja California Sur, Mexico, in scrub and woodland. Very rare vagrant to southern California.
Xantuss_Hummingbird.Similar Looking Birds: White-eared Hummingbird similar. Xantus's rufous belly distinctive.
Xantuss_Hummingbird.Best Ways to Identify: Rufous belly and white eye stripe unique combination. Red bill. Very rare vagrant to California from Baja California.

Yellow-bellied_Flycatcher.Description: Small Empidonax with yellow underparts including throat, yellow eye-ring, olive back, and two yellowish wing bars.
Yellow-bellied_Flycatcher.Behavior: Sings soft per-wee or che-bunk calls; found in boreal bogs; most yellow-tinged of Empidonax flycatchers.
Yellow-bellied_Flycatcher.Habitat: Boreal forest bogs, spruce-fir forests, and moist northern woodlands; migrates through eastern US.
Yellow-bellied_Flycatcher.Similar Looking Birds: Acadian Flycatcher has yellow only on sides; other Empidonax lack yellow throat; Yellow Warbler has different shape.
Yellow-bellied_Flycatcher.Best Ways to Identify: Yellow throat and belly; yellow eye-ring; olive back; greenish tones throughout; boreal bog breeding habitat.

Yellow-bellied_Sapsucker.Description: Black and white woodpecker; male has red crown and red throat; female has white throat; yellow belly wash; white wing stripe.
Yellow-bellied_Sapsucker.Behavior: Drills rows of sap wells in trees; many species drink sap from these wells; drumming is irregular and halting.
Yellow-bellied_Sapsucker.Habitat: Mixed and deciduous forests of eastern North America; breeds in northern forests; winters in southeastern US.
Yellow-bellied_Sapsucker.Similar Looking Birds: Williamson's Sapsucker is different; Red-naped Sapsucker has red nape patch; Hairy Woodpecker lacks yellow belly.
Yellow-bellied_Sapsucker.Best Ways to Identify: White wing stripe; yellow belly; red crown; irregular halting drumming; rows of sap wells drilled in tree trunks.

Yellow-billed_Cardinal.Description: Small bird, red head, black back, white below, bright yellow bill. About 6 inches.
Yellow-billed_Cardinal.Behavior: Forages on ground for seeds near water. Introduced to Hawaii; present on several islands.
Yellow-billed_Cardinal.Habitat: Open areas near water, gardens, and parks. Introduced to Hawaii.
Yellow-billed_Cardinal.Similar Looking Birds: Red-crested Cardinal has crest and gray back. Northern Cardinal has all-red body.
Yellow-billed_Cardinal.Best Ways to Identify: Yellow bill with red head and black back. White belly. Introduced to Hawaii. No crest unlike Red-crested Cardinal.

Yellow-billed_Cuckoo.Description: Slender brownish bird with white underparts, yellow bill base, rufous wing flash, and bold white tail spots below.
Yellow-billed_Cuckoo.Behavior: Eats caterpillars especially tent caterpillars; slow deliberate movements; calls hollow ka-ka-ka-kow series.
Yellow-billed_Cuckoo.Habitat: Dense riparian woodlands, thickets, and forest edges of North America; declining in western US populations.
Yellow-billed_Cuckoo.Similar Looking Birds: Black-billed Cuckoo has red eye-ring and smaller tail spots; Mangrove Cuckoo has buffy underparts.
Yellow-billed_Cuckoo.Best Ways to Identify: Yellow lower mandible; rufous flash in wing; bold white tail spots below; slender build; hollow wooden call series.

Yellow-billed_Loon.Description: Largest loon. Distinctive ivory-yellow upturned bill, black and white checkered back in breeding. About 34 inches.
Yellow-billed_Loon.Behavior: Dives for fish in deep Arctic lakes. Rare but regular winter visitor on Pacific and occasionally Atlantic coasts.
Yellow-billed_Loon.Habitat: Breeds on Arctic tundra lakes in North America and Siberia. Winters primarily on Pacific coast.
Yellow-billed_Loon.Similar Looking Birds: Common Loon very similar. Yellow-billed Loon's pale ivory-yellow upturned bill distinctive.
Yellow-billed_Loon.Best Ways to Identify: Pale ivory-yellow bill that appears upturned at tip. Largest loon species. Rare winter visitor on Pacific coast.

Yellow-billed_Magpie.Description: Black and white magpie with distinctive bright yellow bill and yellow facial skin patch; very long graduated tail.
Yellow-billed_Magpie.Behavior: Social and noisy; caches food; forages in oak woodlands and orchards; corvid intelligence; flocks in winter.
Yellow-billed_Magpie.Habitat: Endemic to Central Valley of California; oak woodlands, farmlands, and riparian areas only in California.
Yellow-billed_Magpie.Similar Looking Birds: Black-billed Magpie is identical in shape and pattern but has dark bill; no other yellow-billed magpie exists.
Yellow-billed_Magpie.Best Ways to Identify: Bright yellow bill; yellow facial skin; long black tail with iridescent sheen; endemic only to California's Central Valley.

Yellow-breasted_Bunting.Description: Medium bunting. Male chestnut above, bright yellow below with chestnut breast band. Female streaked yellow-buff. About 5.5 inches.
Yellow-breasted_Bunting.Behavior: Forages on ground for seeds. Rare vagrant to western Alaska. Globally endangered due to trapping in Asia.
Yellow-breasted_Bunting.Habitat: Wet scrub and meadows of Siberia and East Asia. Rare vagrant to western Alaska.
Yellow-breasted_Bunting.Similar Looking Birds: Pine Bunting has white head not yellow underparts. Yellow Warbler much smaller.
Yellow-breasted_Bunting.Best Ways to Identify: Bright yellow underparts with chestnut breast band on male. Rare Alaska vagrant. Globally endangered species.

Yellow-breasted_Chat.Description: Largest North American warbler; yellow breast, olive-green back, white spectacles, black lores, and heavy bill.
Yellow-breasted_Chat.Behavior: Sings bizarre mix of whistles, cackles, and hoots; often sings at night; very secretive in dense thickets.
Yellow-breasted_Chat.Habitat: Dense brushy thickets, overgrown fields, and shrubby streamside areas throughout temperate North America.
Yellow-breasted_Chat.Similar Looking Birds: No other warbler-like bird has yellow breast with white spectacles and black lore; Common Yellowthroat much smaller.
Yellow-breasted_Chat.Best Ways to Identify: Large size for warbler; bright yellow breast; white spectacles with black lore; bizarre varied song; dense thickets.

Yellow-browed_Bunting.Description: Medium bunting, streaked brown with yellow supercilium, black head with white crown stripe. About 6 inches.
Yellow-browed_Bunting.Behavior: Forages on ground for seeds. Very rare vagrant to western Alaska and Aleutian Islands from Siberia.
Yellow-browed_Bunting.Habitat: Mixed forest of Siberia. Very rare vagrant to western Alaska.
Yellow-browed_Bunting.Similar Looking Birds: Yellow-throated Bunting has yellow throat. Rustic Bunting has chestnut tones.
Yellow-browed_Bunting.Best Ways to Identify: Yellow supercilium on black head with white crown stripe. Very rare Alaska vagrant.

Yellow-browed_Warbler.Description: Small leaf warbler, olive-green above with two yellow-white wing bars, bold supercilium. About 4 inches.
Yellow-browed_Warbler.Behavior: Active and restless forager in canopy. Increasingly common vagrant to eastern North America in fall.
Yellow-browed_Warbler.Habitat: Forests of Siberia and Asia. Increasingly regular vagrant to northeastern North America in fall migration.
Yellow-browed_Warbler.Similar Looking Birds: Pallas's Leaf Warbler has crown stripe and rump patch. Hume's Warbler buffier with less distinct wing bars.
Yellow-browed_Warbler.Best Ways to Identify: Two bold pale wing bars with prominent supercilium. Small olive-green warbler. Increasingly regular fall vagrant.

Yellow-chevroned_Parakeet.Description: Small green parakeet with distinctive yellow wing patches. Short pointed tail, pale bill. About 9 inches.
Yellow-chevroned_Parakeet.Behavior: Established feral populations in Miami and Los Angeles. Often mixes with White-winged Parakeet.
Yellow-chevroned_Parakeet.Habitat: Feral in suburban South Florida and Los Angeles. Replaces White-winged Parakeet in much of Florida.
Yellow-chevroned_Parakeet.Similar Looking Birds: White-winged Parakeet has white in wing patch. Yellow- chevroned has only yellow chevron.
Yellow-chevroned_Parakeet.Best Ways to Identify: Yellow-only wing chevron, no white. Small green parakeet. Feral Miami and Los Angeles suburban areas.

Yellow-crowned_Night-Heron.Description: Medium gray heron with black head, white cheek patch, yellow crown, and red eye; stout bill; adults distinctive.
Yellow-crowned_Night-Heron.Behavior: Specializes in catching crabs and crayfish; more crepuscular and nocturnal; gives barking call in flight.
Yellow-crowned_Night-Heron.Habitat: Coastal mangroves, wooded swamps, and freshwater marshes of southeastern US and Gulf Coast.
Yellow-crowned_Night-Heron.Similar Looking Birds: Black-crowned Night-Heron has white and black head pattern and different crown color; immatures both similar brown.
Yellow-crowned_Night-Heron.Best Ways to Identify: Gray body; black face with white cheek patch; pale yellowish crown; red eye; stout bill for crushing crustaceans.

Yellow-eyed_Junco.Description: Medium junco with bright yellow iris, gray head, rusty back, white outer tail feathers. About 6.5 inches.
Yellow-eyed_Junco.Behavior: Forages on ground in pine-oak forest. Year-round resident in southeastern Arizona mountains.
Yellow-eyed_Junco.Habitat: Pine-oak forests of the Madrean sky islands in southeastern Arizona and New Mexico into Mexico.
Yellow-eyed_Junco.Similar Looking Birds: Dark-eyed Junco has dark eye. No other junco has yellow iris in range.
Yellow-eyed_Junco.Best Ways to Identify: Bright yellow iris distinctive. Rusty back. Pine-oak forest in Arizona sky islands. Year-round resident.

Yellow-faced_Grassquit.Description: Tiny finch. Male olive-green with bright yellow face markings and black breast. Female duller. About 4 inches.
Yellow-faced_Grassquit.Behavior: Forages for grass seeds in open areas. Rare vagrant to Florida and Texas from Caribbean and Mexico.
Yellow-faced_Grassquit.Habitat: Open grasslands and weedy areas. Rare visitor to southern Florida from Caribbean and Gulf Coast.
Yellow-faced_Grassquit.Similar Looking Birds: Black-faced Grassquit male blacker with less yellow. Bananaquit different pattern.
Yellow-faced_Grassquit.Best Ways to Identify: Yellow face markings and black breast on olive-green body. Tiny size. Rare Florida and Texas vagrant.

Yellow-footed_Gull.Description: Large gull, very dark gray back, bright yellow feet and legs, yellow bill with red spot. About 26 inches.
Yellow-footed_Gull.Behavior: Breeds on Gulf of California islands; post-breeding birds move to Salton Sea in summer. Closely related to Western Gull.
Yellow-footed_Gull.Habitat: Gulf of California and Salton Sea. Post-breeding visitors make Salton Sea their specialty summer location in California.
Yellow-footed_Gull.Similar Looking Birds: Western Gull almost identical but has pink legs. Yellow-footed Gull's bright yellow legs diagnostic.
Yellow-footed_Gull.Best Ways to Identify: Bright yellow legs and feet on large dark-backed gull. Salton Sea in summer. Very similar to Western Gull otherwise.

Yellow-fronted_Canary.Description: Small finch, olive-green above with yellow supercilium, yellow-green below, gray cheeks. About 4.5 inches.
Yellow-fronted_Canary.Behavior: Gregarious seed-eater in open areas. Introduced to Hawaii; common in dry open areas.
Yellow-fronted_Canary.Habitat: Open grasslands, scrub, and gardens. Introduced to Hawaii, particularly common on Oahu.
Yellow-fronted_Canary.Similar Looking Birds: Warbling White-eye has white eye ring. Anianiau smaller and brighter in Hawaii. Yellow supercilium distinctive.
Yellow-fronted_Canary.Best Ways to Identify: Yellow supercilium and yellow-green underparts. Gray cheeks. Introduced to Hawaiian open grasslands. Seed-eater.

Yellow-green_Vireo.Description: Medium vireo, olive-green above, yellow-green below and on sides. Gray crown, white supercilium, red eye. About 6 inches.
Yellow-green_Vireo.Behavior: Forages slowly through canopy, picking insects from leaves. Persistent singer like Red-eyed Vireo. Rare vagrant to Texas.
Yellow-green_Vireo.Habitat: Tropical forests of Central America and Mexico. Rare but regular vagrant along Texas Gulf Coast in fall.
Yellow-green_Vireo.Similar Looking Birds: Red-eyed Vireo very similar but whiter below with less yellow. Yellow-throated Vireo has wing bars and yellow throat.
Yellow-green_Vireo.Best Ways to Identify: Yellow-green coloration on underparts and sides. Red iris. Gray crown with white supercilium. Texas vagrant.

Yellow-headed_Amazon.Description: Medium parrot, green with yellow head increasing with age. Red wing patch, yellow-orange on wing bend. About 15 inches.
Yellow-headed_Amazon.Behavior: Critically endangered in Mexico; established small feral populations in California and Florida. Loud screeching calls.
Yellow-headed_Amazon.Habitat: Feral in Los Angeles and possibly Florida. Critically endangered in native Mexican and Central American range.
Yellow-headed_Amazon.Similar Looking Birds: Yellow-naped Amazon has yellow nape only. Yellow-headed has more extensive yellow head.
Yellow-headed_Amazon.Best Ways to Identify: Yellow head with red wing patch. Grows more yellow with age. Critically endangered Mexican species, feral in California.

Yellow-headed_Blackbird.Description: Male unmistakable with brilliant yellow head and breast on black body with white wing patches; female brownish.
Yellow-headed_Blackbird.Behavior: Nests over water in reeds; males sing harsh mechanical grinding songs; forages in large flocks on grain fields.
Yellow-headed_Blackbird.Habitat: Freshwater marshes with tall emergent vegetation; breeds in western North America; winters in southwestern US.
Yellow-headed_Blackbird.Similar Looking Birds: Male unmistakable; female resembles other blackbirds but has yellow wash on face and throat; no similar species.
Yellow-headed_Blackbird.Best Ways to Identify: Brilliant yellow head and breast on black body; white wing patches in male; unmistakable in fresh water marshes.

Yellow-headed_Caracara.Description: Medium caracara with yellowish head and underparts, brown back and wings, streaked face. About 16 inches.
Yellow-headed_Caracara.Behavior: Opportunistic feeder; eats ticks off cattle and scavenges. Very rare vagrant from Central America to Florida and Texas.
Yellow-headed_Caracara.Habitat: Open areas, pastures and roadsides of Central and South America. Very rare vagrant to Florida and Texas.
Yellow-headed_Caracara.Similar Looking Birds: Crested Caracara darker with crest. Yellow-headed smaller with yellow face and underparts.
Yellow-headed_Caracara.Best Ways to Identify: Yellow head and underparts, brown back. Small caracara. Very rare Central American vagrant to Florida and Texas.

Yellow-legged_Gull.Description: Large gull, pale gray back, bright yellow legs, yellow bill with red spot. Similar to Herring Gull. About 24 inches.
Yellow-legged_Gull.Behavior: Mediterranean and Atlantic European species. Very rare vagrant to northeastern North America. Bold scavenger at coasts and harbors.
Yellow-legged_Gull.Habitat: Mediterranean Sea, Atlantic coast of Europe, Azores, Canary Islands. Very rare vagrant to northeastern North America.
Yellow-legged_Gull.Similar Looking Birds: Herring Gull almost identical but has pink legs. Yellow-legged Gull's yellow legs diagnostic.
Yellow-legged_Gull.Best Ways to Identify: Yellow legs on large pale-backed gull. Very rare Atlantic vagrant. Similar to Lesser Black-backed but paler back.

Yellow-rumped_Warbler.Description: Gray warbler with yellow rump, yellow crown patch, and yellow shoulder patch; white or yellow throat depending on race.
Yellow-rumped_Warbler.Behavior: Most abundant warbler; eats bayberries enabling winter residency farther north; often in large flocks.
Yellow-rumped_Warbler.Habitat: Coniferous forests for breeding; widespread in migration; winters throughout southern US in shrubby areas.
Yellow-rumped_Warbler.Similar Looking Birds: Magnolia Warbler has yellow rump but different pattern; no other common warbler shows bold yellow rump in flight.
Yellow-rumped_Warbler.Best Ways to Identify: Bright yellow rump patch most conspicuous; yellow crown and shoulder patches; Audubon's has yellow throat.

Yellow-throated_Bunting.Description: Medium bunting. Male has black crest and face, bright yellow throat, white supercilium. Female duller. About 6 inches.
Yellow-throated_Bunting.Behavior: Forages on ground in woodland. Very rare vagrant to western Alaska from East Asia.
Yellow-throated_Bunting.Habitat: Woodland and scrub of Korea, China, and Japan. Very rare vagrant to western Alaska.
Yellow-throated_Bunting.Similar Looking Birds: Yellow-browed Bunting lacks yellow throat. No other bunting has black face with yellow throat.
Yellow-throated_Bunting.Best Ways to Identify: Bright yellow throat with black face and crest. Very rare Alaska vagrant from East Asia.

Yellow-throated_Vireo.Description: Stocky vireo with bright yellow spectacles, bright yellow throat and breast, two white wing bars, and gray rump.
Yellow-throated_Vireo.Behavior: Sings slow deliberate burry phrases; gleans caterpillars from canopy foliage; builds neat lichen-covered nest.
Yellow-throated_Vireo.Habitat: Mature deciduous forests and forest edges of eastern North America; riparian trees favored.
Yellow-throated_Vireo.Similar Looking Birds: Yellow-throated Warbler has black and white face and different body shape; Pine Warbler lacks yellow spectacles.
Yellow-throated_Vireo.Best Ways to Identify: Bright yellow spectacles; yellow throat and breast; gray back; two bold white wing bars; slow deliberate song.

Yellow-throated_Warbler.Description: Gray-backed warbler with yellow throat, white supercilium, black face mask, and bold black streaked white breast.
Yellow-throated_Warbler.Behavior: Creeps along bark of tree branches like a nuthatch; probes Spanish moss and bark crevices for insects.
Yellow-throated_Warbler.Habitat: Mature forests with Spanish moss, sycamore and pine forests in southeastern US; year-round in Florida.
Yellow-throated_Warbler.Similar Looking Birds: Grace's Warbler is western and has different face pattern; Yellow-throated Vireo has yellow spectacles.
Yellow-throated_Warbler.Best Ways to Identify: Yellow throat with bold black and white face pattern; white supercilium; creeps along large branches; southeastern US.

Yellow_Bittern.Description: Small bittern with yellow-buff body, dark brown wings, black cap. Similar in shape to Least Bittern. About 14 inches.
Yellow_Bittern.Behavior: Stalks prey in reeds like other bitterns. Asian species; very rare vagrant to Alaska and Hawaiian Islands.
Yellow_Bittern.Habitat: Reed marshes and wetlands of East Asia. Very rare vagrant to Alaska; rare in Hawaiian Islands.
Yellow_Bittern.Similar Looking Birds: Least Bittern similar shape but has rufous neck. Yellow Bittern paler buff overall.
Yellow_Bittern.Best Ways to Identify: Small bittern with yellow-buff plumage and dark brown wings. Asian vagrant to Alaska and Hawaii.

Yellow_Grosbeak.Description: Large grosbeak. Male brilliant yellow with black wings and white wing patches. Female streaked yellow. About 9.5 inches.
Yellow_Grosbeak.Behavior: Forages in trees for seeds and insects. Rare vagrant to Arizona and New Mexico from Mexico.
Yellow_Grosbeak.Habitat: Riparian woodland and thorn forest of western Mexico. Rare vagrant to Arizona and New Mexico.
Yellow_Grosbeak.Similar Looking Birds: Evening Grosbeak smaller with different wing pattern. American Goldfinch much smaller. Brilliant yellow with black wings.
Yellow_Grosbeak.Best Ways to Identify: Brilliant yellow with black wings and white patches. Massive grosbeak bill. Rare Arizona vagrant from Mexico.

Yellow_Rail.Description: Very small secretive rail with buffy-yellow streaked plumage, short stubby bill, and white wing patches in flight.
Yellow_Rail.Behavior: Extremely secretive; rarely flushes; white wing patches visible when flushed; clicks like stones knocked together.
Yellow_Rail.Habitat: Wet sedge meadows, shallow marshes, and grassy fields; very difficult to observe; breeds in northern prairies.
Yellow_Rail.Similar Looking Birds: Sora is larger with gray breast and yellow bill; LeConte's Sparrow has similar habitat but is a sparrow.
Yellow_Rail.Best Ways to Identify: White secondaries visible when flushed; buffy yellow streaked plumage; tiny size; ticking call at night in marshes.

Yellow_Warbler.Description: Bright yellow warbler; male has reddish streaks on breast; females paler; yellow spots in tail; beady black eye.
Yellow_Warbler.Behavior: Sings sweet-sweet-I'm-so-sweet; buries Cowbird eggs under new nest layers; common in willows near water.
Yellow_Warbler.Habitat: Willow and alder thickets, shrubby streamside habitats, and gardens throughout North America.
Yellow_Warbler.Similar Looking Birds: Wilson's Warbler has black cap; Orange-crowned Warbler is olive-dull; Prothonotary Warbler has gray wings.
Yellow_Warbler.Best Ways to Identify: All yellow with reddish breast streaks in male; yellow tail spots; black eye stands out; willow thicket habitat.

Yucatan_Vireo.Description: Large plain vireo, brown-gray above, buffy-white below with buffy flanks. Large bill, pale eye. About 6.5 inches.
Yucatan_Vireo.Behavior: Forages deliberately through dense scrub and forest. Rare vagrant to Texas coast. Song is a slow deliberate repetition.
Yucatan_Vireo.Habitat: Scrub forests and mangroves of Yucatan Peninsula. Very rare vagrant to Texas Gulf Coast.
Yucatan_Vireo.Similar Looking Birds: Black-whiskered Vireo similar but has black whisker mark. Red-eyed Vireo smaller with different eye color.
Yucatan_Vireo.Best Ways to Identify: Large vireo with brownish-gray tones and pale eye. Buffy flanks. Very rare Texas vagrant from Yucatan.

Zebra_Dove.Description: Small slender dove with brown upperparts, pale pinkish-buff underparts finely barred with black giving zebra pattern. Long tail. About 9 inches.
Zebra_Dove.Behavior: Forages on ground for seeds in pairs or small groups. Tame and approachable. Introduced to Hawaii from Southeast Asia; very common there.
Zebra_Dove.Habitat: Open areas, gardens, roadsides, and parks. Very common on all Hawaiian Islands. Native to Southeast Asian grasslands and cultivated areas.
Zebra_Dove.Similar Looking Birds: Common Ground Dove similar small size. Zebra Dove has longer tail and barred pattern.
Zebra_Dove.Best Ways to Identify: Fine black barring on underparts giving zebra pattern. Small size and very long tail. Tame and common in Hawaiian urban areas.

Zenaida_Dove.Description: A medium-sized dove with warm brown plumage, iridescent neck patch, white trailing edge on wings, and a rounded tail with white tips.
Zenaida_Dove.Behavior: Walks on the ground to forage for seeds. Often tame around humans. Produces a soft, mournful cooing call similar to the Mourning Dove.
Zenaida_Dove.Habitat: Found in open woodlands, scrub, coastal areas, and gardens across the Caribbean islands and parts of the Yucatan Peninsula.
Zenaida_Dove.Similar Looking Birds: Closely resembles the Mourning Dove but has a shorter, rounded tail and white wing patches visible in flight. Stockier build overall.
Zenaida_Dove.Best Ways to Identify: Look for the white trailing edge on the secondary wing feathers and the short rounded tail with white tips — key differences from Mourning Dove.

Zinos_Petrel.Description: Medium gadfly petrel, gray-brown above, white underparts, gray breast band. Critically endangered. About 13 inches.
Zinos_Petrel.Behavior: Critically endangered; breeds only on Madeira. Very rare in North Atlantic; extremely unlikely vagrant to North America.
Zinos_Petrel.Habitat: North Atlantic Ocean. Extremely rare vagrant. Breeds only on central Madeira mountains; critically endangered.
Zinos_Petrel.Similar Looking Birds: Fea's/Desertas Petrel very similar but larger. Zino's smaller with smaller bill.
Zinos_Petrel.Best Ways to Identify: Smaller than Fea's/Desertas Petrel. Critically endangered species breeding only on Madeira. Virtually impossible vagrant.

Zone-tailed_Hawk.Description: Medium hawk resembling Turkey Vulture; black body with banded tail; two-toned wings held in dihedral; yellow cere.
Zone-tailed_Hawk.Behavior: Mimics Turkey Vulture in flight to approach prey undetected; preys on lizards and birds; vocal in canyons.
Zone-tailed_Hawk.Habitat: Desert canyons, mountain slopes, and riparian areas of southwestern US and Mexico.
Zone-tailed_Hawk.Similar Looking Birds: Turkey Vulture has naked red head and different proportions; Common Black Hawk is stouter with different tail bands.
Zone-tailed_Hawk.Best Ways to Identify: Black hawk with tail bands; holds wings in V-dihedral like Turkey Vulture; yellow cere; canyon habitat southwest.
